540078|2026-06.headline: Mitsu Chem Plast Q1 FY27 net profit rose 566% YoY to INR 873.83 lakhs on a 16.29% EBITDA margin, with total income up 11.62%.
540078|2026-06.overview: Total income reached INR 9,532.78 lakhs (+11.62% YoY) and EBITDA INR 1,549.48 lakhs (+209.50% YoY), with margin expanding to 16.29% from 5.87%. Net profit of INR 873.83 lakhs was up sequentially from INR 771.73 lakhs in Q4 FY26. Management attributed the gain to operating efficiency and product mix, and announced a proposed 3,550 MTPA capacity addition on top of 32,450 MTPA. Management said it now prioritises bottom line over top line, and that the INR 1,000 crore revenue target by FY28 remains in place.

segments.name: Packaging (containers, paint containers, jerry cans, caps and closures)
segments.commentary: Management says packaging is about 80% of business and will remain the largest contributor; the 80:20 split with furniture/other parts is expected to hold to INR 1,000 crores. Containers described as in strong demand.

segments.name: Healthcare furniture (Furnastra brand) and other parts
segments.commentary: Accounts for about 19.8% of the business per management, including furniture parts and other parts. Management expects faster growth here than in containers, but gave no target mix.

guidance_outlook: Management expects sequential revenue growth of roughly the same rate each quarter, 'almost same', while focusing more on bottom line.
Sustainable EBITDA margin described as 10-13% on average; management said double-digit EBITDA will remain, with quarterly variation from product mix.
INR 1,000 crore annual revenue target by FY28 reiterated; management says it is in line with the capacity expansion.
IBC (intermediate bulk container) project expected to start commercial production around Q3 FY27; investment amount not yet disclosed.
Proposed 3,550 MTPA capacity addition: management stated capex of approximately INR 2 crore and that the capacity is already online. Revenue contribution to be announced soon.
Management expects utilisation to stay around 64-65%, or about 70% as a healthier level.
capex_capacity: Current installed capacity above 32,450 MTPA across four facilities, with 53 blow moulding and 22 injection moulding machines.
Proposed addition of 3,550 MTPA, to be used across all three verticals (containers, furniture parts and others).

Capex for the 3,550 MTPA addition stated as approximately INR 2 crore (the transcript figure, which looks low for this capacity and should be verified); funding is a mix of internal accruals and debt. Management said this depends on machinery source.
Lead time from machinery order to commercial operation is about 6-9 months, per management.
Utilisation was 60-64% through FY26; seasonal peaks reach about 85%.
demand_pricing: Management says demand is strong across all verticals, with containers in particular high demand.

Raw material prices rising on geopolitical and crude-linked pressures; management says suppliers have raised prices and customers have accepted pass-through, with local sourcing used since imports were stopped years ago.
Raw material pass-through to customers is generally on a one-month lag; specialised cases are negotiated individually.
Pricing is a cost-plus markup on raw material; management said other value-add and efficiency gains drive the margin, not the pass-through alone.

Company is rationalising SKUs (around 500) by dropping low-margin products; added more than 30 customers in Q1 and more than 150 in the last year (the two figures were stated inconsistently on the call; the 150 figure is probably cumulative for the year).

qa_highlights.question: What drove the margin expansion to about 16%, and is it sustainable given raw material pressure?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited innovation, manufacturing efficiency and product mix, and said raw material increases are passed to customers. It later said sustainable margins are 10-13%, with some quarters higher.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex for the 3,500 MTPA expansion and how will it be funded?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said approximately INR 2 crore, funded by a mix of internal accruals and debt, and that the capacity is already online.

qa_highlights.question: What revenue growth is expected in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects roughly the same sequential growth each quarter, while focusing more on profit than revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Does a 16% EBITDA margin represent a new normal, and how does the pass-through work?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 10-12% is the normal range and double-digit margins will remain, with pass-through about one month in arrears.

qa_highlights.question: Why add capacity when utilisation is only 64%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said machinery lead time plus 6-9 months of set-up requires planning ahead; utilisation is seasonal, reaching about 85% at peak.

qa_highlights.question: Which businesses will drive the INR 1,000 crore target, and what is the IBC project?
qa_highlights.answer: Packaging remains about 80% and the mix is expected to stay around 80:20. IBC commercial production is expected around Q3, on new machinery with the cost not yet disclosed.

risks_watch: Raw material cost inflation linked to geopolitical and crude-price moves; pass-through is one month in arrears, which can squeeze margins during rapid price rises.
Margin sustainability: Q1's 16.29% is well above the 10-12% range management described as normal, and EBITDA has been volatile quarter to quarter.
The FY28 INR 1,000 crore target needs a sharp step-up. Quarterly revenue is about INR 95 crore, so the run rate needs to reach roughly INR 120-130 crore per quarter or more.
Capex disclosure is thin: the INR 2 crore figure for 3,550 MTPA looks low, and the IBC project cost and the revenue from new capacity are both still undisclosed.
Low export share (about 2%) and an unquantified international healthcare contract; ramp-up timing unclear.
Governance: the warrant allottee (Rikhav Securities) was questioned; management said it was a small investor with no existing relationship, and the warrant proceeds are for working capital.
Utilisation of 64% against a 3,550 MTPA addition; management expects utilisation to remain about 64-65%.

Management repeatedly pointed to the bottom line over top-line growth. Audio problems on the call also made several questions hard to hear.

540078|2026-09.headline: Mitsu Chem Plast Q2 FY27 PAT rose 224% YoY to Rs 610.47 lakhs on 12.41% EBITDA margin; revenue up only 3.67%.
540078|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue from operations was Rs 9,580.87 lakhs, up 3.67% YoY, while EBITDA rose to Rs 1,188.55 lakhs at a 12.41% margin and PAT reached Rs 610.47 lakhs (6.37% margin). H1 FY27 revenue was Rs 19,095.40 lakhs (+7.46% YoY) with EBITDA of Rs 2,738.03 lakhs (14.34% margin) and PAT of Rs 1,484.30 lakhs (7.77% margin). Management said the strategy is margin-first, with a shift toward higher-margin niche products, and pointed to IBC entry and a Rs 1,000 crore revenue ambition by FY28 without giving a build-up. Management gave no firm IBC revenue, capex or margin figures, and EBITDA margin was about 3.5-4 points lower QoQ.

segments.name: Industrial packaging
segments.commentary: Management put it at about 81.88% of revenue for the period and called it the core business; analysts said it was broadly flat, and management described a very slight dip with focus shifting to higher-margin items.

segments.name: Hospital furniture parts (Furnastra brand, launched 2025)
segments.commentary: About 16.27% of revenue. Management said niche items are now above 16% of mix, up from 13-15%, and about 30% YoY growth; exports are being developed in 18 registered countries.

segments.name: Infrastructure furniture and others
segments.commentary: About 1.86% of revenue. Management called the sales seasonal and said the decline was not a concern.

guidance_outlook: Management targets Rs 1,000 crore annual revenue by FY28. It gave no build-up and said details would be announced shortly; the current run-rate is about Rs 400 crore.
Management said revenue at optimal utilisation from existing capacity is about Rs 425 crore, and said practical utilisation is 85-90%.
The 1,000-litre IBC facility in Khalapur is expected to be operational in Q3 FY27, with most of the impact in Q4. Management said IBC margins will be higher than the core, without quantifying.
Management expects Q3 and Q4 demand to be strong and says the EBITDA margin is sustainable, with improvement targeted but not quantified.
Management said exports should begin commercially this year, after trials and approvals.
capex_capacity: Four facilities with 58 blow moulding machines and 22 injection moulding machines; capacity above 36,000 MTPA.
Average capacity utilisation about 64% in FY26 (one answer said 63%), and about 50%+ on average per another answer; the figures given were inconsistent.
Fully automated Khalapur facility for 1,000-litre IBCs, expected operational in Q3 FY27. Capital turnover about 15x vs 8-10x for other products. Capex amount and IBC capacity were not disclosed.
Management said no further capex beyond the IBC project is planned for now.
demand_pricing: Management said overall demand is very good, with one or two industries down and the rest strong.
Exports go to USA, Canada and Europe; exports were about 1.5% of revenue in H1 FY27 per management.
Management said realisations should rise under a cost-plus model, but volume growth was not quantified. Management said the focus is on profitability over volume.
Polymers are not hedged; about 90-95% of raw material is bought domestically. Reported margins include no inventory gains.
Management said West Asia tensions have not affected export projects or orders so far.

qa_highlights.question: How does the Rs 1,000 crore FY28 target square with a current run-rate of about Rs 400 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not give a build-up, saying more plans would be announced soon. It said the target is a basket of plans, not mainly IBC, and that it had not said the capacity was enough without capex.

qa_highlights.question: Why did EBITDA margin fall QoQ by about 3.5-4%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margins are sustainable, that double-digit EBITDA is good in the current market, and that it is working to improve further. It did not give a number for the quarter-on-quarter dip.

qa_highlights.question: What is the volume growth, given flat-to-weak revenue growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said volumes were stable to slightly up and that low-margin portfolio items were rationalised in favour of higher-margin products, without giving volume figures.

qa_highlights.question: Is IBC on track, and what revenue and margin will it add?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said IBC will start in Q3 (through December), margins will be higher than the core, and it would give no revenue or market-size numbers until production begins.

qa_highlights.question: What are H1 vs H2 revenue split and capacity utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said H1 is generally about 40% and H2 about 60% of annual revenue. FY26 utilisation was about 63-64%, and practical maximum is 85-90%, which would mean about Rs 400-420 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company outsourcing any production?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said some production is outsourced depending on market conditions, but the share is not considerable and no percentage was given.

risks_watch: FY28 Rs 1,000 crore target looks far from the current run-rate of about Rs 400 crore, and no build-up was given.
IBC start (Q3 FY27), revenue, capex and margins are still undisclosed, and the facility had not started by the call date.
Revenue growth of only 3.67% YoY in Q2 against a large EBITDA gain; the margin dipped QoQ.
Cash balance of Rs 6.07 lakhs against borrowings of Rs 9,648.44 lakhs, with D/E at 0.76x; higher depreciation and interest from new capex could weigh on PAT.
Export commercial revenue is still small (about 1.5% of H1 revenue); exports to Poland and new approvals are yet to show in numbers.
Utilisation figures given on the call were inconsistent (about 50%+, 63%, 64%).

540097|2026-09.headline: GAMCO H1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 79% to INR254 crore and net profit reached INR38.5 crore, with Q2 PAT of INR6 crore.
540097|2026-09.overview: Consolidated H1 FY27 revenue from operations grew 79% to INR254 crore, already about 84% of FY26 full-year revenue, with EBITDA of INR52.9 crore and net profit of INR38.5 crore versus INR6.5 crore in H1 FY26. Q2 revenue rose 61.7% YoY to INR140.6 crore, but Q2 EBITDA of INR12 crore (9% margin) and PAT of INR6 crore were well below Q1, which management attributed to a one-off strong Q1. Net worth rose 24% in six months to INR206.6 crore and debt-to-equity improved to about 1.6x from 1.7x. Management framed the company as a four-vertical group (equity investments, real estate, logistics, hospitality) shifting from marketing gains toward asset-backed income, with most asset revenues expected from FY28 onward.

segments.name: Equity investments / treasury
segments.commentary: Quoted equity investment of about INR230 crore, including stakes in Swiggy, TrucksUp and Drivers4Me. Management said these listed holdings are the most liquid source of funding for expansion.

segments.name: Real estate (Kolkata, OneWorld)
segments.commentary: 9.7% stake in OneWorld, a 212-acre Lucknow township, invested at about INR19.4 crore and revalued at INR153 crore (unrealised gain about INR134 crore). Kolkata plans 13.5 lakh sq ft of residential launches over 1-2 years; Alipore (Uma Properties) expected to yield about INR250 crore revenue, and Jessore Road JV (Elika Realestate, 45% stake) about INR1,100 crore over 5 years.

segments.name: Warehousing / logistics
segments.commentary: Dankuni, Delhi Road land with 40 lakh sq ft development potential and about INR600 crore capex, targeting 8-10% rental yields. Calcutta 100-125 acre project to deliver 25-30 lakh sq ft; revenue expected from calendar 2028. Visco Advisory warehousing asset sold for INR15.8 crore.

segments.name: Hospitality
segments.commentary: Acquired 33.33% of Blissara Resorts (Port Blair) with INR69 crore post-money valuation; planning a 140-key upper upscale hotel on 11 acres with coastal clearance in place. Construction to start in about a month; revenue expected from about 2030 with 5.5-7 year payback including debt and equity.

guidance_outlook: Blissara hotel: construction starting imminently, operations targeted in 2-2.5 years, revenue hitting top line by about 2030.
Warehousing (Calcutta): revenue expected from calendar 2028, within 1-1.5 years of securing land and approvals; leases under negotiation.
Uma Properties (Alipore residential): revenue expected from about March/April 2028, with a possible one-quarter delay.
Management expects constant revenue from most investments after the March 2028 quarter.

Management said the group will keep about 25% of its portfolio in liquid treasury such as equity markets, and expects construction funding and internal accruals to cover much of the next 3 years of spend.

Hotels targeted to be valued at INR500-600 crore each, with at least INR100 crore revenue per property; operator fee structure of about 2% base fee plus GOP-linked incentive, total under about 8-8.5% of revenue.
capex_capacity: Dankuni logistics land: 40 lakh sq ft development potential, capex about INR600 crore.
Calcutta: 13.5 lakh sq ft residential launches over 1-2 years; warehousing 100-125 acres giving 25-30 lakh sq ft immediate supply; construction started on ground.
Port Blair hotel: 140 keys on 11 acres; pipeline in Lucknow, Himachal and Ayodhya under evaluation.
Analyst estimate of INR900-1,500 crore funding need over 3-5 years was not disputed by management; funding to come from market borrowing, internal accruals, treasury and asset sales.
Nanak Logistics (63-acre park, Amazon anchor leasing 6.25 lakh sq ft on 20 acres) cited as prior group track record.
demand_pricing: Management cited zero Grade A warehouse supply in Calcutta and limited hotel supply in Port Blair, Lucknow, Himachal and Ayodhya; no pricing or occupancy data were given.
Warehouse targets: 8-10% rental yields, versus management's view that Tier 1 Grade A warehouses offer about 7-9% returns.
Hotel valuation benchmark cited at 10-16x EBITDA; 40-45% GOP assumed for the hotel.
Management said the Port Blair hotel faces no competition for about 3 years after opening.

qa_highlights.question: How will the company expand into factoring, lease financing and security-backed lending, and how does this fit with real estate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it would be selective and pursue structured niche deals, not plain-vanilla lending, citing the Shalimar Lake City (OneWorld) revaluation and the Visco Advisory exit as examples.

qa_highlights.question: Which vertical will create the most value over 3-4 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is most excited about hospitality, then warehousing, targeting INR100 crore revenue and INR500-600 crore valuation per hotel.

qa_highlights.question: What is the timeline for hospitality and warehousing revenue, and what are the execution risks?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Blissara revenue starts around 2030 after construction; warehousing revenue from calendar 2028; Alipore residential from about March/April 2028. Monsoon delays were the main constraint, now considered over.

qa_highlights.question: How does revenue recognition work with the hotel operator, and what is the payback?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the operator takes a 1.5-2.5% base fee on gross revenue plus a share of gross operating profit, with total fees under about 8-8.5%. Payback is about 5.5-7 years including debt and equity; INR69 crore post-money valuation for Blissara.

qa_highlights.question: How will the INR900-1,500 crore funding requirement be met?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will use the listed equity treasury (keeping about 25% liquid), market borrowing for construction, internal accruals, and asset liquidation as needed. Management did not confirm the analyst's INR400 crore liquidation estimate.

qa_highlights.question: Who owns the other 55% of the Jessore Road project?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said three or four other West Bengal real estate developers hold the remaining 55%, chosen for execution capability.

qa_highlights.question: Why enter hospitality as landowner/investor rather than operator, and how much control does GAMCO have?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it lacks operating experience and prefers global operators, and that development-stage entry captures higher returns (11-12% on Tier 2 land versus 7-9% for Tier 1 warehouses). It said it would provide guidance and strategic input.

risks_watch: Q2 earnings fell sharply from Q1 (EBITDA INR12 crore vs INR41 crore; PAT INR6 crore vs INR32 crore), indicating lumpy income from investment gains.
Funding gap: analyst estimate of INR900-1,500 crore over 3-5 years versus debt of INR327 crore and debt-to-equity of 1.6x; reliance on market borrowing and asset sales.
Timelines are long: hotel revenue around 2030, warehousing from 2028, Alipore from 2028, with possible further slippage.
Heavy reliance on valuation gains (OneWorld INR134 crore unrealised gain) and on the listed equity book, which is market-sensitive.
Limited operating disclosure on the hotel and warehousing revenue models; stated targets are not yet backed by signed leases or contracts. Management said warehousing leases are being negotiated.

540115|2026-03.headline: LTTS Q4 FY26 revenue rose 0.3% YoY to $305.9 Mn and EBIT margin reached 15.2%, with mid-16% margin targeted by Q4 FY27 or earlier.
540115|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 continuing-operations revenue was $305.9 Mn, up 0.3% YoY and down 1.7% QoQ, as the company exited low-margin work and divested SWC (Smart World). EBIT margin rose 40 bps QoQ to 15.2%, the second straight quarter of expansion, with gross margin up 150 bps QoQ. Management said the restructuring is complete, with about $19 Mn annualised revenue exited in Q4 and no further restructuring costs expected. It advanced the margin aspiration to mid-16% by Q4 FY27 or earlier and set a 5-year Lakshya 31 plan of 13%-15% USD CAGR and 16%-17% EBIT margin, with no annual guidance given.

segments.commentary: Q4 EBIT margin 16.1%, up 130 bps QoQ; revenue almost flat QoQ. Over 40% of Q4 large deal wins were in Mobility; management expects growth from Q1 FY27.

segments.commentary: Contributed 36% of FY26 revenue; grew 11% YoY in Q4 and sequentially. EBIT margin 28.7%, steady QoQ. Over 50% of Q4 large deal wins; first $50 Mn+ account reported.

segments.name: Tech (incl. Intelliswift)
segments.commentary: Revenue subdued after exits of non-strategic businesses; EBIT margin 12.6%, up 210 bps QoQ on Intelliswift margin gains and restructuring. FY26 Tech including Intelliswift grew 19.7%.

guidance_outlook: Aspiration to reach mid-16% EBIT margin on or before Q4 FY27; management said it may come earlier.
Lakshya 31 five-year plan: 13%-15% USD CAGR and 16%-17% EBIT margin; 12.4% past 5-year CAGR includes SWC, per Rajeev Gupta.
Combined DSO expected at 85-90 days going forward.
Effective tax rate guided at 26.5%-27%.

Headcount expected to add about 500 more billable staff across Q1-Q3 FY27 for forward deployment engineering skills and ramp-ups.
capex_capacity: Headcount rose 522 QoQ to 23,830 at year-end after fresher onboarding; attrition steady at 14.7%.
Offshore mix 53.5%, slightly up QoQ; management sees room for improvement in coming quarters.
T&M revenue mix 66.1%, up from Q3.
Management plans to invest heavily in talent, AI tools, and alliances for Engineering Intelligence (EI), physical AI, SDV and connectivity.
Patent filings exceeded 1,700 in FY26 (673 by LTTS, 1,033 co-authored with clients), of which 237 are in AI/GenAI.
demand_pricing: Large deal TCV in Q4 was $182 Mn; FY26 large deal wins were $855 Mn, up 40% YoY; average large deal TCV about $200 Mn over six quarters.
North America grew 12% in FY26; all other geographies grew positively.
Realised rupee about ₹93.43/USD in Q4, a 4.3% depreciation vs Q3.
Automotive: North America showing positive momentum with SDV investments; Europe deals being competed against European majors and Indian peers.
Exits of about $19 Mn annualised revenue (Middle East, Europe, Israel, UK, Telecom Infra low-margin work) completed in Q4; no revenue from these in Q4 and none expected to recur.
Middle East exposure in Plant Engineering is very small per management; no impact expected in the current or next quarter.
Less than 50% of revenue currently comes from the six Lakshya bets; management expects more than 70% in five years.

qa_highlights.question: Why was SWC divested, and does continuing-ops reporting exclude it for all FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: Telco Infra and Cyber were scaled internationally, but Smart Cities could not be taken global because of local-government work. Continuing-ops figures exclude SWC from all periods for like-for-like comparison; mostly India and some international SWC operations were sold. Restructuring is complete.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 16%-17% margin a five-year target or achievable sooner?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated mid-16% by Q4 FY27 or earlier as an aspiration; 16%-17% is the Lakshya FY31 band to be maintained over five years, not a reduction.

qa_highlights.question: When will the 13%-15% CAGR show up, and when do $100 Mn+ and several-hundred-million accounts emerge?
qa_highlights.answer: No annual guidance. A $50 Mn+ trailing-12-month account was delivered in Q4, the first in a long time. Build-out to $100 Mn accounts is mostly organic and will take time; Alind Saxena now focuses on large deals and growth markets.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 13%-15% CAGR in USD and does the 12.4% historical figure include SWC?
qa_highlights.answer: The 13%-15% is USD-based, and the 12.4% five-year CAGR includes SWC. Reported-currency targets may be added over time.

qa_highlights.question: How big are the six bets and what investment is planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Less than 50% of revenue today comes from the six bets; more than 70% expected in five years. Management will hold an Investor Day later in the year with detail. Investment focuses on EI, SDV, connectivity, and physical AI.

qa_highlights.question: Will there be more restructuring, and what is the reason for the $19 Mn exit?
qa_highlights.answer: Rajeev Gupta said the Q4 exceptional charge covers the $19 Mn annualised exit in Europe, Israel and the UK, with no further restructuring costs expected.

qa_highlights.question: Could a 15% margin come as early as H2 FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it aims for mid-16% by Q4 FY27 or earlier and did not commit to H2 FY26; margins have improved from the 13.3%-13.6% discussed 2-3 years ago.

qa_highlights.question: How is AI affecting client conversations and pricing?
qa_highlights.answer: Clients are asking for productivity pass-through and AI spend is rising. About 60% of staff are trained on AI tools, with the rest due within six months. Management believes LTTS is 6-8 months ahead of competitors.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any M&A planned and would margins take a hit?
qa_highlights.answer: Only tuck-in acquisitions; no large acquisition is planned. Intelliswift's acquisition has performed well, and margins will be kept within the 16%-17% band.

540115|2026-06.headline: LTTS Q1 FY27 revenue rose 1.5% QoQ in constant currency to $309.9 Mn, with EBIT margin up 50 bps QoQ to 15.7%.
540115|2026-06.overview: LTTS grew revenue 1.5% QoQ and 1.9% YoY in constant currency, to $309.9 Mn (Rs 2,940 crore, +2.9% QoQ, +11.5% YoY in rupee terms). EBIT margin expanded to 15.7%, up 50 bps QoQ and 200 bps YoY, and free cash flow was 153% of net income. Sustainability grew 4.3% QoQ and 11.3% YoY, while Tech declined on a medical program stop and large deals slipping into early Q2. Management reiterated sequential growth in revenue and margins for each quarter and a mid-16% EBIT margin on or before Q4 FY27, but declined to give annual guidance.

financial_highlights.change: vs reported FY26 EPS Rs 115.89, about +15%
lower QoQ, mainly hedge losses partly offset by rupee benefit

segments.name: Mobility
segments.commentary: Grew 2.3% QoQ, led by Aerospace & Rail and Trucks & Off-Highway; segment margin 15.6%, down slightly on onsite ramp-up of new programs. Management expects revenue and margin to improve sequentially as these programs mature. Europe remains challenging.

segments.name: Sustainability
segments.commentary: Grew 4.3% QoQ and 11.3% YoY; the most profitable segment with margin of 29.1%, up 40 bps QoQ. Management confirmed double-digit growth for FY27, citing Plant Engineering (Upstream O&G, LNG, Chemicals) and Industrial Products (Data Centers, Electrical Equipment).

segments.name: Tech
segments.commentary: Declined QoQ on a medical program that ended and a new one that was delayed; segment margin 11.5%. Tech is now 30.6% of revenue vs 34.4% a year ago. Management expects a return to growth from Q2, with a significant telecom deal expected to close in early Q2.

guidance_outlook: Sequential improvement in revenue and EBIT margin expected in every quarter of FY27, reconfirmed by the CEO.
Mid-16% EBIT margin targeted on or before Q4 FY27; long-term aspiration of 16-17% EBIT margin.
5-year aspiration of 13-15% revenue CAGR; management declined to give an annual FY27 revenue outlook.
Combined DSO to stay in the 80-85 day range; FCF to be 90-95% of net income for the year (management said Q1 cash conversion of 153% was exceptional).
ETR guided to 26.2% to 26.7%; other income to stay at Q1 levels for the next few quarters due to hedge losses.
Smart World (Tech) disinvestment expected to close in Q2 FY27.
capex_capacity: Opened Europe's first Engineering Intelligence Center in Munich during Q1.
Launched Ainfonix, an Engineering Intelligence platform for process industry clients.
Headcount broadly flat at 23,845; management said it could have grown Sustainability faster with more talent, and it continues to hire there.
Created a team of 100 forward-deployed engineers and a flexible ramp-up model to start work as soon as deals close.
AI patents at 244; total patent count 1,757.
demand_pricing: Large deal TCV of nearly $100 Mn in Q1; some deals expected to close in Q1 slipped into early Q2. Management said the slippage is not broad-based and is client-specific.
Management said US auto demand is improving and the worst is behind it; Europe OEMs and Tier-1s are under pressure from the Asia/China supply shakeout.
Japan OEMs are looking to use India for engineering and localisation.
Pricing: management said no client has asked for rate cuts recently, and AI-led productivity is partly being passed on to clients to win work in a competitive market.
Management claims a 6-9 month lead over competitors in Engineering Intelligence.
Sustainability pipeline is strong; no pullback seen from clients despite crude price volatility, though Middle East revenue was small and some execution was delayed.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Tech decline QoQ, and what differentiates Mobility in a weak auto market?
qa_highlights.answer: Tech fell due to a medical program ending and a new one not starting on schedule; management expects Mobility and Tech to grow in FY27. Mobility differentiation was cited as EV/hybrid lab investments, SDV with AI, and diversification across auto, T&OH, Aero and Rail.

qa_highlights.question: Will AI-led large deal sizes and vendor consolidation appear in ER&D?
qa_highlights.answer: Alind Saxena said most large deals are now fixed-price or outcome-based and must include process transformation, with AI embedded. Management cited consulting, implementation and owner's-engineer positioning, including a Claude partnership.

qa_highlights.question: Will FCF to net income stay at 153%?
qa_highlights.answer: Rajeev Gupta said Q1 was a stellar working-capital quarter; the full-year FCF conversion expected is 90-95% of net income.

qa_highlights.question: Does AI-led productivity hit pricing, and how is it passed on?
qa_highlights.answer: Amit Chadha said clients have not asked for rate cuts; productivity gains are partly shared with clients to win bids, and LTTS aims to keep gaining share.

qa_highlights.question: Will Q2 growth be better than Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give a full-year view but committed to growth in Q2, with the timing of the telecom deal and medical deals as key drivers.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Tech share of revenue structural, and what is the outlook for other income?
qa_highlights.answer: Rajeev Gupta said Tech will not return to its 34% share soon; growth will come more from Sustainability and Mobility. Other income is lower mainly on hedge losses, and the same range is expected for the next few quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Is crude volatility a risk to Sustainability demand, and what is the Mobility split?
qa_highlights.answer: Amit Chadha said there was no pullback from Plant Engineering clients and reconfirmed double-digit Sustainability growth for FY27. Mobility is no longer split into sub-segments, and the split will not be provided.

qa_highlights.question: Is the deal slippage broad-based, and what is the revenue impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Alind Saxena said the slippage is not broad-based, with two deals delayed; ramp-ups are tied to the win dates. Management said the pipeline is broad across sectors.

qa_highlights.question: How have client conversations changed amid geopolitical uncertainty?
qa_highlights.answer: Amit Chadha said client discussions are mostly focused on market share and AI, with some insulation from the Middle East conflict. Clients are asking whether AI will be net positive for their business, and cost neutrality is a driver.

Europe auto (OEM and Tier-1) demand remains weak, and management said recovery will take time.

540115|2026-09.headline: LTTS Q2 FY27 revenue rose 2.7% QoQ in constant currency to $317.1M, with EBIT margin at 16.3%, ahead of its mid-16% aspiration.
540115|2026-09.overview: Revenue reached $317.1M (up 2.7% QoQ and 4.8% YoY in constant currency, continuing operations), and INR 3,040 crore (up 3.4% QoQ, 12.1% YoY). EBIT margin widened 60 bps QoQ to 16.3%, and management said the mid-16% aspiration was reached a couple of quarters early. Large deal TCV was $203M with over 50% AI-led, and management said the USD100M shortfall from last quarter's target would be recovered over Q3 and Q4. Reported net income of INR 548 crore included a one-time INR 165 crore gain from the SWC divestment, which is now complete.

financial_highlights.change: +53.7% QoQ; +66.8% YoY; includes INR 165 crore one-time SWC gain
vs 77 days in Q1; guided range 80 to 85 days
vs INR 3,394 crore at end Q1

segments.name: Mobility
segments.commentary: Revenue up 2.3% QoQ, with growth from Auto North America, Aero and Rail, and Trucks and Off-highway. Auto Europe remained muted; management expects it to recover next year. Auto is about 50% of Mobility revenue. Margin 16.9%.

segments.name: Sustainability
segments.commentary: Up 13.4% YoY and 4.9% QoQ; now about 30% of revenue per the CFO (38% per the later AI-revenue answer, which conflicts). Nearly half of Q2 large deal wins were here. Margin 29.5%. Management says it is on track for another double-digit growth year.

segments.name: Tech
segments.commentary: Described as stable. Tech Infra and Semcon were strong, Media steady. A global telecom equipment AI program began ramping this quarter. Margin 12%, up 50 bps QoQ. Management expects Tech to be muted in Q3, with Medtech recovery in Q4.

segments.name: Engineering Intelligence (EI)
segments.commentary: Annualized EI-led revenue of $120M in Q2, which management said is about 9.5% of revenue. Headcount was 24,035 and more than 16,000 engineers were upskilled in AI. Over 50% of Q2 large deal wins were AI-led.

guidance_outlook: H2 FY27 revenue expected to be better than H1, both QoQ and YoY, per management.
Near-term EBIT margin expected around mid-16% levels; aspiration to maintain it.
Long-term aspiration: 13% to 15% revenue CAGR with 16% to 17% EBIT margin over 3 to 5 years.
Wage hike effective Q3, expected impact of 50 to 80 bps on margin; margin guidance stated as inclusive of this.

Investment in Munich and an EI center to target European auto work.

Offshore mix 55.9%; fixed-price mix 35.6%, rising toward higher-value and outcome-based engagements.
Average deal tenures have lengthened slightly. Management cited roughly 5 to 7 years for a $100M deal, 4 to 5 years for $50M, about 3 years for $25M.
Management says it charges a premium for AI-led work but declined to quantify AI-led margins by service line.
Rupee realized at 95.9 per dollar in Q2, depreciating 1.09% QoQ.
Attrition range-bound at 14.7%.
Europe auto remains weak; management said there is little Middle East exposure in oil and gas.

qa_highlights.question: How has Sustainability volatility come down, and how much revenue is long-term?
qa_highlights.answer: Management split Sustainability into four areas (Oil and Gas/Chemicals, FMCG, Energy Automation, Industrial Machinery and Building Tech), built digital twin and AI solutions, and said large deals from last year are now converting to revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Middle East situation affecting oil and gas or overall business?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Middle East business is very small and it is not seeing significant impact; work is focused on the US and Europe.

qa_highlights.question: Will European auto recover next year, and is it an industry-wide turnaround?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects Europe auto to stabilize in the next 6 to 9 months and grow again in 9 to 12 months, as European OEMs rebase and India-based providers replace local vendors. Auto Europe is about 50% of the auto portion of Mobility, and the company does not quantify it.

qa_highlights.question: Is the DSO of 78 days comfortable, or is there room to improve it?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said the company is comfortable at 78 days, well below the 80 to 85 day guided range, and expects to operate around this level.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the SWC divestment affect the reported numbers, and what is the run rate from Q3?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said the INR 165 crore was a one-time gain. From Q3 only continuing operations will be reported, with the SWC operating line of about $36M excluded.

qa_highlights.question: Why are clients converting deals to revenue now, and what changed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to AI capex across chips, software, industrials, telecom and infrastructure, clients focusing on growth rather than cost cuts, and LTTS being 9 to 12 months ahead of peers on AI, which it says is gaining share.

qa_highlights.question: What are sustainable margins, and what is the Q4 exit margin?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said near-term margins should be taken at around mid-16% EBIT, with levers from mix, AI and productivity, net of the wage hike. Management did not give a Q4 exit margin.

qa_highlights.question: What is the wage hike impact, and what does H2 growth mean?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said the wage hike in Q3 would have a 50 to 80 bps margin impact. Management said H2 will be better than H1 both QoQ and YoY, without a quarterly number.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the $120M annualized EI revenue was recognized in Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the $120M is annualized, so about $30M per quarter. Most AI deal wins have not yet gone into operation, and the company will report AI-led revenue quarterly.

qa_highlights.question: How is AI-led revenue defined, and what is its profitability?
qa_highlights.answer: AI revenue counts deliverables where a significant part is created using the AI stack. Management declined to quantify AI-led profitability, but said AI is a margin lever.

540133|2026-03.headline: ICICI Pru Life FY26 VNB rose 10.9% to ₹26.29bn with margin up 190bp to 24.7%, but APE grew only 2.2% and RoEV fell to 11.9%.

Retail protection was the standout, up 32.3% for the year and 60.5% in Q4, offsetting weak agency, direct, linked and annuity lines. Profit after tax rose 34.6% to ₹16bn, helped by a ₹1.14bn gain on sale of ICICI Pension Fund Management Company; excluding it, PAT grew 25%. EV operating assumption changes (GST input-tax-credit loss, persistency) and a ₹2.64bn persistency variance (mainly the 100% premium back annuity) pulled RoEV down to 11.9%. Management said West Asia disruption hurt March new business across all lines except protection, and it deferred Ind-AS adoption by a year via forbearance.

qa_highlights.question: Why is agency growing slowly, and how will it be revived?

540133|2026-06.headline: ICICI Pru Life Q1 FY27: VNB up 24.9% YoY to ₹5.71 bn at 26.7% margin, driven by retail protection growth of 60.4%.
540133|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 VNB grew 24.9% YoY to ₹5.71 bn, with VNB margin at 26.7%, up 200 bps from FY26's 24.7%. PAT rose 27.8% YoY to ₹3.86 bn. Growth was led by protection: sum assured up 31.8% to ₹4.90 trn and protection APE up 45.7%, while savings APE rose only 5.8% and non-linked APE fell about 9.5% as fixed deposits attracted customers. Management repeatedly stated there is no margin target and no formal guidance, and that absolute VNB growth is the focus.

segments.commentary: Grew 37.8% YoY; MFI credit life recovered after a long slowdown, non-MFI momentum continued.

segments.name: Savings
segments.commentary: Savings APE ₹15.40 bn, up 5.8% YoY; savings share of mix fell to 72.1% from 78.1%. Linked APE up 6.4%; non-linked including annuity broadly flat at ₹4.94 bn; group funds up 42.2%.

segments.name: Agency
segments.commentary: APE up 2% YoY to ₹4.63 bn, improved from negative growth in prior quarters; channel shifting to higher sum assured and protection.

segments.name: Direct
segments.commentary: APE up 8.3% YoY to ₹2.86 bn; agency plus direct contributed 45.5% of retail APE.

segments.name: Bancassurance
segments.commentary: Grew 5.6% YoY, 27.4% of APE; management attributes this to partner-bank recalibration.

segments.name: Partnership distribution
segments.commentary: Grew 29.5% YoY, 14.6% of APE; management cites a near 20% five-year CAGR and no single partner above 5%.

segments.name: Group business
segments.commentary: Grew 38.8% YoY, 22.9% of APE.

Second-half retail protection growth is expected to taper from the 60%+ level, as the base steepens; management said it would be 'very unlikely' to stay above 60% in H2.
The input tax credit drag continues for one more quarter (Q2) and then enters the base from Q3.
MFI credit life is expected to add to growth in H2 on a favourable base.
Non-par is expected to pick up only when fixed-deposit alternatives become less attractive; no timeline given.
No en-masse protection repricing is planned; repricing will be targeted by cohort as business as usual.

AI/ML is embedded across the customer journey, covering demand generation, automated underwriting, renewals, service and claims investigation (slide 32 of the investor presentation).

Non-linked APE fell about 9.5% YoY, per a question from BNP Paribas; management attributed this to non-par weakness.
Annuity growth of about 33% YoY was led by regular-premium deferred annuity, not single premium; the par to non-par ratio in non-linked is about 2:1.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the VNB margin, and is the GST input tax credit drag still affecting it?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO Dhiren Salian said the margin was largely product mix; the non-availability of input tax credit continues for one more quarter (Q2) before entering the base from Q3. He did not quantify the drag.

qa_highlights.question: Why is non-par not selling, and what is the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Fixed-income alternatives, mainly fixed deposits with high sticker rates, are more attractive to customers. Non-par is not being avoided and is repriced as conditions allow, but the pickup depends on those alternatives easing.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said Standard Chartered has been a 10-year partner, that both sides value it, and that ICICI Bank is the largest single channel at about 15% of business with no other distributor above 5%.

qa_highlights.question: How does expense management look, and what is the ITC drag in rupees?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said cost-to-premium is up on the input tax credit loss, partly offset by productivity and AI/ML gains. It did not quantify the ITC impact and said the schedules would show the GST component. It said EOM is well within the cap, without disclosing the figure.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any VNB growth guidance for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Management declined to give VNB growth guidance, including the 20-25% range an analyst proposed.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the Prudential promoter-to-investor reclassification?
qa_highlights.answer: Prudential holds just under 22%. The board approved its request to reclassify as investor, and the company has submitted it to IRDAI, awaiting its response. Management said no sell-down is required under its reading of the rules.

540136|2026-03.headline: HPL Electric FY26 revenue crossed Rs 1,800 crore; C&I grew 26% to Rs 784 crore and Q4 C&I hit a record Rs 214 crore.
540136|2026-03.overview: FY26 revenue crossed Rs 1,800 crore and Q4 revenue exceeded Rs 500 crore for the first time, with EBITDA growing ahead of revenue and gross margins improving. Consumer and Industrial (C&I) grew 26% to Rs 784 crore and rose to 43% of revenue from 37%, led by wires and cables (up 50% to Rs 340 crore). 540153|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 consolidated total income rose 37.3% YoY to ₹4,116 crores, with EBITDA margin at 14.5%, while raw-material and energy inflation remain a pass-through challenge.
540153|2026-03.overview: Standalone Q4 FY26 total income grew 31.1% YoY to ₹2,975 crores, with EBITDA up 13.7% to ₹371 crores (12.5% margin) and PAT up 20.5% to ₹210 crores. Consolidated Q4 EBITDA rose 30.8% to ₹598 crores, helped by Europe's best-ever quarter (EBITDA €21.9 million, 20.5% margin). Management said full-year standalone RMC rose 1.5 percentage points to 66.82% of revenue, and that ₹73.7 crores of aluminium and steel inflation was not passed through, which would have lifted FY26 EBITDA margin to 13.3% from 12.6%. Management expects Q1 FY27 to stay volatile on energy and metal costs and sees better numbers from Q2.

segments.commentary: Crossed 100,000 wheel sales in January 2026. Total capacity now 48 lakh wheel sets per annum. Bidkin is targeted to reach about ₹600 crores per annum sales by end Q3 or early Q4 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Was there a one-time price impact in Q4 revenue, standalone or Europe?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY26 RMC rose ₹160 crores (66.82% of revenue vs 65.3%), including ₹73.7 crores of non-pass-through aluminium and steel costs and ₹31.3 crores of outsourcing costs. Prior-year Q4 had about ₹25 crores of one-time gains.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ABS revenue trajectory with dual-channel SOP?

qa_highlights.question: Timelines for the greenfield plants and US EV OEM and JLR exports?

qa_highlights.question: Will the company set up manufacturing in the US or Europe given high European energy costs?

qa_highlights.question: Are FY26 margin headwinds behind us?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 FY27 will still be volatile given rising oil, gas and alloy prices. It hopes the war ends next month, expects normalisation after that, and sees better numbers from Q2.

qa_highlights.question: What edge does Endurance have in battery packs and BMS, given OEM backward integration?

qa_highlights.question: What is the Stöferle order book and European growth outlook?

540153|2026-06.headline: Endurance Q1 FY27 standalone total income rose 35.9% to ₹3,194.15 crores, with EBITDA margin at 11.2% after a commodity pass-through headwind.

Consolidated PAT grew 8% to ₹244.52 crores, with Maxwell turning PAT-positive for the first time. Management expects Q2 and Q3 margins to improve as raw material and conversion cost increases are settled with OEMs, and cited multiple SOPs and order wins across 2W, 4W castings, batteries and non-auto solar products.

540153|2026-09.headline: Endurance Technologies Q2 FY27 consolidated income rose 33% YoY to ₹4,811 crore, with EBITDA margin at 12.1% and PAT up 21% to ₹274 crore.
540153|2026-09.overview: Consolidated income grew 33% YoY to ₹4,811 crore, EBITDA rose 17.3% to ₹584 crore (12.1% margin) and PAT rose 21% to ₹274 crore, helped by a ₹36 crore Stöferle step-acquisition gain and offset by a ₹31 crore accelerated depreciation charge in Europe. Standalone India EBITDA margin fell about 2 points to 10.5% as RMC rose to 70% of sales from 66%, because OEMs had not passed through fuel and cutting-tool cost increases in Q1-Q2. Management expects about 0.5% price pass-through from 1 October and a 0.5-0.6% commodity tailwind in Q3, and says the margin trajectory should improve. Order wins were ₹748 crore in H1 FY27, and the company is expanding into 4W castings, proprietary 4W systems, battery packs, solar and non-auto businesses.

financial_highlights.change: +94% YoY, +50% QoQ; PAT positive for consecutive quarters

segments.name: India standalone
segments.commentary: Total income ₹3,761 crore (+40% YoY), EBITDA ₹395 crore at 10.5% margin, up from ₹358 crore in Q1 FY27. Income mix in H1 was 76% India (incl. Maxwell) and 24% Europe.

segments.name: Europe
segments.commentary: Turnover €93.9 million (vs €88.7 million), EBITDA €16.7 million (vs €15.8 million), net result €5.2 million (vs €3.9 million). Net result includes a €3.1 million gain on the Stöferle buyout and ~€3 million accelerated depreciation on a Volkswagen Group project; cash flow €17.7 million.

segments.name: Maxwell (subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue ₹85 crore (+95% YoY, +50% QoQ); H1 turnover ₹141 crore vs ₹161 crore for full FY26. Management targets double-digit margin next financial year.

segments.name: Battery packs / others
segments.commentary: SOP of EV battery packs for a leading 2W OEM, with full ramp-up expected in Q3 FY27; nominations from two PV OEMs with SOP in Q1 and Q2 FY28. Management says margins are decent but not yet disclosed.

guidance_outlook: Q3 FY27: customer price increase of about 0.5% of gross margin from 1 October; commodity basket about 0.5-0.6% positive; overall RMC% to sales expected to fall about 0.6% absolute in Q3.
Greenfield facilities (cumulative capex about ₹1,100 crore) had a ~0.5% negative PBT margin drag in Q2; expected to narrow and turn positive contribution in FY28.
Capex: India FY27 about ₹1,100 crore (FY26 ~₹800 crore); consolidated capex about ₹1,250 crore.
Maharashtra PSI incentive: ₹858 crore total (up from ₹600 crore); ₹75 crore booked in H1 FY27 and ~₹50 crore expected in H2 FY27.
Maxwell targets double-digit EBITDA margin in FY28.

Cumulative SOP targets: 4W suspension, brakes and driveshaft from ₹100 crore in FY28 to ₹800 crore in FY31; non-auto SOP from ₹250 crore in FY28 to ₹650 crore by FY31; proprietary 4W revenue above ₹1,500 crore by FY31 (management says achievable, not within two years).
capex_capacity: ABS capacity to reach 1.54 million units per annum by Q4 FY27, about 70% booked by Bajaj Auto and Royal Enfield; dual-channel ABS supply to Bajaj started October 2026.
New Chennai disc brake assembly plant SOP March 2027; Waluj brakes plant added 1 million units capacity for Hero MotoCorp and TVS (SOP Q2 FY27).
AURIC Shendra 4W casting plant SOP on 25 September 2026, serving Indian, UK and US OEMs; supplies to a US EV OEM have begun. Aluminium forging fifth press SOP in Q4 FY27.
Upside-down fork capacity to reach 100,000 units per month across seven OEM customers including exports by Q4 FY27.
Sanand solar damper plant ready: European client SOP started Q2; US client SOP in H2 FY27; solar actuator SOP Q4 FY27.
Battery pack line capacity cited as about 18,000 2W packs or 8,000 4W packs per month per line.
demand_pricing: Total H1 FY27 business win ₹748 crore (excluding Bajaj), largely HMSI, Tata Motors, Hero MotoCorp, TVS, Ather and a US EV OEM. Cumulative wins since FY22 ₹6,372 crore, of which ₹3,798 crore still to be realised; EV share 24% (11% in FY22); India 4W share 23.5% (16% in FY22).
Europe H1 FY27 order wins €28 million, including two Mercedes orders of €14 million (SOP 2029) and Stellantis €4 million and Mercedes €10 million (SOP 2027).
Bajaj Auto is excluded from order-win figures; management put Bajaj at about 35% of group income (H1 income ₹9,159 crore).
Management says EV revenue margin is broadly similar to the company average, with battery packs and BMS adding new revenue.

Management cites EU policy changes: a 350,000-unit cap on Chinese plug-in and mild hybrid imports from 1 December 2026, duties on Chinese BEVs (BYD 27%, Geely 29%, SAIC 45%), and a proposed 70% EU-origin content rule for non-battery EV components.

qa_highlights.question: How should gross margin in India be read, given commodity easing and conversion-cost pass-through?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said customers agreed to about 0.5% price increase from 1 October, plus a 0.5-0.6% commodity benefit; some customers may pass through in Q4 and others in FY28. Management said the commodity headwind appears largely behind it.

qa_highlights.question: Why diversify, and which non-auto areas are near term versus long term?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the strategy builds on die-casting and aluminium strengths. Engagements are advanced in power backup, robotics and railways; aviation and defence are under active consideration with indirect supply started. Most areas should see commercial production this year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the solar business's size, customer base, margin and asset turnover?
qa_highlights.answer: Two customers, in Spain and the US. Management targets ₹250 crore next year and ₹650 crore by FY31 across railways and solar; asset turnover expected above 8x because it is mostly assembly.

qa_highlights.question: What is Bajaj's share of revenue, and when does Maxwell reach double-digit margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Bajaj is about 35% of group income (H1 FY27 income ₹9,159 crore). Maxwell targets double-digit margin in the next financial year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the battery pack capacity and margin profile?
qa_highlights.answer: One 2W OEM reaches peak sales this quarter; two 4W nominations start around March/April 2027 and Q2 FY28. Management says margins are decent and ROCE is good, but gave no figure.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Fondalpress acquired, and what are the synergies?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Fondalpress is a former competitor with about €80 million turnover in 2017 and 16 die-casting machines (2,300-2,800 ton), 16,400 sq m of buildings, and €10.2 million cash. The purchase price was €12.3 million; it will insource Stöferle castings and enable truck and Stellantis transmission housings.

qa_highlights.question: Can four-wheeler order wins of about ₹1,500 crore translate into revenue, and when?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the proprietary 4W products (driveshaft, brakes, suspension, battery packs) could cross ₹1,500 crore by FY31; the won orders are expected to convert over about two years, and the figure includes casting only in the broader context.

qa_highlights.question: Will EV mix dilute corporate margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said EV margins are similar to the company average and aim to improve them; with the new battery pack business, EV is margin-accretive overall.

risks_watch: Gross margin recovery depends on customer price pass-through: about 0.5% from 1 October is agreed by only some customers, others may pass through in Q4 or FY28.
Standalone RMC at 70% of sales (vs 66%) and whether the expected ~0.6% absolute RMC reduction in Q3 materialises, given management expects steel to rise.
Greenfield facilities (~₹1,100 crore cumulative capex) carried about a 0.5% negative PBT margin drag in Q2; watch whether the drag narrows and turns positive in FY28.
Proprietary 4W revenue target above ₹1,500 crore by FY31 and whether driveshaft, brake, suspension and battery pack SOPs hit the timelines given (several are H1 FY28 or later).
Europe: Stöferle integration, Fondalpress ramp-up, ~€3 million accelerated depreciation on a Volkswagen Group project, and whether EU import caps and local-content rules lift volumes.
Maxwell double-digit EBITDA margin target for FY28 and battery pack margins, which management has not disclosed.
key_quotes: Overall, as of now, we see an absolute 0.6% lowering of RMC percentage to sales in Q3.
So, what I would like to highlight here is that we are seeing that the commodity headwind seems to be largely behind as we stand, and we expect the margin trajectory to improve from here on.
But when you ask me to put a number , it could be what I told you - by FY31 crossing ₹ 1,500 crores for the proprietary.
But of course, margins would be decent. And of course, once we start, our focus is to increase our margins.
540153|2026-09.management_tone: Management was confident on order flow, EV and non-auto diversification and the Q3 margin recovery, but was cautious and non-specific on numbers, declining to give battery pack margins, non-auto mix to 2030 and a firm non-auto revenue figure. Price pass-through and commodity benefits were presented as only partly agreed with customers.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: H1 FY27 order wins of ₹748 crore (excluding Bajaj), with cumulative wins of ₹6,372 crore since FY22 of which ₹3,798 crore is still to be realised; India EV sales rose 185% YoY to ₹229 crore; no explicit volume % guided.

rows.why: Battery pack SOP ramp for a leading 2W OEM completes in Q3 FY27, two PV OEM battery pack nominations start Q1-Q2 FY28, and the Sanand solar actuator SOP is in Q4 FY27 with US solar SOP in H2 FY27.

rows.label: Proprietary 4W and non-auto SOP ramp to FY31
rows.why: Targets are 4W SOPs of ₹100 crore in FY28 rising to ₹800 crore in FY31, non-auto SOP of ₹250 crore in FY28 rising to ₹650 crore by FY31, and proprietary 4W above ₹1,500 crore by FY31, though management says this is not achievable within two years.

rows.label: EU import caps and local-content rules

rows.label: Maxwell double-digit EBITDA margin
rows.why: Maxwell revenue reached ₹85 crore in Q2 (+94% YoY) and PAT has been positive for consecutive quarters, with management targeting double-digit EBITDA margin in FY28.

540173|2026-03.headline: PNB Housing Q4 FY26 disbursements rose 36% YoY to INR 9,355 crores; FY27 guidance is loan book above INR 1 lakh crore and ROA 2.4-2.5%.
540173|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 disbursements grew 36% YoY and 50% QoQ to INR 9,355 crores, with retail disbursements up 32% YoY to INR 9,020 crores. PAT rose 19% YoY to INR 656 crores in Q4 and 18% to INR 2,291 crores for FY26, helped by negative credit cost of 45 bps from write-off pool recoveries. Spread compressed 10 bps QoQ to 2.12% on lower incremental yields and balance transfer pressure in Prime, while reported NIM rose 6 bps to 3.69%. Management guided that yields have bottomed out, with FY27 retail loan growth of 18-20%, NIM of 3.55-3.65% and ROA of 2.4-2.5%.

financial_highlights.change: -15 bps QoQ; FY26 7.57% vs 7.86% in FY25
+13% YoY; opex to ATA 1.05% FY26, 1.08% Q4
Recoveries INR 167 crores in Q4, INR 330-332 crores in FY26

segments.name: Affordable
segments.commentary: Q4 disbursement INR 1,249 crores, up 59% QoQ but flat YoY; FY26 disbursement about INR 3,800 crores, targeted to grow about 50%. Management says GNPA in affordable is below 0.6%.

segments.name: Emerging Market
segments.commentary: Disbursement grew 34% YoY in Q4. Segment share of retail loan book rose with affordable plus emerging at 40% of retail book (37% a year earlier).

segments.name: Prime
segments.commentary: Disbursement grew 43% YoY in Q4 despite yield pressure from rate cuts. Management says Prime disbursement largely replenishes runoff; Prime loan growth is about 9%.

segments.name: Corporate
segments.commentary: Restarted with INR 335 crores disbursed in Q4 FY26; corporate loan book INR 401 crores at 31 March 2026. Target yield 11.5-12%, capped at about 3% of book in FY27.

guidance_outlook: Loan book to cross INR 1 lakh crore in FY27.
Retail loan book growth of 18-20% in FY27; overall book growth stated as 18-20%.
NIM guided at 3.55-3.65% for FY27; management expects spread-NIM gap to normalise from Q1 FY27.
ROA guided at 2.4-2.5% for FY27.
Credit cost expected to stay negative at about 15-20 bps in FY27, with recoveries of INR 200-250 crores.
Opex to ATA expected to stay in a 1-1.1% range; cost of borrowing stable or 5-10 bps better.
Affordable and emerging to reach about 50% of the book in two to three years; corporate to reach 5-6% in year two and 8-9% in year three.
capex_capacity: Opened 35 branches in Q4 FY26, taking the network to 393 branches (229 affordable, 87 emerging market).
Management said the priority is to make existing branches more productive rather than adding many more.
Infinity in-house digital onboarding app is fully adopted by the in-house sales team; direct selling agents are being onboarded.
Digital channels generate about 15% of leads.
Micro LAP and micro housing products planned for launch in Q1 FY27 in the 14-16% yield segment.
demand_pricing: Management cited intense pricing competition, especially in Q4, and said affordable yield fell about 75 bps QoQ to as low as 11.35%.
Balance transfer (BT) out was 8.6% in Q4 FY26 vs 8.95% in Q3 and 8% for FY26.
Industry housing finance growth cited at 12-13%; the company describes itself as third-largest in the industry.
Incremental cost of borrowing rose to 7.23% in Q4 from 7.2% in Q3 amid current liquidity conditions.
Non-housing share of the book at 32.4% vs 30.6% in Q3; PBC retail home loans at 65%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the spread fall while NIM rose, and will the ROA gap normalise?
qa_highlights.answer: Vinay Gupta said the divergence is a methodology difference (daily spread convention vs monthly NIM averaging) and should normalise from next quarter, with NIM in a 5-10 bps range of current trajectory.

qa_highlights.question: What credit cost is built into the 2.4-2.5% ROA guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Vinay Gupta said credit cost is expected to remain negative at about 15-20 bps in FY27, with write-off pool recoveries continuing; mix shift to emerging, affordable and corporate should support NIM over 2-3 years.

qa_highlights.question: Why did affordable disbursements weaken and is it linked to asset quality?
qa_highlights.answer: Ajai Kumar Shukla said affordable disbursements rebounded in Q4, mid-year challenges were temporary and fixed, and quality is not the reason; Prime disbursement reflects replenishment of runoff.

qa_highlights.question: What early bounce and stress indicators are visible for April?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said April bounce rates are similar to March, with no significant jump; a one-off government-employee EMI bounce was cleared the next day.

qa_highlights.question: Why is management confident yields have bottomed out?
qa_highlights.answer: Ajai Kumar Shukla said no repo change in recent months, so balance transfer outflows should restrict, supporting yield; BT out improved from Q3 to Q4.

qa_highlights.question: What was the nature of the INR 335 crore corporate disbursement?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the one case in FY26 was about INR 360-370 crores, primarily in Mumbai; focus is on reputed builders in about seven or eight top cities, with corporate at about 3% of book in FY27.

risks_watch: Yield recovery depends on balance transfer outflows staying restricted and on no further rate cuts; management also flagged possible upside in market rates.
Credit cost is negative because of write-off pool recoveries (about INR 500 crores corporate and INR 325 crores retail remaining); normalisation could weigh on ROA.
Opex grew 13% and the full cost of 35 Q4 branches will flow into FY27; opex to ATA target 1-1.1%.
Cost of borrowing: management expects only stable to 5-10 bps improvement; a rating upgrade is being pursued as a lever.
Geopolitical and crude-oil risk could affect inflation, rates and asset quality, though management sees no early stress as of mid-April.
Prime 30+ DPD on a like-for-like basis is 2.72% (investor presentation figure of 3.31% includes Stage-2 SICR accounts).
540173|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on growth, disbursement recovery and asset quality, with the yield-bottoming call supported by balance transfer trends. Cautious on cost of borrowing, which management says has limited room to fall, and it was hedged on geopolitical risk. Some answers on the Q4 spread-NIM divergence and the 30+ DPD figures needed clarification.
key_quotes: We are looking for loan book to cross more than INR 1 lakh crores mark in FY'27.
In our view, the yield have bottomed out and should start improving from Q1 FY'27.
The mantra would be growth with quality.
Affordable has started shaping up now.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Network grew to 393 branches after 35 openings in Q4 FY26, but management prioritises productivity of existing branches over adding many more, so further openings are not guided.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Q4 FY26 disbursements rose 36% YoY to INR 9,355 crores, and FY27 guidance is retail book growth of 18-20% (FY26 retail book INR 86,946 crores, +16% YoY), backed by affordable and emerging disbursement momentum.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Guidance is set at new levels (book above INR 1 lakh crore, NIM 3.55-3.65%, ROA 2.4-2.5%) with intense pricing competition and falling yields, leaving little room for an upgrade.

rows.why: Credit cost is negative at -45 bps in FY26 only because write-off pool recoveries (INR 330-332 crores) are flowing; guidance assumes -15 to -20 bps, and affordable yield fell about 75 bps QoQ to 11.35%, with cost of borrowing at 7.35% in Q4 and only 5-10 bps improvement expected.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Micro LAP and micro housing products are planned for launch in Q1 FY27 in the 14-16% yield segment, with no size quantified.

rows.label: Corporate book capped at about 3% in FY27
rows.why: Corporate book was INR 401 crores at 31 March 2026, restarted with INR 335 crores disbursed in Q4 FY26, with a target yield of 11.5-12% and cap at about 3% of book.

rows.label: Cost of borrowing 5-10 bps better, rating upgrade pursued
rows.why: Cost of borrowing is 7.35% in Q4 (FY26 7.57% vs 7.86% FY25), management guides only stable to 5-10 bps better and says a rating upgrade is a lever; incremental cost rose to 7.23% from 7.2%.

rows.label: Yield bottoming on restricted balance transfer outflows
rows.why: BT out fell to 8.6% in Q4 from 8.95% in Q3 with no repo change recently, but intense affordable pricing competition (affordable yield 11.35%) and rate-cut risk remain.

tone.note: Management was confident on disbursement recovery, asset quality (GNPA 0.93%) and yield bottoming, but cautious on cost of borrowing and hedged on geopolitical risk; analysts probed the Q4 spread-NIM divergence, the Prime 30+ DPD figures and the sustainability of negative credit cost.

540173|2026-06.headline: PNB Housing Q1 FY27 PAT rose 4% YoY to INR 557 crore, with ROA 2.37% and ROE 11.44%, while NIM fell 19 bps QoQ to 3.50%.
540173|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 PAT grew 4% YoY to INR 557 crore, with ROA of 2.37% and ROE of 11.44%. Disbursements moved to a cheque-realisation basis this quarter, so reported disbursement grew 18% YoY to INR 5,882 crore against 56% on the old cheque-handover basis. Loan book grew 15% YoY to INR 89,670 crore, NIM moderated to 3.50% and gross NPA was 0.95%. Management says margin and yield have bottomed and expects Q2 to be much better than Q1, especially in Affordable.

financial_highlights.change: -19 bps QoQ (12 bps leverage, 7 bps Q4 true-up)

financial_highlights.metric: Spread / portfolio yield / cost of borrowing
financial_highlights.change: Spread stable QoQ; yield +1 bp; cost of borrowing +1 bp

financial_highlights.value: Negative 12 bps (recoveries INR 67 crore from written-off pool)

segments.name: Prime
segments.commentary: Disbursement INR 3,083 crore in Q1 FY27, double-digit YoY growth; Prime yield up about 8 bps QoQ, which management attributes mostly to mix shift toward self-employed and non-home loans.

segments.name: Emerging Markets
segments.commentary: Disbursement INR 2,029 crore in Q1 FY27, double-digit YoY growth; INR 71 crore disbursed under the new Emerging Developer Finance programme.

segments.name: Affordable / Emerging (retail)
segments.commentary: Affordable and Emerging book grew 27% YoY and is 41% of retail portfolio (target 45% by FY27-end). Affordable net disbursement only INR 555 crore, below target; management cites about 11% YoY growth on a like-for-like basis.

segments.name: Corporate loan book
segments.commentary: INR 493 crore outstanding at 30 June 2026, with about INR 215 crore disbursed in Q1 FY27.

segments.name: Written-off pool (retail)
segments.commentary: About INR 340 crore remaining; INR 67 crore recovered in Q1. One legacy account of about INR 420 crore was classified as fraud, already fully provided in FY23, so no incremental P&L impact.

guidance_outlook: Full-year FY27 overall loan book growth guidance of 18% to 20% maintained; management says it expects to beat it.
Affordable loan book growth guidance of 50% to 60% maintained for FY27.
Construction finance capped at about 3% of the overall book in FY27.
Affordable and Emerging share to reach 45% of book by FY27-end and about 50% in FY28.
FY27 ROA guided around 2.4%; FY28 ROA around 2.3% as credit cost normalises. Long-term ROA 2.3% to 2.35%.
NIM expected to have bottomed; gradual improvement from H2 FY27. Yield expected to keep improving on mix.
Credit cost expected to stay negative through FY27 on continued recoveries.
Q2 FY27 disbursement (net) expected 60% to 70% above Q1 overall and 2.5x to 2.6x in Affordable; management says July was promising.
Rating upgrades (CARE done; ICRA and CRISIL pending) expected to cut cost of borrowing by at least about 10 bps.
capex_capacity: Branch network expanded by 12 in the quarter to 404 branches.
Affordable business launched from selected Prime and Emerging branches; about INR 30 crore disbursed in June, and 15% to 18% of Affordable business in July.
Management does not plan to open more branches; plans to use existing branches to contain opex.
Micro-housing policy formulated and rolled out in Q2 FY27; meaningful contribution expected from H2 FY27.
Full buyout transactions started; loan assets of INR 146 crore acquired in Q1 FY27.
demand_pricing: Management cites steady housing demand across retail mortgage segments, particularly Affordable and Emerging Markets; RBI repo unchanged at 5.25%.
Gross disbursement YoY growth of 56% on cheque-handover basis vs 18% on the new net basis; the gap reflects the accounting change, not lost demand.
Incremental disbursement yield is above the 9.48% book yield, per management.
Incremental cost of borrowing rose about 18 bps in Q1 on tighter liquidity and market volatility; management says it has eased somewhat but remains elevated.
BT-in share of sourcing fell to 4.4% from 5% a year ago; Affordable BT-in fell to 3.4% from 10.5%.
Prime yield mix benefit about 10 to 15 bps; Affordable yield up about 50 bps QoQ per management.

qa_highlights.question: How should yield and cost of funds trend, and does the medium-term NIM expansion thesis from mix shift toward Affordable/Emerging/CF still hold over two years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margin, yield and cost of funds have all bottomed; gradual margin improvement expected from H2 FY27. Construction finance capped at 3% of book in FY27; Affordable and Emerging share at 41% now, targeting 45% by FY27-end and nearly 50% in two years.

qa_highlights.question: Will the gross disbursement momentum (55%+ on cheque-handover basis) carry into Q2 and make the 18-20% loan growth guidance conservative?
qa_highlights.answer: Management aims to beat both gross and net Q2 numbers, said Q2 gross will be much better than Q1 and July showed strong gross and net momentum. It said it expects to do much better than the 18-20% loan growth guidance but did not raise it.

qa_highlights.question: Why did leverage and NII move sharply when debt-to-equity barely changed?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said average leverage rose from 3.6x to 3.75x; Q4 disbursement realisations flowed into Q1 borrowings, and lower investment yields also weighed on total yield.

qa_highlights.question: Is the gap between reported and gross disbursement across all segments, and what is Affordable growth on a like-for-like basis?
qa_highlights.answer: The gap spans Prime, Emerging and Affordable since retail and wholesale moved to debit-from-account recognition. Like-for-like Affordable YoY growth is about 11%.

qa_highlights.question: Will credit cost turn positive in H2, and what ROA path follows?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said credit cost should stay negative through FY27 given line of sight on recoveries. FY27 ROA guided around 2.4%; FY28 around 2.3% as credit cost normalises; long-term 2.3% to 2.35%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did recoveries of about INR 77 crore not fully flow through ECL writeback, and where did the difference go?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said regular OTS settlements cost about INR 10-12 crore, booked as write-offs in Prime and Emerging legacy pool, explaining the gap versus the INR 67 crore recovery figure.

qa_highlights.question: What is Q2 net disbursement growth versus Q1 net, and what does July look like?
qa_highlights.answer: Overall Q2 net disbursement expected about 60-70% above Q1 net; Affordable 2.5x-2.6x Q1 net. Management said July was promising, with Prime and Emerging contributing 15-18% of Affordable business in July.

qa_highlights.question: How much benefit from rating upgrades and when will it show in cost of borrowing?
qa_highlights.answer: CARE upgrade is done; ICRA and CRISIL pending. CFO said at least about 10 bps reduction in cost of borrowing should come through; some fresh borrowing already at better rates.

qa_highlights.question: Prime yield rose 8 bps: how much is mix versus like-for-like, and does self-employed mix raise risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed about 10-15 bps benefit to mix shift toward self-employed and non-home loans; without mix, Prime yield would have been roughly stable at 8.92-8.95%. Delinquency in Prime and Emerging said to have improved QoQ.

risks_watch: Affordable execution: Q1 net disbursement of INR 555 crore is below target; Q2 needs 2.5-2.6x Q1 net and 50-60% full-year Affordable growth is guided, with new CBO leadership still unproven.

Cost of borrowing: incremental cost rose about 18 bps in Q1 and management says it is still elevated; the NIM bottoming thesis depends on yield gains offsetting this plus further leverage increase (average 3.6x to 3.75x).
Rating upgrades: ICRA and CRISIL still pending; management expects at least 10 bps cost-of-funds benefit, timing not firm.

540175|2026-03.headline: Regency Fincorp FY26 PAT rose 170% to INR13.4 crore on AUM of INR261.2 crore (up 45%), with secured MSME now about 61% of AUM.

Management outlined a target of INR500-550 crore AUM this year and INR3,000 crore by FY30, funded by INR400-450 crore of expected lender borrowings. Cost of funds is currently 13-14%, with a target of 11-12% and a longer-term aim of 10-10.5%.

540175|2026-06.management_tone: Confident and expansive on growth, digital strategy and cost-of-funds reduction, but evasive on promoter holding (deferred to one-to-one) and on quarterly profit outlook beyond calling the numbers conservative. Several answers were long and repetitive, and some figures (NNPA 0.74% vs 0.76%, digital share 6% vs 20% target) were inconsistent across the call.
key_quotes: We are not wanting being at a 23%, 24%. Our desire is 15%, 16%, 17%, okay?
We are not funding any thing which is related to livestock, whether it is a poultry, whether it is an animal husbandry onto it.

Our medium-term objective is very clear, that is to scale AUM towards INR500 to INR550 crores by the end of this fiscal year while maintaining strong asset quality, capital adequacy and governance standards.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: AUM is guided from INR345 crore to INR500-550 crore by year-end, about 45-60% growth in roughly three quarters, backed by secured book up 44% QoQ to INR230 crore and the planned INR50-75 crore NCD placement in Q2.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex was not discussed; the asset-light model with branches capped at INR12 crore AUM and growth funded by NCDs of INR50-75 crore and a INR10 crore bank line points to no major capex announcement.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management called FY27 revenue guidance of upwards of INR75 crore conservative against Q1 total income of INR17.4 crore (+86% YoY), but gave no quarterly path.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Guided PAT of INR25-30 crore requires a step-up from INR7.0 crore in Q1 (roughly 3.5-4x over the remaining three quarters), and NCDs are still being raised at 13-14%, so the cost-of-funds path is not yet proven.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: PPI licence approved and expected to be operational in about 3-5 months, so launch falls around Q2 FY27 end to Q3 FY27.

rows.label: Debt funding via NCDs and bank lines to fund growth

rows.label: Small finance bank conversion by FY30
rows.why: Management targets SFB status by FY30 with no deposit-taking until then, and cites an AUM target of INR3,000 crore by FY30; this is a long-dated, conditional goal.

rows.label: MSME secured yield reduction to 15-17%
rows.why: Yield on MSME deployments is about 21-22% today and management plans to pass lower borrowing costs to customers, which would compress yields toward 15-17% over time and could trade off against spread.
