540358|2026-03.headline: RMC Switchgears FY26 consolidated revenue rose 26.4% to Rs 401.59 crore, but profit fell short, with Q4 back to Rs 9.3 crore net profit after a Q3 loss of Rs 7.07 crore.
540358|2026-03.overview: Management framed the call as an analyst day rather than a results discussion, covering FY26 as a year of progress and learning. Consolidated revenue grew 26.4% to Rs 401.59 crore, but margins were hit by PulseBox product development spend, rain-delayed execution in Maharashtra, and solar EPC cost pressure from China-linked supply, safeguard duty and aluminium/silver prices. Q4 returned to profit (Rs 9.3 crore) from a Rs 7.07 crore loss in Q3, which management attributed to execution catch-up and better material availability. Receivables rose from Rs 148 crore to Rs 205 crore and operating cash flow turned negative; management attributed this mainly to March-concentrated billing. No FY27 revenue or profit guidance was given; management said the unexecuted order book is about Rs 850 crore plus and the tender pipeline about Rs 1,500 crore plus.

540376|2026-06.headline: DMart FY26 revenue near INR67,000 crore (+16%), PAT margin ~4.8%; management targets ~15% annual store additions and says SSSG stays at last year's levels.
540376|2026-06.overview: This was DMart's annual analyst call, the first with Anshul Asawa as MD & CEO, covering FY26 results and the outlook for FY27. Management said the fundamentals were intact but flagged higher staff costs for capability build, a slowdown in same-store growth in mature metro stores, and heavy competitive pressure from quick commerce. Avenue E-commerce (DMart Ready) was narrowed to 11 cities after exits from seven cities, with its EBITDA falling about 43% and a net loss of INR307 crore. Management reiterated a roughly 15% internal store-addition target and did not disclose e-commerce KPIs.

financial_highlights.change: Roughly flat; gross margin +16 bps, employee cost +27 bps, other expenses -9 bps
Total debt incl. AS 116 INR2,267 crore
Retail business area ~20.6 million sq ft
Sales +17%; PBT -24%; net loss INR307 crore

segments.name: Avenue Supermarts (standalone DMart stores)
segments.commentary: Sales +~16% with gross margin up 16 bps to within the 14-15% range; employee cost up ~33% in standalone financials including wage code impact. Entered five new states in FY26.

segments.name: Avenue E-commerce (DMart Ready)
segments.commentary: Sales +17% but EBITDA down ~43% and net loss INR307 crore. Exited seven quick-commerce cities; now focused on 11 cities, with 165 pickup points cited. Contract labour cost +24% and transport +34%.

segments.name: Align Retail (grocery packing)
segments.commentary: Sales +~16.5% and PAT +~24%.

segments.name: Avenue Food Plaza (fast/ready food)
segments.commentary: Sales +~35.5%; returned to profit with PAT margin ~9% after prior-year losses from expansion.

guidance_outlook: Internal store-addition benchmark ~15% of store base annually; could run a few points higher or lower depending on real estate timing.
Same-store growth expected to hover around last financial year's level (~7.5-8%) for FY27 for older stores; no sharp increase expected, all else equal.
Long-term North Star: ~15% gross margin and ~5% net margin; no intention to expand margin at the cost of customer proposition.
Expect efficiency gains in AEL from consolidation to 11 cities in FY27 onwards, per AEL CEO.
Staff cost built ahead of volume growth; management says it is hard to say if the build-up has ended.
Plans to invest in ERP and wider technology upgrades; management expects only marginal near-term margin impact.
capex_capacity: FY26 store additions: 85, with 15 on long-term lease; 68 stores in total now on lease out of 500+.
Land-to-store conversion takes 2-3 years depending on store configuration; pipeline of projects covers the next 2-3 years.
Debt: CP outstanding ~INR800 crore; INR1,000 crore NCD approved, may take total borrowing to ~INR2,000 crore by year-end, mainly to fund capex and reduce cost of debt.
Warehouses added in FY26 raised inventory days to 33.2.
demand_pricing: Quick commerce competition intensifying in dense metros (Mumbai, Bangalore, Hyderabad) where mature stores are saturated; management cites capacity, saturation, high throughput and competition as reasons for slower metro SSSG.
Management says FMCG vendors are not shifting attention away from DMart; many are doubling down.
Management says monthly/bulk shopping in metros is stable and strong, with good traction in Tier 1 and Tier 2 cities; newer Tier 2/3 stores are doing better than older metro stores.
Pricing follows vendor pass-through; no pricing guidance given.
Quarterly growth was 13% (Dec-25 quarter, deflation in staples), 19% (Mar-26 quarter, panic buying), and 15% (Jun-26 quarter).

qa_highlights.question: Will SSSG recover to double-digit levels given quick-commerce and maturity pressures in metros?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said SSSG is likely to hover around the current range (~7-8%) and not rise considerably, especially for older stores; new stores are opened nearby to reduce pressure on existing stores.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the 15% store-addition target conservative and can it go to 100-150 stores a year?
qa_highlights.answer: Internal target is ~15%; capital and people are not constraints, and land acquisition, permissions and build time (2-3 years) are. Management said 100-150 stores is not a reasonable number at about 500 stores currently.

qa_highlights.question: What is the economics of leasing versus owning stores?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to share lease vs owned economics; said both models work. 68 stores are on long leases and 15 of the 85 stores added in FY26 were leased. Niladri said PBT is a fair measure of lease impact.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the mix of AEL get cut to 11 cities and why not experiment with faster delivery?
qa_highlights.answer: Seven cities were exited because their contribution was minimal. Management said it will not pursue immediate delivery; it will prove the six-hour slotted model in 11 cities first because losses had grown with expansion.

qa_highlights.question: What is driving the rise in employee costs and why are contractual headcounts lower?
qa_highlights.answer: Permanent headcount rose ~4,000 (75-80% of additions are store-management cohorts). Frontline staff are non-permanent; productivity and mechanisation held down non-permanent headcount. Wage code from December 2025 also added costs.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company add non-metro growth via quick commerce given Flipkart and Blinkit expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: Management does not see a risk of LFL falling below 5%; it sees organised retail still under-penetrated in smaller towns and has no point of view on QC adoption outside top cities.

risks_watch: Continued SSSG slowdown in mature metro stores (~7-8% range expected) as quick commerce and new nearby stores take share.
AEL profitability: EBITDA down ~43% with net loss INR307 crore; watch whether consolidation to 11 cities improves throughput and transport/labour costs in FY27.
Rising staff costs (employee cost +27 bps of sales, standalone employee expense up ~33%) with wage code impact and capability build.
Lower return ratios (ROE ~13.5%, ROCE ~17.1%) and rising debt to fund expansion; NCD plan of INR1,000 crore.
Store-addition pace (85 in FY26 vs ~15% target) depends on land and lease availability; slower ramp in new Tier 2/3 stores.
Management declined to disclose DMart Ready KPIs, store-level margins, lease economics, land value, and category-level data.

540401|2026-06.headline: Maximus Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose about 52% YoY to INR59.91 crores, but EBITDA margin fell to 7.64% from 9.81% on Middle East war input costs.
540401|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue from operations was INR59.91 crores versus INR39.52 crores a year earlier, with EBITDA up about 18% to INR4.58 crores. Margin compression, attributed to higher input and freight costs from the ongoing Middle East war, and higher finance costs (INR1.53 crores vs INR0.92 crores) left PAT at INR2.05 crores versus INR2.33 crores a year ago. Management highlighted the proposed associate acquisition of Quebec Petroleum (40% stake), a Kenya grease plant planned for Q3 FY27, and a Tanzania warehousing expansion. Management guided to crossing about INR200 crores revenue in FY27 on a conservative basis.

segments.name: Manufacturing
segments.commentary: Highest EBITDA margin among the three verticals (manufacturing, toll blending, trading) in Q1 FY27 and historically. Operations in UAE and Kenya.

segments.name: Toll blending
segments.commentary: Management says it is being pursued aggressively; in talks with an East African MNC for toll blending.

segments.name: Trading
segments.commentary: Lowest-margin vertical per management. Long-term target split: manufacturing plus toll blending 75-80%, trading 20-25%.

segments.name: Specialty lubricants
segments.commentary: Contribute around 40% of topline, per CFO.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue expected to cross about INR200 crores on a conservative basis, with healthy EBITDA margins (stated even under the ongoing war scenario).
Margins expected to hold at current levels or improve over the next couple of quarters if supply disruption persists, through product mix diversification.
Kenya grease manufacturing facility planned for commissioning in Q3 FY27.
Tanzania expansion: initially warehousing and distribution, moving to manufacturing once scale is reached.
Recently launched modernisation programme: automated batch blending, additional storage and warehousing, improved filling lines, and capacity expansion at UAE and Kenya plants.
Capacity considered sufficient for next 2-3 years on single-shift basis; additional storage capex needed for full utilisation.
capex_capacity: Combined manufacturing capacity of about 50,000 KL across UAE and Kenya plants.
Capacity utilisation at about 45% across both units.
Kenya grease plant to cater to East African market, which has few grease manufacturers; also to support toll blending.
Proposed acquisition of an additional manufacturing unit as an associate; process underway, details to be shared later.
Quebec Petroleum: associate investment with initial 40% stake, aimed at entering the Indian domestic market.
demand_pricing: Management says demand for lubricants is supported by industrialisation, infrastructure, vehicle ownership and mining, power and construction; customers are shifting toward premium and specialty products.
Cited Middle East and Africa lubricant market growing from about USD 9.1 billion (2024) to USD 12.4 billion (2034).
Company serves more than 400 customers across 25+ countries and 50+ industries.
Top 10 customers account for roughly 70-75% of revenue, including distributors; company sells mainly through distributors, not B2C.
Product prices and landed costs (freight, insurance) rose due to the Middle East war; company passed on a partial cost increase, which also raised receivables.
Base oil and white oil prices are positively correlated with crude, with a lagged and non-identical impact on lubricant prices.
In Kenya, incumbents Shell and Total have not changed payment terms despite new entrants.

qa_highlights.question: How sensitive are margins to base oil and crude price movements?
qa_highlights.answer: Not directly coupled but positively correlated; raw materials (base oils and white oils) move in the same direction with a lag and not in the same proportion.

qa_highlights.question: Current utilisation of the 50,000 KL capacity, and targets over 2-3 years?
qa_highlights.answer: About 45% utilised; capacity is sufficient for 2-3 years on a single shift, but full utilisation would need additional storage capex.

qa_highlights.question: Which vertical has the highest EBITDA margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Manufacturing, both in Q1 FY27 and historically; toll blending is being pursued more aggressively.

qa_highlights.question: Share of premium and specialty versus conventional revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Specialty lubricants contribute around 40% of topline.

qa_highlights.question: Why have receivables risen faster than revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Higher topline (about 50% growth), higher product prices and landed costs from the war, and partial pass-through of cost increases to selling prices.

qa_highlights.question: What if supply disruption lasts more than six months?
qa_highlights.answer: Management has onboarded new customers and broadened product baskets; margins may dip further but aim to hold or improve through diversification; still expects over INR200 crores revenue in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: How will Quebec Petroleum contribute?
qa_highlights.answer: Associate with 40% stake; its profits will be included in consolidated financials; focus is India domestic market, while Maximus covers Middle East, East and North Africa.

qa_highlights.question: Target revenue split between trading and toll blending over three years?
qa_highlights.answer: Manufacturing plus toll blending 75-80%, trading 20-25%; split between manufacturing and toll blending not disclosed as they overlap in co-branding.

qa_highlights.question: Concentration of revenue and B2B versus B2C mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Top 10 customers about 70-75% of revenue (distributors included); no own retail outlets; major revenue comes via distribution channels.

risks_watch: Margin compression: EBITDA margin down about 217 bps YoY to 7.64% due to input and freight costs from the Middle East war.
Working capital: receivables rising faster than revenue; financial cost up about 65% YoY to INR1.53 crores.
Customer concentration: top 10 customers about 70-75% of revenue.
Quebec Petroleum associate acquisition and additional manufacturing unit acquisition: terms and financials not yet disclosed.
Competitive response in Kenya from incumbents such as Shell and Total; payment terms unchanged so far.
Management did not split revenue between manufacturing and toll blending; the reported Q1 PAT decline despite revenue growth needs monitoring.

up ~INR0.6 crores from INR0.92 crores in Q1 FY26

540403|2026-03.headline: CL Educate revenue rose about 55% to ₹570 crore in FY26 and EBITDA more than doubled to ₹69 crore, driven by the DEXIT acquisition.
540403|2026-03.overview: Management reported FY26 as the first year the group crossed ₹500 crore revenue, with revenue up from ₹368 crore to ₹570 crore and EBITDA up from ₹33 crore to ₹69 crore. Cash generated from operations rose to ₹79 crore from ₹26 crore, and the acquisition-linked borrowing has been reduced from ₹210 crore to ₹180 crore. The DEXIT (assessments) integration is described as complete. The L&D/EdTech segment remains under structural pressure, with realisations down 12-14% and revenue down about 11%, and management expects it to stay flat for roughly four more quarters. Fundraising has been put on a slight pause.

financial_highlights.change: acquisition debt reduced to ₹180 crore from ₹210 crore

financial_highlights.metric: Cash and bank balance (as on date)
financial_highlights.change: from about ₹50 crore last year, excluding ₹185-190 crore pending RPS redemption

segments.name: Assessments (DEXIT)
segments.commentary: Revenue rose to ₹223 crore from ₹205 crore and EBITDA to about ₹51 crore from ₹34 crore. All existing contracts were rolled over and 20 new customers were added. FY27 order book is about 80-85% of FY26 revenue, per management.

segments.name: L&D / EdTech (test prep, university engagement, publishing)
segments.commentary: Enrollment volume grew about 4% but average realisation fell 12-14%, so revenue declined about 11%. Management expects revenue to stay roughly flat for about four quarters, with profitability improving from Q1 FY27 after cost recalibration.

segments.name: MarTech (Kestone, events, VOSMOS, VIRSA)
segments.commentary: Revenue grew about 11% to about ₹161 crore: international up about 20%, India up about 5%. EBITDA was slightly lower due to set-up costs for the new social events and luxury wedding business. Domestic to international mix is about 1:2.

guidance_outlook: Assessments: management expects reasonably healthy revenue growth in FY27, backed by an order book of about 80-85% of FY26 revenue six weeks into the year.
L&D: revenue expected flat for about four more quarters; profitability expected to show upward movement from Q1 FY27.
MarTech: shift to higher-margin CEP and VOSMOS/VIRSA products over 12-18 months; pruning low-margin MMS and pass-through businesses.
Discontinued operations: bulk of losses done, with a little residual impact possible in Q1 FY27 and none expected beyond that.
Talevate: target to sign 8-10 corporates and about 100 jobs over the next few quarters, testing the MVP before scaling.
capex_capacity: Working capital is about 50% of revenue despite about 50% revenue growth, per management.
Management is marketing land assets, including a Raipur plot earmarked for a school, and is seeking a buyer at the right price.
A new EdTech personalised-learning pilot is to launch in about one month, with a roll-out to all programmes and centres if successful.
Remote proctoring and BYOD technology is being built out at DEXIT; the mySathi IP platform has started going to market.
Settlement of ₹185-190 crore RPS amount awaits NCLT capital reduction approval; order reserved, next hearing on May 15, 2026.
demand_pricing: L&D: enrollment volume up about 4%, but realisation down 12-14%. Students are shifting from ₹30,000-60,000 full programmes to ₹2,000-4,000 modular components.
MBA revenue expected flat to slightly down, with volumes rising. UG segments (law, BBA, IPM) are holding or raising prices, and growth is expected there.
Assessments: government contracts are about 40-45% of mix and private 55-60%. Pricing is similar across both and the market is price-sensitive.
Assessments: rollover of exam dates by 60-120 days shifted some FY26 revenue into FY27.
Competition: PhysicsWallah-type players are seen as low-price and not a direct threat; management launched products at about 50% above PhysicsWallah pricing and one-third of regular prices.

qa_highlights.question: Does the NEET controversy open opportunities for DEXIT in nationwide exams?
qa_highlights.answer: Yatrik Vin said it is a significant opportunity; DEXIT already conducts exams for IRDAI, ICAI and NISM, and its digital and surveillance tech is ready.

qa_highlights.question: What is the DEXIT government/private mix, contract duration, and government tender criteria?
qa_highlights.answer: Government is about 40-45% and private 55-60%. Contract tenure varies from one to five years, or order-based. RFPs weigh technical at 65-70% and commercial at 30-35%.

qa_highlights.question: How does the order book work, and why is it not 100% revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says 80-85% coverage is in hand for FY27, and sales efforts target a higher rollover. Exam timing set by clients can push revenue into the next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the fundraising plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Satya Narayanan said fundraising is on a slight pause given the environment, and the boards want value at the right valuation. Updates are expected in the next quarter or two.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the cash and current liabilities linked to NSE?
qa_highlights.answer: About ₹182 crore was left behind from the NSEIT transition and has earned ₹11-12 crore of interest, so about ₹193-194 crore is on the balance sheet. It will be knocked off against RPS after NCLT approval and moved from non-current to current liabilities.

qa_highlights.question: How will VIRSA affect MarTech in North America?
qa_highlights.answer: Pilots with Salesforce, Dell and Infosys have had positive feedback. The Salesforce work is for Canada, with a scale-up to the US expected over the next couple of quarters.

Assessment revenue timing depends on client exam schedules, which have rolled over by 60-120 days before.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Assessments revenue timing can slip 60-120 days when client exam dates roll over, as happened in FY26, and L&D pricing pressure from modular products is expected to persist for four to five quarters.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: A personalised-learning EdTech pilot launches in about one month, with roll-out to all programmes if successful, and Talevate targets 8-10 corporates and about 100 jobs, while VIRSA scales from Canada to the US over the next couple of quarters.

rows.label: Assessments FY27 order book at 80-85% of FY26 revenue
rows.why: Order cover of 80-85% of the ₹223 crore FY26 base supports management's expectation of reasonably healthy FY27 revenue growth, with all existing contracts rolled over and 20 new customers added.

rows.when: after NCLT approval, timing 'hopefully this year'
rows.why: Cash of about ₹94 crore plus ₹193-194 crore earmarked for RPS settlement would be knocked off after NCLT approval, but the approval hearing is still pending and the timeline is uncertain.

rows.label: Fundraising on slight pause
rows.when: next quarter or two at the earliest
rows.why: Management said fundraising is on a slight pause and boards want the right valuation, with updates only expected in the next quarter or two.

540403|2026-06.headline: CL Educate Q1 FY27: revenue fell about ₹17.5 crore QoQ-type decline offset by ₹18 crore cost cuts, lifting EBITDA margin ~218 bps to 16.6%, though still loss-making after tax.
540403|2026-06.overview: Management said Q1 revenue was weak, with a decline of about ₹17.5 crore on a full-quarter basis, but operational and overhead cost cuts of about ₹18 crore (₹9.3 crore service delivery, ₹8.7 crore fixed overheads) kept EBITDA marginally above Q1 FY26 and margin at about 16.6%. After-tax profit remained negative due to interest and depreciation. Test prep (EdTech L&D) revenue fell about 15% to ₹45 crore from ₹53 crore amid MBA market churn, while DEX digital assessments revenue fell about 17% on a base effect and ₹4.7 crore of deferred revenue. Management framed Q1 as the seasonally weakest quarter and guided to Q2 and Q3 recovery for MarTech and DEX.

financial_highlights.change: up about 218 bps YoY (call also cites ~340 bps in EdTech context)

financial_highlights.value: about ₹18 crore (₹9.3 crore service delivery + ₹8.7 crore fixed overheads)

financial_highlights.change: down ~15% from ₹53 crore; EBITDA down ~13%, margin up ~60 bps

segments.name: EdTech – Test Prep (L&D)
segments.commentary: Revenue down ~15% to about ₹45 crore from ₹53 crore; EBITDA down ~13% with margin up ~60 bps. Volume decline from market churn not offset by price; franchise mix rising.

segments.name: DEX – Digital Assessments
segments.commentary: Revenue down ~17% YoY; EBITDA down ~4.3%. Drivers: ~₹6 crore rollover exams in Q1 FY26 and ₹4.7 crore revenue pending customer result declarations, expected in Q2. Won nine contracts worth ~₹34 crore TCV, ~₹22 crore to execute this year.

segments.name: MarTech
segments.commentary: Revenue up ~₹7 crore (about 3.8%-7% cited); EBITDA up ~32-35%; margin up ~180 bps. Technology business ~10% of revenue last year, targeted at 13-15% this year. Q2 is largest season.

segments.name: EasyApply (platform monetisation)
segments.commentary: Adoption widened to most management institutes and exams except IIMs; new admission cycle started with 'extremely positive' traction in first 15 days. Q1 is seasonally slow.

guidance_outlook: Management expects significant change in parameters across Q2 and Q3 as seasonally heavy quarters for MarTech and DEX.
VIRSA revenue growth targeted at 45-50% for FY27.
Target to return to near-zero net debt within 36 months; strategic discussions with global and Indian players may surface in next two quarters.
Preference share redemption (DEX acquisition RPS) expected to complete within August 2026 after NCLT approval in July.
Overhead cost rationalisation to continue reflecting in Q2 and Q3 before tapering.
Management aims to expand EBITDA margin YoY on a quarterly basis; MarTech and DEX operate at 25-30% EBITDA margin per management.
capex_capacity: Depreciation rose ~28% after fixed-asset additions toward end of Q4 FY26.
DEX technology roadmap: 60-70% of FY27 technology projects complete (examination engine, cyber/IT security, network layer, node expansion).
BYOD (Bring Your Own Device) and on-device app-based testing being rolled out to expand DEX business modes.
Centralised monitoring (NOC/SOC plus a Mumbai surveillance layer) for remote proctoring at DEX.
demand_pricing: DEX pricing is per seat/candidate; 60-65% of DEX business is government tenders (techno-commercial, L1 pricing risk), 30-35% non-tender.
DEX revenue recognised per exam/contract, typically at exam conduct and/or results declaration; generally no advance payments.

Test prep: MBA segment in significant market churn; BBA/IPM described as growth segment; free online resources and AI adoption cited as headwinds. Franchise share rising, supporting average realisation.
MarTech pipeline described as robust for Q2 and Q3; VIRSA pilots with Salesforce, Dell and Infosys moving to scaled deployment; Singapore/US empanelment expected by end Q2 or early Q3 (90-150 days).
Management sees exam rationalisation and digitisation (CBT, multiple slots) as potential opportunities for DEX and consolidation across assessment and test prep over 1-2 years.

qa_highlights.question: How will exam rationalisation and the NTA/Nilekani task force affect DEX, and what is its near and medium term growth outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects exam digitisation and consolidation (possibly into SAT/GMAT/GRE-like exams) with some opportunities emerging and others disappearing; timing is 12-24 months and too early to quantify. Management sees enrolment growth of ~60% over nine years as expanding the addressable market.

qa_highlights.question: Could NTA build in-house proctoring software to mitigate malpractice, and how does DEX compare?
qa_highlights.answer: Management argued few players have DEX-level secure, AI-enabled, real-time remote proctoring with control-room monitoring, and sees tighter scrutiny as an opportunity for credible providers.

qa_highlights.question: How is BBA/IPM performing in test prep, and what is the impact of PhysicsWallah's AI content?
qa_highlights.answer: Gautam Puri said BBA/IPM is a growth segment with more five-year programmes, and that AI content generation has been in use for 1.5-2 years; PhysicsWallah targets the lower end while CL focuses on mid-to-upper segments.

qa_highlights.question: What is the debt reduction plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Target to be near net-zero debt within 36 months; scheduled repayments on track; acquisition loan reduced from ₹210 crore to ₹174 crore. Accelerated repayment possible if surplus cash arises, but MarTech and DEX need cash for expansion.

qa_highlights.question: How does DEX pricing work and how sensitive is it to price changes?
qa_highlights.answer: Pricing is per seat/candidate; over 60% of business is government tenders awarded on techno-commercial basis, where CL usually wins on technology (T1) but can lose on lowest price (L1).

qa_highlights.question: How is VIRSA progressing in Singapore and North America?
qa_highlights.answer: Pilots with Salesforce and Dell moved to recurring campaigns; Infosys scaling from pilot to multi-division in India; Singapore/US empanelment underway; pilots with Deloitte, PwC, Elastic and AWS; management targets 45-50% VIRSA revenue growth for FY27.

risks_watch: Q1 revenue decline of about ₹17.5 crore on a full-quarter basis; recovery depends on Q2 and Q3 delivery in MarTech and DEX, which management called the heavier quarters.
₹4.7 crore of DEX revenue pending customer results declaration, which management expects to resolve in Q2; any further slippage would hit Q2 DEX revenue.
Test prep: MBA volume churn not offset by pricing; management says churn is stabilising but gave no volume numbers; AI and free online resources cited as headwinds.
DEX government tender exposure of 60-65% of business, where L1 price can disqualify CL even when it wins on technology (T1).
Exam rationalisation and NTA/Nilekani task force outcomes are still unclear; management said it is too early to quantify and timing is 12-24 months.
Still loss-making after tax given interest and depreciation (D&A up about 28%); watch whether overhead savings flow through to PAT.
Preference share redemption tied to DEX acquisition expected by end August 2026; 36-month net-zero debt target depends on cash generation and possible strategic deals within two quarters.
VIRSA 45-50% FY27 growth target depends on Singapore/US empanelment (90-150 days, expected end Q2 or early Q3).
key_quotes: while the revenue has been a little bit of a challenge, a slight abnormality, because of operational optimization as well as the cost optimization, we were able to drive in an EBITDA which is marginally higher than the first quarter of last year

But Quarter One is usually our leanest and the weakest quarter for our DEXIT digital assessments as well as the MarTech business, and as we roll into Q2 and Q3, I think there will be a significant bit of change in almost all the parameters
it is too premature for us to say anything more than that, whether it happens in 12 months or 24 months, if three steps are taken in one go.
So at this stage there is nothing specific more than what we have outlined as a plan, that in the next 36 months we again wish to become a net zero debt company, and we are working towards that.
540403|2026-06.management_tone: Management was confident on cost control and on Q2/Q3 recovery, but openly described Q1 revenue as a challenge and gave few hard numbers on test prep volumes or the timing of the strategic discussions. It was evasive on the exact timing and scale of exam rationalisation, calling it too premature to quantify.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: EBITDA margin rose to about 16.6% (up ~218 bps YoY) on ~₹18 crore of cost cuts (₹9.3 crore service delivery, ₹8.7 crore overheads), and management said overhead rationalisation continues in Q2 and Q3 before tapering and aims to expand margin YoY each quarter; MarTech and DEX run at 25-30% EBITDA margin.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: DEX tech roadmap is 60-70% complete for FY27 (exam engine, cyber/IT security, network layer, node expansion) and BYOD/on-device testing is rolling out, but no new physical capacity number or size was given; D&A already up ~28% to ₹11.2 crore base from Q4 FY26 additions.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Q1 revenue fell about ₹17.5 crore on a full-quarter basis and test prep fell ~15% to ₹45 crore from ₹53 crore; recovery rests on MarTech (up ~₹7 crore) and DEX (nine contracts, ~₹34 crore TCV, ~₹22 crore to execute this year) plus ₹4.7 crore of DEX results pending for Q2, with no group growth figure given.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex was not discussed as a new programme; depreciation rose ~28% from Q4 FY26 additions and the company is targeting near-zero net debt within 36 months, with MarTech and DEX needing cash for expansion.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management guided VIRSA revenue growth of 45-50% for FY27 and MarTech tech share of 13-15% (from ~10%), but Singapore/US empanelment (90-150 days, end Q2 or early Q3) gates the VIRSA ramp and Q1 revenue was down ~₹17.5 crore.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: ₹4.7 crore of DEX revenue is pending results declaration expected in Q2, and 60-65% of DEX is government tender business where L1 price can disqualify CL; MBA volumes are still churning with no volume numbers given.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: BYOD and on-device app-based testing are being rolled out for DEX and EasyApply adoption widened to most institutes and exams with 'extremely positive' first-15-day traction, but no named product launch dates were given.

rows.label: Near-zero net debt within 36 months
rows.why: Acquisition loan cut from ₹210 crore to ₹174 crore and scheduled repayments are on track, though MarTech and DEX need cash for expansion, so accelerated paydown depends on surplus cash.

rows.label: DEX preference share redemption and possible strategic deal
rows.when: Aug 2026 (redemption); strategic talks within next two quart
rows.why: RPS redemption tied to the DEX acquisition is expected to complete in August 2026 after NCLT approval in July, and management said strategic discussions with global and Indian players may surface in the next two quarters.

rows.label: Exam rationalisation and digitisation (NTA/Nilekani)
rows.why: Management sees CBT and multi-slot digitisation as an opportunity for DEX, but said it is too early to quantify and enrolment growth of ~60% over nine years is the addressable-market argument.

tone.note: Management was confident on cost control, margin trajectory and the Q2/Q3 MarTech and DEX recovery, but was cautious on Q1 revenue and gave no test prep volume numbers or timing on exam rationalisation; analysts pressed on DEX pricing under L1 tender rules, MBA churn and exam rationalisation impact.

540403|2026-09.headline: CL Educate H1 FY27 EBITDA rose to ~₹57 crore (margin ~18.6% vs 15.7%) on 4% revenue decline to ₹305 crore, with PAT back positive.
540403|2026-09.overview: H1 FY27 revenue fell about 4% to ₹305 crore from ₹319 crore, driven by EdTech (down ~13%) and DEXIT base effects from rollover contracts in Q1 FY26. Cost actions cut overheads by about ₹12.5 crore, lifting EBITDA from ~₹50 crore to ~₹57 crore and margin about 3 percentage points, with PAT returning to positive (up ~350%). Management flagged ~₹172 crore of new multi-year DEXIT contract wins, of which ~₹40 crore accrues in FY27, and a pending DEXIT merger into CL Educate. Overall tone was upbeat on H2 but the call gave few hard forward numbers.

segments.name: EdTech (Learning & Development)
segments.commentary: Revenue down ~13% on test prep market flattening; EBITDA up ~8% with margin about 21-22% vs 17%, helped by overhead cuts and a shift toward franchise/network channels with higher ARPU. CL Media (platform monetisation) flat in H1, with admission-cycle seasonality shifting to start in October.

segments.name: DEXIT (Digital Assessments)
segments.commentary: Revenue down ~8% (about ₹10-11 crore), mainly due to Q1 FY26 rollover contracts not recurring; Q2 roughly flat vs Q1. EBITDA down ~2% in absolute terms with margin up ~171 bps. New wins include IIT GATE (shared with an existing vendor), GPSC, Bihar Civil Services, Edsel; IIBF and DGFMS renewed for 2-3 years.

segments.name: MarTech (Kestone/VOSMOS/VIRSA)
segments.commentary: Revenue up ~14% and EBITDA up ~26-27%; international about 40%, India about 60% of revenue. Large Dell events; Infosys signed for a global implementation; talks with other IT majors over the next 6-12 months.

guidance_outlook: Overhead savings of about ₹20-22 crore expected in the current fiscal year, with the H2 contribution tempered versus H1's ₹12.5 crore.
Management expects H2 FY27 numbers to look significantly better than H2 FY26, with a significant portion of the ~₹40 crore FY27 DEXIT contract accrual landing in H2.
CL Media expected to have a solid H2 with significant revenue growth and a reasonably positive EBITDA margin.
EdTech revenue expected to stay around current levels for about one more year, with margin flat to slightly up.
Merger tax savings estimated at ₹11-15 crore annually for three years, plus ₹3-5 crore annual admin/overhead savings.
Long-term debt repayment expected at ₹24-30 crore a year absent equity raise or other events; ₹100 crore NCD refinancing to complete in 4-6 weeks.
DEXIT merger via NCLT expected to complete by roughly September-October 2027 (9-15 month estimate), with timing uncertain.
capex_capacity: Management is increasing capacity to qualify for NEET and other exams; NEET moving to CBT mode announced by government, with the expert committee blueprint expected around January 2027.
mySathi: about 15,000 tests executed to date; target 25,000 students over next 4-5 months and 35,000-40,000 by year-end.
Registered office shifted to Mumbai (INC-22 approved); DEXIT merger scheme approved by both boards, NCLT filing expected this month.
₹203 crore DEXIT redeemable preference shares redeemed in mid-August after NCLT approval in July, trimming balance sheet by over ₹200 crore.
demand_pricing: Test prep market flattening across segments, affecting most test prep players including those outside CL's segments.
DEXIT exam pricing ranges from about ₹150 to ₹1,200 per student depending on services and sessions; ~80 lakh exams done last year on ~₹230 crore revenue (about ₹300 per exam on average).
IIT GATE sees 8-10 lakh students a year; DEXIT empanelled for the first time, sharing orders with an existing vendor.
Offline assessments market cited at ~₹2,500 crore in 2023 growing ~8% CAGR, with a projection of ~₹3,500 crore in a couple of years.
Pilots planned with 3-5 corporates in BFSI/IT over 3-6 months for corporate internal exams.

qa_highlights.question: Update on mySathi and its scale?
qa_highlights.answer: Gautam Puri said it is in pilot and expected to launch fully in the coming season; Nikhil Mahajan said ~15,000 tests done with 35,000-40,000 students targeted by year-end.

qa_highlights.question: Tax and other savings from the DEXIT merger, timeline, and route?
qa_highlights.answer: Management chose the NCLT route over fast-track; estimated 9-15 months at Bombay NCLT. Tax savings ₹11-15 crore annually and other overhead savings ₹3-5 crore annually.

qa_highlights.question: Yatrik Vin's status and succession at DEXIT?
qa_highlights.answer: Gautam Puri said Yatrik Vin resigned from the CL Educate board for health reasons but remains DEXIT chairperson; succession exists but he is expected to stay for the next three to six months.

qa_highlights.question: DEXIT contract duration and right of refusal?
qa_highlights.answer: Harshit Maniar said contracts typically run 2-3 years; some are reverse e-auctions where DEXIT can match the lowest price, others are fixed-price bids that cannot be revised.

qa_highlights.question: Capital raise at DEXIT level and DEXIT IPO?
qa_highlights.answer: Nikhil Mahajan said options remain open until the merger takes effect (12-15 months); an IPO is unlikely if the merger proceeds, but an equity offer could change the course.

qa_highlights.question: NEET CBT shift and DEXIT's revenue opportunity?
qa_highlights.answer: Gautam Puri said NEET (about 20 lakh students) moves to CBT and will likely be split among multiple vendors; Harshit Maniar said the committee sought inputs and the report is expected around January 2027.

qa_highlights.question: UG vs PG mix and when revenue and margins stabilise?
qa_highlights.answer: Gautam Puri said UG and PG are about 50-50 now, with UG expected to grow; revenues likely flat around current levels for about a year, then rising, with margins steady or slightly up.

qa_highlights.question: Debt outlook for the next two years?
qa_highlights.answer: Arjun Wadhwa said annual repayments are ₹24-30 crore, long-term acquisition debt about ₹174 crore and working capital about ₹55-60 crore at 30 September; the company aims to become net debt-free.

risks_watch: EdTech top-line decline (~13%) from test prep market flattening; revenue guided flat for about a year.
DEXIT H1 revenue decline and reliance on new contract ramp-up (₹172 crore wins, ~₹40 crore in FY27).
NEET CBT award split and timing depend on the expert committee report (expected January 2027).
NCLT timing for DEXIT merger is uncertain (9-15 months; some cases 15-18 months).
Refinancing of ₹100 crore acquisition loans via listed NCDs to complete in 4-6 weeks.
Yatrik Vin's health and succession at DEXIT.
Overhead savings tapering in H2 relative to H1.
540403|2026-09.management_tone: Confident on margins and H2 recovery, with specific figures on savings and contract wins. Cautious and deliberately non-committal on NEET volumes, merger timing, DEXIT capital options and the Yatrik Vin succession, deferring several questions to later updates.
key_quotes: As you can see, our EBITDA margin has expanded by about 3 percentage points from the same time last year.
The total multi-year contract wins, as we speak, aggregate to about ₹ 172 crores, which will get delivered over the next two to three years.
But on an overall basis, I think we should be able to reflect total cost savings of around ₹ 20 to 22 crores on overheads during the current fiscal year, during the remaining part of H2.
We have expressed in the past our desire to be a net debt -free company as soon as possible, and we continue to work towards that.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: H1 FY27 EBITDA margin rose to ~18.6% from 15.7% on ~₹12.5 crore overhead cuts, with ₹20-22 crore full-year FY27 savings guided (implying ~₹7.5-9.5 crore in H2) and EdTech margin guided flat to slightly up.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.when: NEET CBT ramp, around Jan 2027 onward
rows.why: Capacity is being increased to qualify for NEET and other exams with no size given, and mySathi targets 35,000-40,000 students by year-end from ~15,000 tests done, so capacity adds are planned but unquantified.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: DEXIT H2 revenue guided above prior-year H2 on ~₹40 crore of the ₹172 crore new contracts accruing in FY27, but EdTech revenue is flat for about a year after a ~13% decline.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex is not discussed, and the company is prioritising deleveraging (₹24-30 crore annual repayments, ₹203 crore preference shares redeemed) and the DEXIT merger over new plants.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management gave no firm revenue number and EdTech is guided flat, so there is no sign of a raise beyond the ₹20-22 crore overhead savings target.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Overhead savings taper in H2 (₹7.5-9.5 crore implied vs ₹12.5 crore in H1), NEET award timing depends on the January 2027 committee report, and NCLT timing is uncertain at 9-15 months.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: mySathi is in pilot and expected to launch fully in the coming season, with 35,000-40,000 students targeted by year-end, though no launch date was firmly committed.

rows.label: DEXIT ₹172 cr new multi-year contract wins
rows.why: About ₹40 crore of the ₹172 crore wins accrues in FY27, with a significant portion landing in H2, though the contracts are 2-3 years and some are reverse e-auctions.

rows.label: DEXIT merger into CL Educate via NCLT
rows.why: Scheme approved by both boards with NCLT filing expected this month, and tax savings of ₹11-15 crore a year plus ₹3-5 crore overhead savings are estimated, though timing is uncertain at 9-15 months.

rows.label: Net debt-free aspiration
rows.why: Long-term acquisition debt is ~₹174 crore and working capital ~₹55-60 crore at 30 Sep, with ₹24-30 crore annual repayments, so net debt-free status is a multi-year aim with no date set.

tone.note: Management was confident on margins, overhead savings and the H2 DEXIT recovery, but cautious and non-committal on NEET volumes, merger timing, DEXIT capital options and the Yatrik Vin succession; analysts probed these areas.

540404|2026-06.headline: Prime Fresh Q1 FY27 revenue rose 15.7% to INR81.71 crore and EBITDA jumped 51% to INR6 crore (9.83% margin), which management says is not fully sustainable.
540404|2026-06.overview: Prime Fresh reported Q1 FY27 sales of INR81.71 crore (vs INR53.34 crore), EBITDA of INR6 crore (9.83% margin vs 7.53%) and PAT of INR4.35 crore (vs INR2.89 crore). Management attributed part of the jump to one-off recoveries of pending service-business billings, inventory gains from rising F&V and onion prices, and strong service volumes, and guided that margins may not be sustained. Forward guidance is EBITDA margin of 7% to 7.5% and volume growth of 15% to 25%, with value growth of 25% to 30%. The company is pursuing the Nashik cluster development project under the National Horticulture Board, expected to be awarded in August 2026, and a Bank of Baroda working capital limit increase to INR20 crore.

financial_highlights.metric: Bank of Baroda cash credit limit
financial_highlights.change: Raised from INR7.8 crore at 8.5% cost

segments.name: F&V business (B2B)
segments.commentary: Management stated FY23 sales of about INR275 crore, of which about INR245 crore plus came from F&V and the balance from service business. B2C is 1% to 2% of business; exports stopped post-COVID.

segments.name: Service business
segments.commentary: Q1 saw good volume growth and strong margins, plus recovery of old pending billings that aided the quarter. Management said this contribution is not expected to recur at the same level.

segments.name: Subsidiaries
segments.commentary: Florens Farming Ltd is the key focus for own farming and land tie-ups; management said it contributes about 10% of F&V and could pay off from next year. Prime Fresh Retail India Pvt Ltd is held for strategic partners; B2C entry deferred.

guidance_outlook: EBITDA margin guidance of 7% to 7.5%; net profit margin guidance stated as 5.5% to 5% (as transcribed, likely a typo).
Volume growth of 15% to 20% minimum in one answer and 15% to 25% in closing remarks; value growth of 25% to 30%.
Internal aspiration of 9.5% to 11% EBITDA margin in 2 to 2.5 years (around 2029) and a vision of INR2,000 crore revenue by 2031; longer-term EBITDA margin of 14% to 16% in 4 to 5 years.
Operating margin expected to rise slowly from mid-FY28.
Debtor target of 88 to 94 days of sales, debtors below 25% of sales, and no single rupee of working capital or equity needed for an incremental INR60 crore sale by FY29.
Product portfolio to add three to four more categories within a year (currently 9 to 12 F&V products).
capex_capacity: Nashik (Sinnar) cluster development programme under National Horticulture Board: company as implementing agency; expected award in August 2026; INR75 crore investment (excluding INR5-6 crore preoperative spend), of which INR50-52 crore eligible for 40-50% grant (about INR24 crore grant expected on milestones).
Capex to start around end-October to end-November 2026 over 18 to 20 months; Phase 1 INR6-9 crore, Phase 2 INR12-15 crore, balance in Phase 3, funded from own balance sheet including debt.
Project debt peak about INR35 crore against INR42 crore sanctioned, falling to INR18-20 crore after grants.
Farmer component of about INR60 crore with around 35% government subsidy; target of 15,000 farmers and 15,000 tons incremental sourcing in year 1, scaling to 2 lakh tons in six years.
Sourcing capacity close to 2.5 lakh tons vs FY sales of about 65,000 tons.
demand_pricing: Customer mix: about 20 large modern trade and e-commerce accounts, around 90 APMC partners, 10 to 15 food processors, 20 to 30 exporters; added four to five food processing customers in Q1.
Price pass-through of 4 to 8 days on procurement changes for most business; HoReCa about one month; 5-star and tender business up to 3 months, which is under 4% of business.
Pomegranate: about 13,000 farmers and 40 plus local area aggregators; onion prices rising sharply, benefiting inventory gains.
Procurement advantage of direct farm sourcing stated at 3% to 15% on price, with 10% to 15% operational cost initially; long-term advantage 5% to 8% over supplier purchase.
Company is positioned as a pan-India supplier to modern trade and e-commerce across 10 cities for onion, pomegranate and orange.

qa_highlights.question: Can receivables (about one-third of revenue) be reduced and can trade payables be extended?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a client credit exposure system, stricter onboarding with PDCs and security cheques, and about INR12 crore debtor reduction in Q1. It aims at 88-94 debtor days and a 25% of sales cap; a BoB limit rise to INR20 crore plus INR20 crore for Nashik was cited; payables to farmers are expected to rise to INR10-15 crore on credit by FY28.

qa_highlights.question: What does the Nashik Sinnar project add beyond the asset-light model?
qa_highlights.answer: Prime Fresh is implementing agency for a farmer component (subsidy-led) and an IA component of INR75 crore with 40-50% grant on eligible capex; it aims at order-book model, farm-gate packhouse and cold chain, and a separate call was offered.

qa_highlights.question: Cumulative capex, revenue/tonnage and margin impact, and replication to other cities?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex over about 18-20 months with phased balance-sheet spend; quantified margin uplift not given. Replication via subsidiary or SPV route is open, with full equity payback in up to 5 years targeted.

qa_highlights.question: Lag between procurement price changes and customer price resets?
qa_highlights.answer: Typically 4 to 8 days; HoReCa up to one month; tender business up to three months, under 4% of business.

qa_highlights.question: Why were Q1 trading and direct expenses up faster than revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not have the numbers and said it would respond by mail.

qa_highlights.question: Why not enter B2C given the city footprint?
qa_highlights.answer: B2C needs heavy upfront investment; an earlier franchise attempt cost INR55-75 lakh in 2021-2023. Management decided not to pursue it now, with B2C at 1-2% of business.

540497|2026-03.headline: S Chand FY26 EBITDA hit Rs1,449m (18.1% margin) with net cash Rs1,048m; FY27 revenue growth guided at 10-15%, margin at 17-19%.
540497|2026-03.overview: FY26 revenue came in at the guided Rs8,000m, with gross margin held near 68% despite a 6% GST hike on paper. EBITDA rose to Rs1,449m (18.1% margin, within the 18-20% guidance) and PAT grew 21% to Rs731m. Operating cash flow was Rs747m, below the ~Rs1,000m five-year average, because receivables (160 days) and inventory (232 days) rose. Management guided FY27 operating revenue growth of 10-15%, EBITDA margin of 17-19% (1pp below FY26), and OCF above Rs1,000m.

Old and new syllabus books were adopted in FY26, and new series (Mylestone, My Zen, SmartK, Solid Steps) are in over 1,500 schools.

segments.name: International (CPD Singapore)
segments.commentary: Acquired January 2026; supplementary books for Singapore/IGCSE/IB curricula. Last-year revenue was about USD0.5m (Rs5-6 crore), with sales only in Singapore and Malaysia. Management expects roughly Rs5-7 crore of capex over 2-3 years and a 1-2 year build-up in India.

qa_highlights.question: Is the FY27 10-15% growth guidance inclusive of any NCF upside, and how big can AI licensing become?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 10-15% is a sound guidance on a large base, with growth volume-driven. AI licensing targets Rs100 crore over time; it is a mix of one-time (about 30%) and term licences (about 70%). Management said it would not give margins due to client confidentiality, though in-house content is near 90% margin.

qa_highlights.question: Why is there no buyback despite a strong net cash position and low valuation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said a buyback is under consideration and the Board will decide later. It is waiting for the war-related uncertainty to ease and for paper and consumables prices to settle. FY27 year-end net cash is expected at about Rs130-135m.

qa_highlights.question: Can margins return to 25%?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said the company now prioritises cash conversion over margin. Operating cash flow was Rs800m-era levels of Rs38m in the past versus Rs75m this year, and the company wants working capital efficiency and not revenue growth that does not convert into cash.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Rs400m+ licensing revenue be from in-house or sourced content?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects roughly 60% in-house and 40% sourced, based on the current pipeline. The target is per SKU or title licensed, not per user.

qa_highlights.question: Why are the entities kept separate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said each acquired brand has its own sales team and school relationships, which lets the group capture more of each child's book bag. Consolidation would risk losing market share.

540497|2026-06.headline: S Chand Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 12% YoY to Rs1,145m, but EBITDA loss of Rs97m and PAT loss of Rs187m widened the reported loss.
540497|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue was Rs1,145m, up 12% YoY, with gross margin improved. EBITDA turned to a loss of Rs97m and PAT to a loss of Rs187m, hit by marketing costs pulled into Q1 from Q2 and a one-time tax rate adjustment. Management pre-bought paper ahead of expected price rises, lifting inventory and slightly raising net working capital days. Net cash reached a record Rs1,182m after Rs141m dividend, and FY27 guidance of 10-15% operating revenue growth and 17-19% EBITDA margin was reiterated.

540530|2026-06.headline: HUDCO guides FY27 disbursement of about INR65,000 crore and a INR3 lakh crore loan book by 2029-30, with spreads held near 2%.
540530|2026-06.overview: Management skipped the headline numbers and focused on policy tailwinds (urban challenge fund, bankable projects) and the pipeline. FY27 disbursement target is about INR65,000 crore against about INR5,000 crore achieved last year, with borrowing plan of about INR70,000 crore approved. Two June MoUs (Gujarat and Bihar, each above INR1 lakh crore) were presented as pipeline, with sanctions expected to start this quarter. Management reiterated a spread of around 2% and NIM of around 3%, though an analyst cited Q1 spread near 1.8%, and said compression is due to fast growth and should reverse by Q3.

financial_highlights.value: about INR20,000 crore; INR4,000 crore+ received in Q1

Management said water and sanitation are the core sustainable-finance focus, aligned with AMRUT and MoHUA priorities.

segments.name: Housing
segments.commentary: Housing portfolio is shrinking because states are not bringing counterpart funding under PMAY; housing lending is priced around MCLR of about 8.6%.

segments.name: Private sector / PPP project finance
segments.commentary: New PPP project finance division; 2 projects sanctioned in Q1 worth about INR6,000-7,000 crore. Disbursement expected to start in the latter part of FY27. No internal target set.

Loan book target of INR3 lakh crore by 2030 (FY30); FY28 not planned, with mid-FY28 review and market disclosure if course correction needed.
Spread to be maintained around 2% and NIM around 3%; spread expected to reflect in Q3 as Q4 FY26 and Q1 FY27 disbursements capitalise.

Gujarat and Bihar MoUs (each above INR1 lakh crore; combined about INR2 lakh crore): sanctions to start in Q2 FY27 for Gujarat, with works in Q4 FY27 or earlier; MoUs valid 5 years, disbursement over around 5 years.

FX borrowing: RBI forex window tie-up of about USD2 billion (about USD700 million drawn), all-in cost about 5.5-6.5% including hedging, with ECB share possibly rising from about 10% to 20% of borrowings.
capex_capacity: Gujarat MoU: metro, RRTS, Olympic/Commonwealth Games infrastructure (Commonwealth Games Ahmedabad 2030), highways; sanctions expected this quarter.
Bihar MoU: 12 satellite towns; Bihar road projects of about INR21,000 crore identified; tourism, metro and digital parks under discussion.
Repayments of INR15,000-16,000 crore expected over remaining quarters of FY27.
demand_pricing: Analyst cited Q1 spread near 1.8%; management attributed compression to accelerated growth and expects 2% spread to return by Q3.
Competition for state financing from NABARD, NaBFID and commercial banks has pushed rates down, per management.

qa_highlights.answer: Finance director said no FCNRs maturing in FY27 or FY28 except USD200 million maturing in 2028, which is secured; no forex losses foreseen this year. Gujarat sanctions expected this quarter; Bihar has 12 satellite towns and road projects.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 disbursement and repayment outlook?

qa_highlights.question: What is the forex window borrowing size and cost?

risks_watch: Spread: Q1 spread near 1.8% per analyst vs 2% guidance; watch Q2 and Q3 for recovery as higher-yield disbursements capitalise.

Tax rate change from no DTL on special reserve (effective rate about 20.6%) affects comparability.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade

rows.why: Two June MoUs total about INR2 lakh crore (each above INR1 lakh crore), with management guiding Gujarat sanctions to start in Q2 FY27, though land, political and state-compliance delays could slow conversion.

rows.label: PPP / private sector project finance division
rows.why: Two PPP projects sanctioned in Q1 worth about INR6,000-7,000 crore, with disbursement expected to start in the latter part of FY27 and no internal target set.

rows.label: FY27 repayments
rows.why: Repayments guided at about INR20,000 crore for FY27, with INR4,000 crore+ received in Q1 and INR15,000-16,000 crore expected over the rest of the year.

540530|2026-09.headline: HUDCO H1 FY27: disbursements above INR35,000 crore (up ~37%), loan book up 29% to INR1.86 lakh crore, net NPA 0.04%.
540530|2026-09.overview: Management reported strong H1 FY27 growth: disbursements above INR35,000 crore, sanctions above INR1 lakh crore, and loan book up 29% to INR1.86 lakh crore. Net profit rose 31% and revenue from operations rose 26% on a half-yearly basis, with gross NPA around 0.7% and net NPA 0.04%. Management said spreads are about 1.96% (ex the INR20,000 crore low-yield GoI loan) with NIM about 2.93%, and reiterated 2% spread and 3% NIM targets, while flagging near-term repricing pressure from higher borrowing costs. The call also covered first PPP sanctions (about INR9,000 crore, Dharavi redevelopment yet to disburse) and RBI Upper Layer NBFC classification.

segments.name: Lending - sovereign / GoI loan
segments.commentary: INR20,000 crore loan to Government of India carries about 40 bps spread; repayment expected in FY2028-29, after which spread and NIM are expected to rise to about 2% and 3%.

segments.name: PPP / private lending
segments.commentary: About INR9,000 crore of PPP sanctions (slum redevelopment incl. Dharavi, HAM road projects, one renewable energy project); no PPP disbursement yet except Dharavi, expected to start in Q3.

segments.name: PMAY / housing
segments.commentary: Cumulative PMAY 1 and 2 sanctions about INR58,000 crore, releases about INR48,000 crore; state counterpart funding demand is uncertain as states prefer SDLs.

guidance_outlook: FY27 internal disbursement target INR65,000 crore; about INR30,000 crore remaining after H1.
FY27 loan book target about INR2 lakh crore; FY30 target INR3 lakh crore retained (management did not indicate a revision).
Spread targeted at about 2% and NIM at least 3% on a year-to-year basis, with possible temporary slippage from resets and market moves.
ROA targeted at 2% to 2.2%.
Negative credit costs (reversals) expected for a year or two given provision coverage around 95%.
About INR35,000 crore of ECB borrowing at around 6.5%-6.75% expected before the RBI swap window closes on 31 December; targeting slightly more than $3 billion under the window.
15 bps MCLR increase and ECB impact expected to reflect in Q3 FY27 results; about INR20,000 crore of loans to reset in H1.
capex_capacity: Around 1 lakh square metres of space to be created in next three years for asset monetisation; income expected from it.
Strategic business group being set up; regional offices being strengthened for post-sanction monitoring.
Sanctioned PPP pipeline long gestation (3 to 5 years), so disbursement conversion will be slow.
Overall sanctioned pipeline estimated at INR3 lakh crore to INR4 lakh crore; about INR1 lakh crore sanctioned each half-year.
demand_pricing: Management expects urban infrastructure demand to be large (World Bank estimate about INR250 lakh crore requirement by 2050, as cited).
Loan repricing on tranche-wise one-year reset tied to quarterly-revised MCLR; some states moving to quarterly reset.
Management said borrowers will pass higher costs through at reset; yields expected to rise over next two quarters.
Bond yields around 8% over last two to two and a half months; Q1 FY27 bonds of about INR2,200 crore raised at roughly 7%-7.25%; bank funding around 7.25%; no bond issuance in Q2.
PMAY 2 sanctions around 20 lakh units; government target 40 lakh units this year.

qa_highlights.question: How will yields and margins hold up over next one to two years as growth continues?
qa_highlights.answer: Management assured about 2% spread at year-end and NIM at least 3%, with temporary slippage possible from resets and disbursement timing; current spread 1.96% and NIM 2.93% including the INR20,000 crore low-yield GoI loan.

qa_highlights.question: Will the currency translation losses continue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FX translation loss is zero this quarter and no losses foreseen; ECB maturities about five years and new FX exposure covered under RBI swap window; small FCNR portion maturing 2028 hedged.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 disbursement target?
qa_highlights.answer: Internal target INR65,000 crore; INR35,000 crore done in H1, INR30,000 crore remaining; target to be revised only if project pace accelerates.

qa_highlights.question: How are PPP sanctions and pipeline progressing; cost of borrowing by source?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR9,000 crore PPP sanctioned with Dharavi disbursement expected this quarter; sanction pipeline INR3-4 lakh crore. ECB blended cost about 6.75% after hedging on $2 billion raised; bonds about 8% currently; banks about 7.25%.

qa_highlights.question: What gives confidence in maintaining 2% spread given no relief in cost of funds?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited RBI swap window borrowings at about 6.5%-6.75%, INR20,000 crore resets in H1, 15 bps MCLR hike, and moves to quarterly resets; said yields will rise over next two quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of RBI Upper Layer classification?
qa_highlights.answer: Mainly additional compliance; exposure norms of 25% and 5% (board approval) are not a constraint given loan book size; no material impact expected.

qa_highlights.question: Guidance on ROA and credit costs?
qa_highlights.answer: ROA targeted at 2%-2.2%; negative credit costs likely for one to two years due to reversals with 95% provision coverage.

risks_watch: Spread compression risk: cost of funds elevated (bonds around 8%) and repricing lag; management expects margin recovery after FY28-29 GoI loan runs off.
Dependence on RBI swap window for cheaper ECB funding; about INR35,000 crore intended before 31 December.
Recovery of about INR1,200 crore in stressed assets under NCLT/DRAT, mostly private sector; timing uncertain.
PPP lending: risk premium rising, limited disbursement so far, state counterpart funding under PMAY uncertain.
Compliance requirements under RBI Upper Layer NBFC classification.
Negative credit cost may be unsustainable beyond one to two years; watch reversal pace.
540530|2026-09.management_tone: Confident on growth, asset quality and spread targets, but cautious on cost of funds and repricing; several answers were hedged ("temporary slowdown" possible) and key numbers such as revenue and profit growth were stated as percentages without absolute values.

rows.why: Management did not indicate revising the FY27 INR65,000 crore disbursement or INR2 lakh crore loan book targets; revision only if project pace accelerates.

rows.why: First PPP disbursement (Dharavi) expected in Q3 from about INR9,000 crore of PPP sanctions, but no new product launch was specifically guided.

rows.why: About INR35,000 crore of ECB at about 6.5%-6.75% is expected before the window closes, targeting slightly above $3 billion, which should cap funding costs.

540544|2026-03.headline: PSP Projects Q4FY26 revenue rose 66% YoY to INR1,115 crores, but a INR29 crore Kashi ECL provision kept FY26 PAT flat at INR55 crores.
540544|2026-03.overview: Q4FY26 was the company's highest-ever quarterly revenue at INR1,115 crores (up 66% YoY), with EBITDA up 85% to INR60 crores and PAT up to INR21 crores. Reported margins were depressed by a INR29 crore expected credit loss provision on unbilled revenue from the Kashi project, which took other expenses from INR17 crores to INR46 crores. For FY26, revenue grew 25% to INR3,149 crores, EBITDA rose 5% to INR189 crores with margin down to 6% from 7.14%, and PAT was flat-to-down at INR55 crores. Order book reached INR13,447 crores (up 85%) after record order inflow of INR10,925 crores, 85% of it from the Adani group.

segments.name: Adani group (in-house) orders
segments.commentary: Adani group accounted for 85% of FY26 order inflow and about INR9,000 crores (67%) of the current INR13,400 crore order book. Management says materials are pass-through on Adani contracts.

segments.name: External / non-group orders
segments.commentary: External projects are about 33-43% of the order book (about INR4,300 crores per the Q&A). Government projects fell to about 25% of the order book from 43% a year earlier.

segments.name: Precast manufacturing
segments.commentary: Current precast capacity is 3 million sq ft per year. Management says expansion to 1.5x would need only INR15-20 crores of equipment since sheds are already built. Project 90 was pre-executed in 148 days.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guidance is about INR4,500 crores, reiterated by management.
FY27 EBITDA margin guided at 7-8%, with management saying it can move 1% plus or minus; the Q&A confirmed 7-8% as the band for the next two years.
Management expects to be debt-free within about two to three quarters, with interest cost of about INR11-12 crores per quarter falling toward nil.
Working capital: trade receivable days are expected to fall to about 60 days (60-70 days per the Q&A) from about 94 days.

Order inflow is expected at INR5,000-6,000 crores from the group plus INR1,000-2,000 crores from outside in FY27. The bid pipeline is about INR6,500 crores, of which about INR5,000 crores is group and INR1,500 crores external.
Capex for FY27 is expected at about INR120-150 crores (roughly 2-4% of revenue), with quarterly lumpiness possible.
Employee cost is expected to grow about 2-4% (per the Q&A), with operating leverage as revenue rises.
Medium-term goal is 20-25% growth per year, with a target of about INR9,000-10,000 crores revenue by FY30 (per the analyst's recap, not restated by management).
capex_capacity: FY26 capex was INR192 crores; Q4FY26 capex was INR40 crores. Gross block is INR764 crores and net block INR412 crores.
Precast plant capacity is 3 million sq ft per year; management sees no major expansion needed at the current pace.
Projects under execution: 94 ongoing across Gujarat, UP, Rajasthan, Karnataka, Maharashtra and Delhi NCR; over 256 completed to date.

Mumbai projects (Mahim, Matunga) are at early foundation stage; Matunga is at sheet piling. Tree-cutting approvals are a delay risk. Management says about INR10,000 crores of the order book is at peak execution pace.
Dharoi Dam Phase 1 was handed over and Phase 2 is in finishing. SMC RCC is complete and RVNL core and shell is complete.
demand_pricing: Order book INR13,447 crores (+85% YoY), with group projects at 67% and external at 43% per the CEO's figures (these overlap; the Q&A split is 67% Adani and 33% non-Adani).
Record FY26 order inflow of INR10,925 crores, 85% from Adani group. Major wins include SVPI Airport Ahmedabad development, Matunga Rehab Building Mumbai, and Shri Ambaji Mata Temple extension.

Key outstanding orders: Shree Ambaji Mata Temple INR966 crores, SMC Highrise INR731 crores, Human & Biological Science Gallery INR254 crores, GIFT City Fintech Building INR261 crores, Dharoi Dam INR223 crores, Gati Shakti Vishwavidyalaya INR216 crores, Sabarmati Riverfront Phase II INR218 crores, GIFT City residential INR210 crores.

Commonwealth Games-linked tenders (about INR7,000-8,000 crores potential, per analyst) are expected to be announced but had not been formally released; management expects them 'anytime in this quarter'.
Mobilisation advances of INR814 crores from the group are interest-free. Management says the group advance will fund most working capital.

qa_highlights.question: Is FY27 revenue guidance of INR4,500 crores and FY30 target of INR9,000-10,000 crores changed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management stuck to INR4,500 crores for FY27 and said margins are improving; Q4 EBITDA margin excluding the INR30 crore provision would be about 8%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Kashi ECL provision and will more come?
qa_highlights.answer: The INR29 crore provision was made because receivables beyond one year must be provided for. Management is still chasing the UP Medical College accounts through government channels and does not expect major further ECL provisions.

qa_highlights.question: How much UP Medical College money is outstanding?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR60 crores unbilled and INR40 crores trade receivable across seven projects. INR40 crores of GST invoices are pending, and final certification is awaited.

qa_highlights.question: Will PAT margin reach 4-5%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects to be debt-free within about two to three quarters, which would remove about INR41-45 crores of annual interest. It said PAT margin could reach 3-4% and that 4.5-5% is the target for next year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the working capital outlook and receivable days?
qa_highlights.answer: Receivable days were about 90-100 at March 2026 because most revenue was booked in February and March. Management expects them to fall to around 60-70 days, with collection in April.

qa_highlights.question: Is capex/depreciation going to stay at 3% of revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY27 capex is about INR120-150 crores, with possible flexibility to about 2% of revenue. Depreciation is expected to keep rising from new assets, so it cannot be cut.

qa_highlights.question: What is the SDB receivable status?
qa_highlights.answer: The client has just started operations. About INR90 crores of principal is in receivables, with interest billed separately. Management expects resolution during FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Does the Adani mix or the ongoing war pressure margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said most orders are Adani with pass-through materials, so it sees no major war-related margin risk. Only SMC and RVNL may see small impact.

risks_watch: Receivables jumped to INR928 crores (about 90-100 days) at March 2026; watch April-June collections against management's 60-70 day target.
Collection risk on UP Medical College (about INR60 crores unbilled and INR40 crores receivable) and the remaining Kashi and SDB balances. Further ECL provisions are possible.
Margin guidance (7-8%) depends on no further provisions. Q4 margin was depressed by the INR29 crore provision, and FY26 EBITDA margin fell to 6%.
Concentration risk: about 67% of the order book is Adani group. Mobilisation advances of INR814 crores are a funding source; a slowdown in group inflows would matter.
Execution risk in Mumbai (tree-cutting approvals, monsoon, labour availability in Q1-Q2 FY27), and the timing of Commonwealth-linked tenders.
Debt-free target and interest saving depend on collections; gross debt of about INR317 crores (INR43 crores long-term plus INR274 crores short-term) remains.

Management repeatedly framed the 7-8% margin band as conservative and pointed to group advances and pass-through terms as mitigants.

So we don't see any risk related to war to bring the bad impact on the overall guidelines otherwise.
I think it should be nil, so I'm expecting the company should be debt-free by this year or maybe in next two quarters.

540544|2026-06.headline: PSP Projects Q1 FY27 revenue rose 65% YoY to INR853 crores, with order book at INR13,245 crores (up 103% YoY) and EBITDA margin of 6.42%.
540544|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 65% YoY to INR853 crores and EBITDA rose 121% to INR55 crores, with margin expanding to 6.42% from 4.79%. Net profit reached INR18 crores versus INR37 lakhs a year earlier. Management attributed the margin shortfall versus its 7-8% target to weak April-May billing against labour-heavy costs, with employee cost at 5.4% of sales. Management reiterated FY27 revenue of INR4,400-4,500 crores and a 7-8% EBITDA margin for the full year, with the bulk of improvement expected in the second half.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR35 crores; ~5.39% of sales; headcount ~2,400 to ~2,600

segments.name: Adani Group projects
segments.commentary: Management estimated roughly 45% of Q1 revenue came from Adani Group projects, including RVNL and SMC. Within the order book, group projects are about 70% (61% of the INR6,200 crore bid pipeline).

segments.name: Order book by sector
segments.commentary: Industrial 39%, residential 37%, government 23%, institutional about 1%. Q1 order inflow was INR630 crores, 93% from Adani Group.

segments.name: Precast
segments.commentary: No separate revenue disclosed. Management indicated plant capacity of about INR200 crores, with INR150-200 crores executed per year.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue of INR4,400-4,500 crores reaffirmed; management expects average growth of more than 25% going forward.
EBITDA margin of 7-8% for the full year; management said the bulk of the improvement comes in the second half, and could go beyond 7-8% as execution speeds up.
Employee cost expected to normalise to 4-4.5% of sales once sales pick up and labour availability improves.
Capex guided at 3-4% of revenue; larger projects could push it higher.
Order inflow of INR400-500 crores above prior expectations is not assumed; management expects FY27 inflows in the INR4,000-5,000 crore range, with more projects expected to click in Q2 and Q3.
Management expects finance costs to fall further and says the company could become net debt-free within two to three quarters.
Guidance is on a consolidated basis, and government orders are excluded from inflow guidance until they are firm.
Expects end-FY27 order book of about INR1,000 crores above the INR5,000-6,000 crore range if more than INR4,000 crores is executed.
capex_capacity: Q1 capex of INR28 crores; guided to 3-4% of revenue on average.

Workforce of 16,000+ labourers deployed in Q1; management expects requirement of 16,000-17,000 at peak, with a further 3,000-4,000 to be added over the next one to two quarters as finishing and MEP work starts.
Mahim project: first two blocks raft foundation complete, now in first basement work. Matunga: piling under way, sheet piling before excavation.
SMC high-rise: core and shell complete, MEP, interiors and facade under way; completion expected by June 2027.
RVNL: two of three buildings to be handed over soon, hospital building RCC complete; project expected to complete by October 2026.
Ahmedabad Airport cityside: RCC work in full swing. Ambaji Mata Temple: excavation stage, some buildings at footing level.
demand_pricing: Order book INR13,245 crores as of 30 June 2026. Largest projects: Shree Ambaji Mata Temple INR962 crores, SMC High-Rise INR693 crores, GIFT City FinTech building INR259 crores, Science City gallery INR248 crores.

Dharavi: about INR3,000 crores of the order book across two projects, which management equated to roughly 30,000-32,000 of the 2 lakh houses planned. Right of first refusal on further Dharavi work depends on performance over the next 1-2 years.

Cost escalation: aluminium and copper price increases hit some SMC and RVNL activities. Adani projects are pass-through, so management sees little impact there. Cost-plus contracts target about 7% EBITDA; Adani projects 6-7%, non-Adani 8-9%.

Management said the company will concentrate on Gujarat and Mumbai and aims for a 70-75% Adani / 25% non-Adani mix. Government order inflows are excluded until firm, and the Commonwealth Games project tender has not yet been issued.
UP medical project receivables: about INR40 crores receivable and INR60 crores unbilled; management expects EOTs to be signed and collections to close by end-August or mid-September 2026.
SDB receivables outstanding: INR90 crores; management plans a meeting with the counterparty's board.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR4,500 crore FY27 revenue target and 20-25% growth still intact?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reaffirmed INR4,400-4,500 crores and said average growth would exceed 25%.

qa_highlights.question: When does the 7%+ margin start, Q2 or H2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 7%+ range comes from H2. Q1 margin was hit by about 1% from low April-May billing against labour cost. Q1 billing was INR319 crores in June versus INR270 crores in each of April and May.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company be net debt-free within two to three quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said this could happen as working capital use falls and surplus FDs build.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a Dharavi opportunity beyond the current two projects?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it holds the first right of refusal. Further projects depend on performance on the current two. Redevelopment of about 2 lakh houses over roughly five to six years is planned, with separate development of cleared land after that.

qa_highlights.question: What is the tax rate outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 tax rate was 35%. Management expects the full-year rate to be slightly above 25% because some expenses are non-deductible.

qa_highlights.question: Is the margin on cost-plus projects tightly controlled?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said cost-plus contracts work out to about 7% EBITDA, with a 1-2% gap depending on location (Mumbai about 3%, Mundra about 1.5%).

risks_watch: Margin delivery: Q1 EBITDA margin 6.42% vs 7-8% FY27 target; management says the bulk of improvement is in H2 and depends on April-May billing catching up, labour availability and employee cost falling to 4-4.5% of sales.

Receivables and collections: UP medical project (about INR40 crores receivable, INR60 crores unbilled) expected to close by end-August or mid-September 2026 once EOTs are signed; SDB receivables of INR90 crores still unresolved with a board meeting pending.
