540575|2026-09.headline: Star Cement Q2 FY27 EBITDA fell to INR164 crores (from INR194 crores) and PAT to INR39.58 crores, with management guiding 12-13% H2 volume growth.
540575|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 cement volumes rose to 11.23 lakh tons from 10.72 lakh tons, but EBITDA fell about 15% YoY to INR164 crores and per-ton EBITDA dropped to INR1,372 from INR1,651. Q2 demand was hit by Assam floods, elections and Manipur unrest, while October sales were reportedly above 12% growth. Management kept the FY27 EBITDA guidance, reiterated a 7-8% full-year volume outlook, and said the Nimbol clinker and grinding project (ground-breaking from 1 December) and the Jhajjar grinding unit are on track. Capex phasing for FY28 was raised to about INR1,900 crores, with the timing flagged as flexible.

segments.name: Northeast cement
segments.commentary: Q2 sales were 7.96 lakh tons vs 7.84 lakh tons last year. Management said Assam and Nagaland flooding and Manipur unrest drove a roughly 25% decline in those markets. Trade share was 77%.

segments.name: Outside Northeast cement
segments.commentary: Q2 sales were 3.27 lakh tons vs 2.88 lakh tons last year, with West Bengal growth in the higher teens expected for H2. Blend was about 18% OPC and the rest PPC.

segments.name: Clinker sales
segments.commentary: Q2 clinker sales were 0.74 lakh tons vs 1.01 lakh tons last year, and H1 clinker sales were about 1.26 lakh tons. Management said clinker tonnage will fall from Q3 as prices are raised to sell selectively.

guidance_outlook: Management expects double-digit H2 volume growth, with about 12-13% YoY company volume growth in Q3 and Q4 and October above 12%.
Full-year 7-8% cement volume growth target is said to remain intact.
FY27 EBITDA guidance is reaffirmed, though the specific figure was not restated on the call; an analyst cited INR1,500-1,600 crores.
Assam Norway (incentive) subsidy accrual is expected at about INR65-70 crores in H2 after the scheme change; H1 subsidy booked was about INR60 crores.
Fuel cost is guided to about INR1.5 per kcal through Q3 and Q4, with management targeting INR1.45 by end-March.
Target of about 20 million tons capacity by 2030-31, with about 18 million tons expected in roughly two years.
capex_capacity: Nimbol (Rajasthan) expansion is now 6 million tons (up from 5 million): 3.3 million tons clinker rated (about 3.6 million tons at full capacity) and 3 million tons cement grinding. EC is expected within a week or two, and ground-breaking starts 1 December 2026, with commissioning around July-August 2028.

Jhajjar grinding unit is 3 million tons (up from 2 million). About 50 acres of land is aggregated, with clarity expected in about a month, and it is expected to commission in the same quarter as Nimbol clinker.

Second eastern grinding unit (2 million tons): Siliguri (West Bengal) is estimated at about INR350 crores capex, vs Bihar at about INR550 crores. EC has been applied for in Siliguri, and the decision is expected in the next call.

Capex guidance (Q1 deck): about INR560 crores in FY27, about INR1,910 crores in FY28 and INR610 crores in FY29. H1 FY27 capex spend was about INR203 crores. Management said the figures are flexible and can shift between FY28, FY29 and FY30 via buyer's credit.

Umrangso (Northeast) clinker plant: EC ToR received, EC expected in 2-3 months, plant land acquired, and the project can be commissioned in about 18-20 months once triggered. The decision depends on demand.
Silchar: power connection partly done; railway siding expected by January 2027, which should lower fly ash costs and improve plant economics from Q4.
demand_pricing: Northeast pricing was broadly flat in September and rose about INR10 per bag in October in Northeast, with INR10-15 outside Northeast (including West Bengal). Management said the increase outside Northeast is weaker.

Competitive threat: JK Lakshmi, Ambuja (4 million tons) and Shree Cement are planning Northeast capacity. Management expects 2-2.5 years for kilns to come up, a 1 million ton kiln each for Shree and JK Lakshmi, and short-term price pressure.
Outside-Northeast cement, about 15-16% of Northeast market (about 2.4-2.5 million tons per year), comes via rakes from Chhattisgarh and West Bengal on consignment.
Premium share 17.3%, lead distance 208 km, clinker factor 68.6%, green power 28%.

Fuel mix in Q2: FSA about 45%, washery and coke fine coal about 40%, biomass about 11.5%, spot auction coal about 10%. About three months of coal stock is held. Coal India FSA deliveries resumed in November (about five rakes so far, with about 60 rakes pending).
Incentive: Nimbol and Northeast incentive structure is expected to be similar in quantum, though new schemes allow about 110% of fixed capital investment vs about 200% under the existing scheme.

qa_highlights.question: How will H2 volumes shape up and how was October?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects double-digit H2 growth, with about 12-13% YoY in Q3 and Q4. October growth was above 12%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did fuel cost stay flat at INR1.55 vs the guided INR1.45 in Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q2 was INR1.52 and that AFR availability was constrained in the rains. Fuel is guided to about INR1.5 for Q3 and Q4, with INR1.45 targeted by end-March.

qa_highlights.question: Has the Nimbol EC come through and when does ground-breaking start?
qa_highlights.answer: The EAC meeting was successful, the EC is expected to be granted in a week or two, and ground-breaking is planned for 1 December 2026.

qa_highlights.question: Will the QIP be pursued?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Management said the stance of net debt to EBITDA staying below 1.5x holds for now, and capex will be funded through debt and internal accruals.

qa_highlights.question: Why was clinker sold in H1, and how will this continue?
qa_highlights.answer: Clinker is sold to non-branded grinders, with some going to Siliguri and Nepal. Prices were raised from Q3, so tonnage will fall but margins are expected to improve.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Northeast price outlook secure given new entrants?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects short-term price pressure but long-term stability, since the market is about 1.5 million tons per year of growth, and the incumbents retain trade dominance.

risks_watch: Coal supply: FSA deliveries were absent through September and October, with about 60 rakes pending. Industry fuel prices are rising above INR2 per kcal, which could cut margins if the guided INR1.5 is missed.
Northeast competition: JK Lakshmi, Ambuja and Shree Cement capacity could pressure prices, and out-of-region rake supply (15-16% share) is a swing factor.
Capex and timing: FY28 capex outlay is about INR1,910 crores, and Bihar vs Siliguri and Jhajjar land and EC clarity are pending. The Q2 deck update is due in about a week.
Manipur unrest and Assam flooding have hurt Northeast demand, and H2 relies on about 12-13% company growth against a 7-8% industry growth outlook.
Non-cement and incentive income: Assam incentive accruals (H2 about INR65-70 crores) are a material part of profit. The power cost per unit was not disclosed on the call.
Q2 EBITDA and per-ton EBITDA declined sharply YoY, so the reaffirmed FY27 EBITDA guidance needs H2 recovery.

540595|2026-03.headline: Tejas Networks Q4 FY26 revenue rose 8% QoQ to INR333 crores, but Q4 PAT loss widened to INR211 crores; FY26 PAT loss INR909 crores.
540595|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue was INR333 crores, up 8% QoQ from INR307 crores, with EBIT loss narrowing to INR219 crores from INR239 crores. PAT loss widened to INR211 crores from INR197 crores in Q3, and FY26 revenue was INR1,103 crores against a PAT loss of INR909 crores. Management described FY26 as a transition year after the BSNL 4G project, with delayed wireline and wireless projects causing a revenue shortfall, while R&D and capex were maintained. Order book closed at INR1,514 crores versus INR1,019 crores a year earlier, with India at about 88% of revenue and around 83% of order book, excluding the BSNL 4G add-on PO. Senior management and CFO changes were announced during the call.

540595|2026-06.headline: Tejas Q1 FY27 revenue rose about 20% QoQ to INR402 crore, with PBT still negative at INR271 crore and BSNL expansion order awaited.
540595|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 revenue was INR402 crore, up about 20-21% QoQ from Q4 FY26, split evenly between India and international. PBT was negative INR271 crore versus negative INR281 crore in Q4, and PAT improved slightly. Inventory eased to INR2,358 crore from INR2,438 crore, while net receivables rose to INR2,232 crore from INR1,905 crore and net borrowings reached INR4,277 crore. Management said the BSNL 26,000-site expansion order is in final stages and expected soon, and that its first international 5G end-to-end win in South America was secured.

segments.commentary: Roughly 50% of Q1 revenue, largely wireless 5G radios shipped to a European customer and a global customer with NEC; first end-to-end 5G network win in South America (radio, BBU and core). Optical expansion for an African wholesale bandwidth provider.

segments.name: India (wireline and wireless)
segments.commentary: Roughly 50% of Q1 revenue, driven by domestic optical and FTTx shipments; Tier 1 telco FTTx expansion, 100G/400G DWDM for 5G backhaul and hyperscaler DC connectivity, and a large power utility modernisation win. Management does not split wireless vs wireline revenue.

D2M broadcast: field and lab trials completed with Prasar Bharati and FreeStream; commercial path depends on a Prasar Bharati tender that has no clear timing. Management cited a TAM of close to $1 billion if rolled out nationwide, with fewer sites than BSNL.

540595|2026-09.headline: Tejas Networks Q2 FY27 revenue rose 55% YoY to INR406 crores, but PAT stayed at a INR207 crore loss; order book rose to INR2,315 crores on BSNL 4G LOI.

EBITDA was negative INR108 crores (Q1: negative INR99 crores) and PAT was negative INR207 crores (Q2 FY26: negative INR307 crores). Order book rose to INR2,315 crores from INR1,529 crores in Q1, driven by LOI and subsequent POs for the BSNL 4G expansion of 18,000-plus sites. Net working capital fell to INR4,235 crores on lower receivables, while net debt rose to INR4,384 crores from INR4,277 crores as capex and operating costs were funded.

segments.commentary: Q2 revenue driven by optical IP and FTTx shipments to private operators and system integrators. Received POs for GPON FTTx from several Indian ISPs, an LOI from a new SI for IP/MPLS routers for BharatNet middle mile in 3 states, and an order for a pan-India OTN network for a Government of India enterprise.

Developing a compact baseband unit supporting up to 5 frequency bands per site, and expanding 5G radio portfolio across custom bands from 700 MHz to 4.9 GHz.

demand_pricing: Order book INR2,315 crores at Q2-end, 96% India and 4% international; management said the BSNL LOI accounts for only part of the order book and non-BSNL customers contributed the rest.

International traction is in new 5G deployments in emerging markets, where Tejas positions itself as a new, responsive vendor to Tier 1, Tier 2 and smaller operators; several deals are joint solutions with partners such as NEC and Rakuten.
Won a new Tier 1 pan-African operator contract for 400G optical equipment.

Data center interconnect is a focus area, working through system integrators building full data center racks rather than with GPU vendors directly; management cited DCI wins in India and abroad without quantifying them.

qa_highlights.question: How much BSNL dues have been recovered and how much is still due, and when will payment come?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the milestone delivery requirements have been met and a significant amount of collections linked to those milestones should come in this quarter. It did not give an exact figure but said receivables will fall substantially.

qa_highlights.question: Does the INR2,300 crore order book include the INR1,500 crore BSNL order?
qa_highlights.answer: Only a part is in the order book. Purchase orders are issued site by site, and management expects most of the INR1,500 crore to convert by quarter-end. The rest of the order book comes from non-BSNL customers, but no breakdown was given.

qa_highlights.question: Why no wins outside BSNL in India for wireless?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Indian operators had built their 4G/5G networks already and Tejas must wait for the next expansion phase; qualification through POCs and trials is under way, including with Vi.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company partnering with GPU vendors for AI data centers, and what is the DC stage with TCS?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Management said it partners with system integrators building complete data center racks, and the focus is data center interconnect rather than GPU vendors. No further detail was given on the TCS POC.

qa_highlights.question: What was the INR145 crore contract manufacturing loss in COGS, and will it recur?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said the provision related to the prior year (September 2025) and there is no such provision in Q2 FY27. Management said it was tied to manufacturing for the first 100,000-site order and will not recur.

qa_highlights.question: How much inventory and gross debt will reduce over 6 to 9 months?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give numbers, saying inventory should fall significantly over the next few quarters toward levels in line with normal quarterly business, with debt also falling significantly as the order converts.

qa_highlights.answer: Railways: a 700 MHz 5G network trial section is deployed under a PO, to support internal railway communications and potentially Kavach; expansion depends on results. D2M: Tejas has developed broadcast radio heads and trialled them around Delhi, but will supply as a radio provider to SIs, not as the system integrator.

qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to comment on NEC's revenue. It said Tejas licensed massive MIMO 5G radio technology from NEC, supplies it to NEC's existing customers and new customers with changes, and is a radio development partner for NEC's future radios.

540602|2026-03.headline: GTPL Hathway swung to a Q4 FY26 net loss as consolidated reported EBITDA margin fell to 9.7% and operating margin to 18%.
540602|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 4% YoY to INR9,344 million, but the quarter posted negative PAT driven by two fewer operating days (~INR12 crore revenue impact), year-end impairment/provisions (~INR7.5-8 crore) and a forex revaluation loss (~INR9 crore). FY26 consolidated revenue grew 7% to INR37,466 million, with net profit attributable to parent of INR156 million. Subscriber base was flat in the quarter as capex shifted to the Headend-In-The-Sky (HITS) platform, and management guided to renewed consolidation and capex of about INR350 crore per year.

Says management expects more consolidation announcements, with named deals possibly disclosed by the next quarterly call; no quantified target given.

Transponder contracts for HITS are USD-denominated, creating forex revaluation exposure; accounted under depreciation and ROU assets.

qa_highlights.question: Why was there no subscriber growth in cable and broadband this quarter, and are the exceptional items recurring?
qa_highlights.answer: Cable focus shifted to converting the base and HITS cost savings, with expansion from Q1 FY27; broadband net adds were muted but are expected to resume next quarter. The impairment was described as a one-time item on old analogue-era investments.

qa_highlights.question: How long can industry consolidation last, and what has held back other HITS adopters?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says 40-45 million subscribers sit with small MSOs and that consolidation will accelerate post-HITS launch, with about 800 MSOs in India. Competition is defined broadly to include OTT, telcos and social platforms.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the 40-45 million small-MSO base can be acquired in FY27-FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to quantify, saying talks are underway with large players and that deal announcements should come by next quarter.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 18% is affected by the two-day shortfall (Q4 has 90 days versus 92 in Q3, when margin was 24%); the one-time items sit below EBITDA.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex plan for FY27-FY29 and the maintenance versus growth split?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR350 crore per year, with about INR150 crore for broadband and about INR200 crore for cable and HITS; about 50% maintenance and 50% growth, totalling about INR700 crore over two years.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ROCE target?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says normalised ROCE is about 15%, and expects to return to that level in 2-3 years as growth capex is deployed; FY26 ROCE was in single digits.

540602|2026-06.headline: GTPL Hathway Q1 FY27 consolidated income rose 12% YoY to INR 1,020 crore, but net profit fell to INR 2.3 crore on higher depreciation and finance cost.
540602|2026-06.overview: Consolidated total income grew 12% YoY and 9% QoQ to INR 1,020 crore, with consolidated EBITDA of INR 109 crore (10.7% margin) and net profit of INR 2.3 crore. Management attributed the PAT decline of about INR 8 crore YoY mainly to a roughly INR 6 crore rise in depreciation and finance cost from capitalising right-of-use assets for HITS infrastructure. Standalone total revenue rose 16% YoY to INR 693 crore, with standalone EBITDA of INR 64.4 crore (9.3%) and net profit of INR 1.9 crore. The company signed a business transfer agreement to acquire the digital TV business of 7 ACT Group companies for INR 36.23 crore cash, with about 6 lakh subscribers, targeted to close by 15 September 2026.

540602|2026-09.headline: GTPL Hathway Q2 FY27 consolidated total income rose 19% YoY to INR11,464 million, but reported EBITDA was flat at INR1,103 million (9.6% margin).

540611|2026-03.headline: AU SFB Q4 FY26 profit rose 65% YoY to ₹832 crore with ROA 1.8%, but management guided FY27 credit cost near 0.90% and flagged margin pressure.
540611|2026-03.overview: AU Small Finance Bank reported a strong Q4 FY26, with PAT up 25% QoQ and 65% YoY to ₹832 crore and quarterly ROA of 1.8%, helped by seasonal factors. Deposits grew 10% QoQ and 23% YoY, and loans grew 8% QoQ and 21% YoY, both ahead of the stated private sector benchmark of 13%. Slippages fell 17% QoQ to ₹659 crore and GNPA improved to 2.03%. Management said Q4 was flattered by seasonality, a day-count benefit and lower reversals, and that cost of funds may have bottomed after recent rate hikes.

segments.name: Retail secured (wheels, mortgages, gold)
segments.commentary: Retail secured is 66% of portfolio and grew 21% YoY. Wheels reached about ₹46,400 crore (+27% YoY), gold loans about ₹4,000 crore (doubled), and mortgages (micro business and affordable housing) about ₹42,400 crore (+11% YoY).

segments.name: Commercial banking
segments.commentary: Commercial banking is 22% of lending, at about ₹31,000 crore (+29% YoY, +12% QoQ), plus about ₹11,000 crore of non-fund book. It currently funds about 56% of its requirement internally, with a goal of full self-funding alongside transaction banking and CMS.

segments.name: Inclusive banking (MFI)
segments.commentary: Inclusive banking grew 8% QoQ. Non-overdue collection efficiency in MFI was 99.7% (vs 99.3% in Q3), and 92% of the MFI book is covered under CGFMU.

segments.name: Digital unsecured (cards and personal loans)
segments.commentary: Digital unsecured grew 4% QoQ. Personal loans rose 19% QoQ from a low base, and credit cards broadly stabilised after about five quarters of decline. Total unsecured fell 1% YoY.

segments.name: Deposits
segments.commentary: Total deposits reached ₹1.52 lakh crore (+10% QoQ, +23% YoY). CASA grew 9% QoQ and 20% YoY, with CASA ratio about 28%. Branch banking is about 60% of deposits, and stable deposits are 79%.

guidance_outlook: Management guided FY27 credit cost of around 0.90% of average assets, and said Q4's 0.6% should not be used as the run-rate.
Full-year FY27 cost to assets is expected to fall below 4%, from 4.1% in FY26.
Cost of funds may have bottomed after recent rate hikes. Seasonal margin benefits from Q4 are not expected to recur in the next one to two quarters, implying margin pressure.
Asset mix shift toward secured assets may pressure yields, as unsecured grows slower than the rest of the book.
Management aims to grow at 2 to 2.5x nominal GDP, and said 1.8% ROA is not a permanent level. Its goal is to hold ROA around 1.8% on a full-year basis next year.
Universal bank licence: final application filed in March 2026, pending regulatory approval. Fincare core banking migration completed in April 2026.
capex_capacity: Plans to open 80 to 100 branches every year, with 2,790 touchpoints cited on the call (the 2,500 figure was corrected).
Retail secured distribution has nearly doubled in two years to about 900 to 1,000 branches per retail secured business.
First AI-native loan origination system (gold loans) went live the week before the call. Expansion to mortgages, commercial banking, wheels, personal loans and credit card LOS is underway.
Outbound AI-led calling campaigns aim to reach 25% of total calls over the next two quarters.
Organisational consolidation: agri merged into business banking, and home loans and MBL share back-end teams.
demand_pricing: Management said the home loan/affordable housing market is too competitive, with new NBFCs and HFCs entering, so it is not growing there irrationally.

Deposit rates on savings and term deposits were raised ahead of peers. Management said this reflects the mix of retail vs wholesale, CASA and CD ratio targets, and that it will be managed monthly through ALCO.
Long-term cost-of-funds aspiration is to trade near the prevailing repo rate (5.25% currently), against about 6.75% now.
Wheels growth was driven by improving affordability across segments.

qa_highlights.question: What are the details of the ₹21 crore contingency provision created in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Vivek Tripathi said these were ordinary business banking working-capital standard accounts, not high-value specific cases. The provision was added on an internal risk assessment of security cover, with no specific segment or aggregate exposure disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: Why were savings and term deposit rates raised well ahead of the industry?
qa_highlights.answer: Sanjay Agarwal said it is a combination of how much to raise, cost of money, CASA and retail/wholesale mix and CD ratio. He noted cost of money fell 32 bps in FY26 against an expected 15-20 bps, and that liabilities are managed daily and monthly through ALCO.

qa_highlights.question: What is the sustainable ROA and what levers drive it?
qa_highlights.answer: Gaurav Jain said Q4 is seasonally strong and the aim is to hold ROA around 1.8% on a full-year basis next year. Levers are opex-to-assets improvement and lower credit costs from MFI and credit cards. No numeric target was given.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the Q4 margin was from IT refund and other one-offs?
qa_highlights.answer: Gaurav Jain said the IT refund helped only slightly and was not material. He said cost of funds may have bottomed, and the seasonal benefits from lower day count and lower slippages will not recur next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: How should cost-to-assets evolve as the bank moves to a universal banking licence?
qa_highlights.answer: Sanjay Agarwal said FY27 cost to assets should go below 4%, with a first benchmark of about 3.5% in three to five years. He declined to give a number for AI-driven cost savings, calling the technology too early-stage to quantify.

qa_highlights.question: What credit cost should be assumed going forward, and how will the new RBI ECL norms affect it?
qa_highlights.answer: Sanjay Agarwal suggested building credit cost around 0.90%, and said Q4 should not be annualised. On ECL, management said it was too early to comment. Vivek Tripathi said 90% of the book is secured and CGFMU covers MFI, and the guideline applies from April 2027.

540673|2026-09.headline: SIS Ltd Q2 FY27 revenue hit a record INR 4,816 crore (up 28.1% YoY) and EBITDA a record INR 222 crore, while working capital turned negative.
540673|2026-09.overview: SIS reported record consolidated revenue of INR 4,816 crore (up 28.1% YoY, 4.6% QoQ) and record EBITDA of INR 222 crore (up 32.7% YoY), with EBITDA margin at 4.6%, up 16 bps YoY. PAT rose 37.1% YoY to INR 111 crore, the highest in company history. Operating cash flow was negative INR 99 crore on a INR 273 crore working capital outflow, mainly a delayed INR 216 crore collection in Security Solutions International from a large defence client, which management said was received in October. Net debt/EBITDA rose to 1.24x from 1.05x in Q1, and management attributed the rise mainly to the international working capital delay.

segments.name: Security Solutions International
segments.commentary: Record revenue INR 2,020 crore (+25.7% YoY; +6.3% in constant currency). EBITDA INR 72 crore (+35% YoY), margin 3.6% (+23 bps YoY). Australian wage-linked price pass-through lags due to contract anniversaries.

segments.name: Facility Management Solutions
segments.commentary: Record revenue INR 677 crore and record EBITDA INR 38 crore (ninth consecutive record EBITDA quarter). Margin 5.7%, highest in six years, up almost 50 bps YoY.

segments.name: Cash Logistics (JV, not consolidated)
segments.commentary: Revenue of about INR 220 crore in the quarter with EBITDA above 17%, per management. SIS holds a minority stake and only its share of profit is reported, under share of profit from JV.

guidance_outlook: Overall revenue growth guidance maintained at 15% to 18%; management said Q2 is in line with it.

Most of the minimum-wage repricing benefit is still ahead, as enforcement is state-by-state (Karnataka, Haryana, Uttar Pradesh and Uttarakhand have revised minimum wages so far).
International working capital expected to normalise to about 50 days DSO in Q3; group net debt expected to fall by December.
Management targets debt-to-equity around 1x (currently 1.24x, expected to return to 1x or below) while continuing dividends and buybacks.
Management said FY27 should be one of its better years on a YoY basis.
No India acquisition expected to close in Q3 FY27.

India DSO improved to 73 days from prior levels, and FM DSO was stable at 93 days; international DSO was about 50-51 days in normal cycle.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the INR 290 crore gratuity one-time cost (Q3 FY26) has been recovered, and is there further write-off?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said there is no further write-off; the INR 290 crore was an exceptional item under ICAI guidance. Gratuity paid on separations is being claimed from customers, so no cash impact. A Q4 reversal was an accounting adjustment (liability moved to OCI), not business-related.

qa_highlights.question: Can revenue uplift from the minimum wage code be quantified?
qa_highlights.answer: CEO gave no numeric estimate. Guidance remains 15-18% overall growth; early repricing is visible with margin up from 5.2% to 5.4%, and the trend is expected to continue.

qa_highlights.question: What is the policy on dividends and buybacks relative to PAT?
qa_highlights.answer: CEO said returns will continue via a mix of dividends and buybacks under the existing policy, alongside investment and debt reduction; no PAT-linked payout figure was given.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the Cash Logistics IPO?
qa_highlights.answer: CEO said the approval period has expired; the company will revisit at an opportune time. The business reported record revenue of about INR 220 crore with EBITDA above 17%.

qa_highlights.question: How much revenue is at stake in the Australian pass-through, and how is contract repricing timed?
qa_highlights.answer: Murali Krishna said pass-through happens at contract anniversaries, not renewals; bulk falls in Jul-Sep and Oct-Dec quarters. Costs are provisioned ahead, so no loss is expected.

qa_highlights.question: Why did international working capital deteriorate, and when does it normalise?
qa_highlights.answer: One large defence client's collection (about AUD/INR 120 million annually per the analyst's figure, confirmed by CFO) was missed at end-September and collected in October. International DSO should return to about 50 days in Q3.

qa_highlights.question: What is the group's sustainable debt level, and what is the cost of debt?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said India net debt fell to INR 769 crore from INR 796 crore; international net debt rose to INR 256 crore from INR 11 crore. Weighted average cost of debt is about 7.2% (India about 8.5%, international about 6.5%). Target debt-to-equity is about 1x.

qa_highlights.question: What inorganic opportunities are being considered?
qa_highlights.answer: International: targets are being sought for capability, geography or scale, with acquisitions seen as attractive at current multiples. India: focus on solutions-oriented businesses with higher EBITDA margins; nothing expected to close in Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Cash Logistics not visible in the reported segment numbers?

540678|2026-06.headline: Cochin Shipyard Q1 FY27 PAT fell to INR 151.45 crore from INR 187.82 crore on turnover of INR 1,094.21 crore; ISRF JV with DP World's Drydocks World valued at INR 1,800 crore.
540678|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 turnover rose about 2.4% YoY to INR 1,094.21 crore, but PBT fell to INR 202.49 crore from INR 249.54 crore and PAT to INR 151.45 crore from INR 187.82 crore. Management cited EBITDA margin around 24% and PAT margin around 14% for the quarter. The company delivered three vessels in the period, plus three by subsidiary Udupi Cochin Shipyard. Management announced several strategic moves: a 50:50 JV with Drydocks World for the ISRF ship repair facility, a scaled-down block fabrication plan after HD KSOE talks failed, a Tuticorin hybrid yard lease, and a Green Maritime battery JV.

vs INR 249.54 crore in Q1 FY26 (about -19%)
vs INR 187.82 crore in Q1 FY26 (about -19%)
Around INR 27,000 crore after NGSV contract (L1, about INR 5,000 crore)

segments.name: Shipbuilding
segments.commentary: Management said shipbuilding is about 70% of turnover at 10-12% EBITDA margin. Deliveries in FY27 so far include the third of eight ASW shallow water crafts, a second multipurpose vessel for a German client, and a Ro-Ro ferry for Kochi Municipal Corporation.

segments.name: Ship repair
segments.commentary: Ship repair is about 30% of turnover at roughly 20-24% EBITDA margin. ISRF has a 6,000-ton ship lift, about 1,400 m berthing and annual capacity of up to 82 ships.

segments.name: Udupi Cochin Shipyard (subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Delivered three vessels in the period: two 3,800 TDW general cargo vessels to Wilson Group, Norway, and a 70-tonne bollard pull tug to Polestar Maritime (Adani Group). Management said land constraints limit its new order intake.

segments.name: Green Maritime battery JV (with HBL, 40% CSL)
segments.commentary: Incorporated June 2026 for marinized energy storage systems. Target revenue INR 640 crore by year 5 and about 20% EBITDA margin (ballpark, business plan not final). Total capital INR 50 crore; no manufacturing facility, as HBL will manufacture.

guidance_outlook: Turnover growth guidance of about 12% per year, with management saying it could reach 12-15%.
Blended EBITDA margin guided at around 14-15% for the year on a conservative basis, down from prior years' higher margins.

Target to deliver about 10 vessels in FY27 (three delivered so far in Q1): two more ASWs by December 2026, two more multipurpose vessels, a trailing suction hopper dredger next month, and commissioning service vessels and Samskip container vessels through early 2027.
Operating cash flow expected to turn positive in FY27 as delivery-linked milestone payments come in.
ISRF JV transaction targeted for completion before end of FY27, subject to Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways, DIPAM, and CSL shareholder (postal ballot) approvals.
New investments targeted at a return on capital of about 14-15%.
capex_capacity: ISRF JV: INR 1,800 crore slump-sale consideration, 50% in cash and 50% in JV equity. Expected revenue about INR 600 crore over the next 2 years, scaling to INR 1,000-1,200 crore over 5 years. Plan adds 10 workstations.

Block fabrication: Earlier 1 lakh tonne plan with HD KSOE is now a solo facility of about 60,000 tonnes per annum. Current capacity is about 12,000 tonnes per annum, for total throughput near 72,000 tonnes.

Vadinar (Gujarat) ship repair with Deendayal Port Authority: two floating drydocks for ~250 m vessels. CCEA approval received May 2026. Environmental clearance expected shortly; operations targeted within 36 months of EC. Revenue about INR 300-600 crore after 3 years.

Tuticorin (V.O. Chidambaranar Port): won 30-year lease at one-time payment of INR 305.76 crore for about 110 acres land and 17.29 acres waterfront. In DPR stage; revenue of INR 650-700 crore initially, scaling to INR 1,800-2,000 crore over 7-8 years.

Total capex over about 5 years estimated by an analyst at INR 6,000-6,500 crore across the four projects. Funding targeted at about 80:20 debt-equity. Applied for Shipbuilding Development Scheme (25% capex subsidy) and MDF Interest Incentivisation Fund (up to 3% interest subvention).
demand_pricing: Defence pipeline per management: LPD (4 numbers, about INR 32,000 crore), MCMV (12 numbers, about INR 36,000 crore), P-17 Bravo (7 numbers, about INR 49,000 crore). Management said these are RFPs with competition; LPD and MCMV seen as more suitable than P-17 Bravo.
NGSV: CSL is L1 for five next-generation survey vessels worth about INR 5,000 crore; order signing expected around November 2026. Navy procedures are slow (CCS and PNC approvals).

Commercial: Dredging Corporation of India sister dredger (about INR 1,300 crore, nomination basis) expected within about two months. Andaman 4 x 500-passenger vessels under nomination discussion. Government demand aggregation for about 432 vessels over 10 years, with SCI/BCSL tenders in progress. MR tanker technical bid indicative cost about INR 1,700 crore; Aframax EOI indicative cost about INR 2,600 crore.
Export: European commercial vessels from 2023-24 orders are 80-90% complete but only about 30% paid; payment is tail-ended (around 70% on delivery).
Management said the Green Tug Transition Program could create about INR 1,000 crore of battery-led investment over 10 years, with real volume expected in 3-4 years.

qa_highlights.question: Green Maritime battery JV: product basket, 3-year scale, and timing of meaningful contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: Target product range is marine energy storage and power management systems, with revenue target of INR 640 crore by year 5. Management said the JV will not contribute much revenue immediately; it has placed an order for the battery systems for four green tugs being built, and the JV's turnover will be battery-system only, not the tug. Total capital is INR 50 crore, with no manufacturing facility; HBL manufactures.

qa_highlights.question: ISRF JV with Drydocks World: will it serve DP World vessels only, and how is overlap with CSL's business handled?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said CSL will take orders and the JV will execute them, with DDW free to bring in its own clients. Management said the ISRF only handles vessels up to 130 m and 6,000 tonnes, larger vessels go to the main yard, and the two parties have a clear understanding that DDW will not enter CSL's other segments.

qa_highlights.question: Defence and commercial order pipeline and timing?
qa_highlights.answer: Defence RFPs: LPD 4 numbers (about INR 32,000 crore), MCMV 12 numbers (about INR 36,000 crore), P-17 Bravo 7 numbers (about INR 49,000 crore). NGSV contract expected around November 2026. DCI sister dredger (about INR 1,300 crore, nomination) expected within about two months. Demand aggregation of 432 vessels over 10 years is in tender stage.

qa_highlights.question: Why was FY26 operating cash flow negative, and what are the normalised cash conversion and ROC targets?
qa_highlights.answer: European export contracts are tail-ended: about 30% received against 80-90% construction completion, with 70% due on delivery. Management expects operating cash flow to turn positive in FY27 as deliveries come in, and targets a return on new investments of about 14-15%.

qa_highlights.question: Why are EBITDA margins falling from the past three years, and how should the 14% full-year guide be read against a Q1 margin above 17%?
qa_highlights.answer: Past higher margins came from nominated orders (indigenous aircraft carrier, two aircraft carrier refits) and interest income on a cash surplus of INR 2,000-3,000 crore that has been used for ISRF and drydock capex, so is no longer available. Shipbuilding runs at 10-12% EBITDA margin (about 70% of turnover) and ship repair at 20-24% (about 30%), giving a blended 14-15% on a conservative basis. Management said EBITDA includes interest income as a recurring item.

qa_highlights.question: Vessel delivery schedule for FY27 and the capex revenue potential for the four new projects?
qa_highlights.answer: Target is about 10 deliveries in FY27, with three done. Two more ASWs by December 2026, two more MPVs, a trailing suction hopper dredger next month, two Cyprus commissioning service vessels (October 2026 and around February/March 2027), and one Samskip container vessel by February. ISRF revenue of about INR 600 crore over 2 years, rising to INR 1,000-1,200 crore over 5 years. Vadinar about INR 300 crore after 36 months from EC. Tuticorin INR 650-700 crore initially, scaling to INR 1,800-2,000 crore over 7-8 years. Funding around 80:20 debt-equity, with 25% capex subsidy and 3% interest subvention applied for.

risks_watch: Full-year EBITDA margin guide of 14-15% sits well below prior years; loss of nominated, high-margin defence and refit work and of interest income from the cash surplus are the drivers.

Operating cash flow was negative in FY26 and is expected to turn positive only in FY27, dependent on about 7 vessels of delivery-linked milestone payments (around 70% of contract value) from European export orders that are about 30% paid.

Order inflow depends on RFPs and tenders with uncertain timing: NGSV (about INR 5,000 crore, expected around November 2026), DCI dredger (about INR 1,300 crore), and MR and Aframax tenders. Management declined to give a timeline for LPD, MCMV and P-17 Bravo.
ISRF JV needs MoPSW, DIPAM and CSL postal-ballot approvals before completion, targeted before end FY27. Watch for the postal ballot notice and EC for Vadinar.

Green Maritime JV economics are not final: the business plan is still being prepared, the 20% EBITDA margin is ballpark, and the JV's revenue is battery-only and largely unconsolidated (CSL holds 40%).

Capex of about INR 6,000-6,500 crore across four projects relies on subsidy and interest support; monitor debt levels, the 80:20 funding mix and execution of the block fabrication facility, now solo at about 60,000 tpa.

rows.label: New product launch

rows.label: NGSV order signing (5 survey vessels, ~INR 5,000 cr, CSL L1)
rows.why: CSL is L1 for five NGSVs worth about INR 5,000 cr, lifting unexecuted order book from ~INR 22,000 cr to ~27,000 cr, though Navy CCS and PNC approvals are slow.

rows.label: DCI sister dredger nomination (~INR 1,300 cr)
rows.when: within about two months of call
rows.why: Nomination-basis order of about INR 1,300 cr flagged as expected within about two months.

540691|2026-09.headline: ABCL Q2 FY27 PAT rose 38% YoY to Rs 1,288 Cr on revenue of Rs 16,545 Cr; NBFC RoA reached 2.45% with credit cost at 0.92%.
540691|2026-09.overview: Consolidated PAT of Rs 1,288 Cr grew 38% YoY and 10% QoQ, with revenue up 31% YoY to Rs 16,545 Cr. NBFC PAT rose 41% YoY to Rs 1,008 Cr with RoA of 2.45%, and credit cost improved to 0.92%, which management called its best in seven years. Housing finance PAT rose 73% YoY to Rs 261 Cr, and the company raised lending rates by 20-25 bps after the RBI repo action. Management also launched gold loans (AUM Rs 200 Cr after about 70 days) and continued AI rollout across businesses.

segments.name: NBFC
segments.commentary: AUM Rs 1,76,557 Cr (+26.5% YoY); Q2 sourcing Rs 24,708 Cr, near the record Q4 FY26. MSME AUM Rs 1,01,119 Cr (57% of book, 30% YoY), GS3 1.2%. Personal & consumer AUM Rs 24,955 Cr (+37% YoY), GS3 1.3%. Corporate 29% of book, GS3 1.6%.

segments.name: Housing finance (ABHFL)
segments.commentary: AUM Rs 57,373 Cr (+50% YoY); disbursements Rs 8,957 Cr (+55% YoY). GS2+3 at 0.65% and GS3 at 0.37%. Over 100 new branches launched so far this FY; target Rs 1 lakh Cr+ AUM in 8-10 quarters and 15% ROE.

segments.name: Asset management (ABSLAMC)
segments.commentary: Total average AUM Rs 11.06 lakh Cr (+140% YoY, including ESIC/EPFO mandates). Equity MF QAAUM Rs 2.09 lakh Cr (+9% YoY); passive QAAUM Rs 39,860 Cr; ETF QAAUM +42% YoY vs industry +27%. About 85% of funds in top quartile; SIF assets about Rs 700 Cr.

segments.name: Life insurance (ABSLI)
segments.commentary: H1 total premium Rs 12,656 Cr (+42%); individual APE growth 25% vs industry 12%. VNB margin 16.1%, solvency 190%. AUM Rs 1,20,736 Cr (+16% YoY). Guidance: 20%+ individual FYP CAGR for three years, VNB margin above 20%.

segments.name: Health insurance (ABHI)
segments.commentary: H1 GWP Rs 4,543 Cr (+48% YoY), market share 14.2% (from 13.6%). Retail +43% YoY, corporate +55% YoY. H1 FY27 profit Rs 46 Cr under IFRS; combined ratio 107%.

guidance_outlook: NBFC RoA targeted near 2.5% by Q4 FY27; management says it is already at 2.45%.
NBFC opex/AUM to stay around 1.85-1.9% even with gold loan branch investments.
NBFC margins expected to improve over a few quarters through mix shift, but management is not chasing high-risk customers to do so.
Expected Q3 cost of borrowing increase of 5-10 bps, following the 11 bps increase in Q2.
Life insurance guidance intact: 20%+ individual FYP CAGR, VNB margin above 20%, and net VNB doubling in three years.
Gold loans: 200-300 dedicated branches by March 2027, scaling to 1,000+ branches over three years.
capex_capacity: Gold loan business launched August 2026: about 70 branches opened and AUM Rs 200 Cr in the first ~70 days.
Housing finance: more than 100 new branches launched in the current fiscal year to date.
Life insurance plans to add people and branches in proprietary channel; IndusInd Bank onboarded as a bancassurance partner, with business commencement targeted for Q4 FY27.
GIFT City retail fund platform launched; about six more retail funds in the pipeline.
demand_pricing: NBFC retail/MSME focus: Retail and MSME were 71% of H1 disbursements vs 67% a year earlier; 85% of Q2 AUM addition came from these segments.
NBFC disbursements Rs 11,252 Cr for MSME (about 16% QoQ growth); unsecured business loans disbursed Rs 1,515 Cr (+9% QoQ).
NBFC raised benchmark lending rates by 25 bps effective 26 October on about 70% variable-rate book. HFC raised PLR by 20 bps effective 1 November.
Management said HFC BT-outs stay around 5-5.5% versus BT-ins about twice that; peers have also raised rates.
Life individual business: traditional/protection 66% and ULIP 34% of mix; annuity 14% of retail new business; partnership channel grew 31%, proprietary 10%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did NBFC retail disbursement growth moderate QoQ to about 12% versus the historical 20-30%, and was there pricing screening?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there was no slowdown and that retail is being calibrated to risk appetite; quarter-to-quarter variation is normal, personal & consumer AUM grew 37% YoY and unsecured business 53% YoY.

qa_highlights.question: Why did NBFC employee opex decline QoQ despite growth and new branches?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 had a one-off; Q2 normalised. Opex/AUM should stay at 1.85-1.9% even with gold loan branch investments.

qa_highlights.question: HFC cost of funds rose about 20 bps QoQ; was PLR raised?
qa_highlights.answer: Cost of funds rose 11 bps (6.00% to 6.11%), partly from higher leverage after the April capital infusion; cost of borrowing was 7.46% in Q1 and 7.47% in Q2. PLR was raised 20 bps effective 1 November.

qa_highlights.question: Exposure to agri and drought-hit geographies, and outlook for the next two quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: No direct agri exposure in the NBFC book; the main impact is indirect, through inflation and interest rates.

qa_highlights.question: Life insurance: how will bank relationships evolve under distribution reform and how will the opex-to-premium target be met?
qa_highlights.answer: Opex-to-premium is 21.2%. Management will wait for final regulation; growth is expected to lower the ratio. Direct channel is 8-9% of business (from 2-3%), and 98% of net VNB comes from individual business.

qa_highlights.question: NBFC ROA levers now that credit cost is below 1%, and when will disbursement yields feed into the book yield?
qa_highlights.answer: Levers are growth, margin, opex and credit cost. Disbursement yields are well above portfolio yield, but the impact will take a few quarters to show in the book. Management expects ROA to stay near 2.5%.

qa_highlights.question: Cost of funds on book vs incremental basis after the rate hike, and any management overlay on credit?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 57% of borrowings are floating and 30% of assets are fixed (70% floating), so repricing can pass through increases. A management overlay was created for stressed segments and sits within the 0.92% credit cost.

risks_watch: Rising rates and inflation (deficient monsoon, higher energy and food prices) could pressure borrowing costs and personal loan customers.
Life insurance and health distribution regulation: commission caps (EOM) and the consultation paper could compress margins and bank tie-ups.
Early-stage gold loan book (Rs 200 Cr) and its branch build-out (200-300 branches by March 2027) carry execution and credit risk.
Management says NBFC margins will improve only over a few quarters, so NIM expansion is not yet visible.
Health insurance combined ratio of 107% and profit of Rs 46 Cr in H1 under IFRS transition.
540691|2026-09.management_tone: Confident on growth, asset quality and ROA, with explicit caution on the rate and inflation backdrop. Management was evasive on the life insurance regulation (EOM caps), saying it would wait for final rules, and on near-term NBFC margin expansion, which it framed as a multi-quarter story.
key_quotes: Despite volatile market conditions and uncertainties in operating environment, our asset quality across both lending businesses remains best -in class.
We already are almost there at 2.45% ROA in quarter 2.
So, we are quite focused on building a resilient book over a period and to answer your question on product mix, if you look at the unsecured mix, it has gone up by 1% over the last quarter.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Gold loan dedicated branches go from about 70 to 200-300 by March 2027 (1,000+ over 3 years), HFC has added 100+ branches this FY, and IndusInd bancassurance commencement is targeted for Q4 FY27.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: NBFC AUM grew 26.5% YoY to Rs 1,76,557 Cr with Q2 sourcing Rs 24,708 Cr near record; HFC AUM +50% YoY; life individual APE growth 25% vs industry 12%; health GWP +48% YoY.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: No capex amount or utilisation figure was given; the brief's capex read is 'not discussed'.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management is guiding NBFC RoA to 'closer to 2.5%' by Q4 FY27 from 2.45% today, which is a held target rather than a raise, and it flagged rate and inflation pressure.

rows.why: Rising rates and inflation (deficient monsoon, higher energy and food prices) could pressure borrowing costs (Q3 cost of borrowing +5-10 bps) and personal loan customers, while health combined ratio is 107%.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Gold loan rollout is under way (about 70 branches, Rs 200 Cr AUM) and about six more GIFT City retail funds are in the pipeline.

rows.label: Life insurance 20%+ individual FYP CAGR and VNB margin above 20%
rows.why: Individual APE grew 25% vs industry 12% in H1 FY27, VNB margin 16.1% (+~450 bps YoY), and guidance held for 3 years.

rows.label: IndusInd Bank bancassurance partnership go-live
rows.why: IndusInd Bank is onboarded and business commencement is targeted for Q4 FY27, adding a bank distribution channel alongside the 31% partnership channel growth.

rows.label: Life and health distribution reform (EOM commission caps)
rows.why: Commission caps and the consultation paper could compress life and health margins and bank tie-ups; management is waiting for final rules, with opex-to-premium at 21.2%.

tone.note: Management was confident on growth, asset quality (credit cost 0.92%) and ROA (2.45%), and cautious on rates and inflation; analysts probed disbursement moderation, opex, cost of funds and EOM regulation, which management was evasive on, saying it would wait for final rules.

540692|2026-03.headline: FY26 revenue rose 14% to INR931 crore and EBITDA margin expanded 405 bps to 7.7%, while Q4 volume fell to 1,912 MT from 2,349 MT.
540692|2026-03.overview: Apex Frozen Foods reported FY26 revenue of INR931 crore (up 14% YoY) and EBITDA of INR73 crore (up 145%), with PAT of INR39 crore versus INR4 crore. Q4 FY26 revenue was INR168 crore versus INR197 crore, on volume of 1,912 MT versus 2,349 MT, while Q4 EBITDA margin rose to 9.8%. Non-US markets, led by the EU (up 19% in FY26, 15% in Q4), became the largest sales contributor at about 52% for the first time, as US volumes fell on tariffs and logistics disruption. Management expects US volumes to recover now that tariffs have fallen to about 10%, and it is targeting roughly 30% volume growth in FY27, though it said this is subject to production and shipping constraints.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR197 crore in Q4 FY25

segments.name: US market
segments.commentary: Volumes fell due to IEEPA tariffs (peaking near 50%, now about 10%) and logistics disruption; management says orders are returning. US revenue was about INR500 crore versus about INR700 crore previously, per an analyst's estimate.

segments.name: European Union
segments.commentary: EU grew 19% YoY in FY26 and 15% in Q4 FY26; management says the EU accounts for about 50% of total volume. UK FTA is expected soon and EU FTA around end of calendar 2026.

segments.name: Ready-to-eat
segments.commentary: RTE was 12% of revenue mix in FY26, up from 10% in FY25.

guidance_outlook: FY27 volume expected to rise, with management originally envisaging about 30% volume growth; a planned volume of around 14,000 MT was mentioned, subject to production and logistics.
Management said FY26 EBITDA margins should be sustainable if markets remain stable, but gave no formal FY27 margin guidance.
US volumes expected to recover following tariff reduction to about 10%; a US-specific FTA is not yet defined.
New markets such as Russia are being approved for both facilities.
Export incentive (rebate of indirect taxes) expected at about 5% to 6% of exports, subject to caps and no policy change.
capex_capacity: Both facilities are operating in the summer crop season after a brief consolidation period in FY26.
Capacity utilisation was about 30% for the full year FY26, leaving headroom for growth.
Q4 volume was affected by worker-related issues in January and February; volumes recovered in March.
Shipping equipment shortages and vessel schedule delays are postponing shipments by 3 to 5 days.
demand_pricing: Average realisation was about $9.5/kg in FY26 and about $9.1 to $9.2/kg currently; INR830/kg realisation in Q4 FY26 versus INR348/kg average farm-gate procurement cost.
Full-year FY26 farm-gate price averaged INR327/kg; Q4 averaged INR348/kg; Q1 FY27 is expected around INR340/kg.
Management said depreciating rupee is partly passed on to farmers and competitors, and realisations lag orders by 70 to 90 days.
Forward cover is about 30% to 32% of exposure.
Management said freight costs have risen marginally, with the Middle East crisis affecting shipping lines' equipment availability.

qa_highlights.question: Will US revenue return to about INR700 crore once tariffs ease?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said US volumes will scale back up, and revenue will follow based on dollar unit values and currency realisation; tariffs are now about 10%.

qa_highlights.question: Is the EBITDA margin sustainable and what drove the margin gain?
qa_highlights.answer: Drivers were inventory from earlier quarters, lower debt cost, process efficiencies, favourable raw material pricing and rupee depreciation; management said margins should hold if markets are stable.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q4 volume fall while gross margin improved?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited January worker issues and holiday-period disruption; margin was supported by stable farm-gate prices and inventory use.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 volume outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects an increase in volume, originally envisaging about 30% growth, with US recovery and EU/UK FTAs as drivers, subject to production and logistics.

qa_highlights.question: What is the export incentive outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Rebate of about 5% to 6% of exports, subject to caps and no policy change; management described it as a duty reimbursement rather than an incentive.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Middle East impact on logistics?
qa_highlights.answer: Freight costs rose only marginally; the main issue is shipping line equipment shortages causing 3 to 5 day shipment delays.

risks_watch: Pace of US volume recovery after tariff reduction and any US trade agreement terms.
Shipping equipment shortages and Middle East-related logistics delays affecting shipment timing.
Rupee movement: only about 30% to 32% of exposure is hedged, and management declined to predict Q1 realisation (analyst estimate of 7% to 10% rupee realisation increase was not confirmed).
Farm-gate price trends and government feed-price measures in Andhra Pradesh.
Non-recurrence of FX gains: other income of about INR17 crore was mainly forex difference gains.
Sustainability of margin, which management linked partly to inventory usage and favourable raw material prices.
540692|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on diversification and recovery, but cautious on logistics and macro uncertainty. Management was direct on pricing and margin drivers, but avoided commenting on competitors and gave no formal FY27 margin guidance.
key_quotes: For the first time in Apex's history, non-U.S. export markets became the largest contributor to sales in FY '26, accounting for almost 52% of the total sales mix.
So we are optimistic, but at the same time, we are also being cautious.
We are getting back our orders from the U.S. market also.

540692|2026-06.headline: Apex Frozen Foods Q1 FY27 PAT rose 138% YoY to INR22 crores on 15% higher shrimp realisation (INR930/kg), despite 13% lower volumes at 2,624 MT.
540692|2026-06.overview: Revenue was flat at INR257 crores against INR258 crores a year earlier, while EBITDA rose 79% to INR33 crores and margin expanded to 12.7% from 7.1%. Shrimp sales volume fell to 2,624 MT from 3,015 MT, hit by April-May labour shortages, container and equipment shortages, and EU shipment clearance delays that spilled into Q2. Management kept full-year production guidance at around 12,000 MT and said Q2 volume should recover, subject to global transport normalising. Realisation was guided to hold near INR900 per kg in Q2.

financial_highlights.change: flat vs INR258 crores in Q1 FY26

segments.name: USA
segments.commentary: Accounted for 70% of shrimp sales in Q1 FY27 vs 54% a year earlier; sales rose 13% YoY and 121% QoQ. Pricing includes a 10% tariff plus ADD/CVD (about 9%).

segments.name: EU and UK
segments.commentary: Contributed 25% of shrimp sales vs 39% in Q1 FY26, hit by war-led transport disruption and origin-side testing and certification requirements; management said EU volumes spilled into Q2.

segments.name: Ready-to-Eat (RTE)
segments.commentary: 16% of Q1 volume vs 15% last year; management targets at least 18-20% of volume in FY27, with RTE margin about USD 0.50/kg above RTC at minimum.

guidance_outlook: Full-year FY27 production guided at around 12,000 MT, reiterated from the start of the year; management said the earlier 14,000 MT figure was not a company guidance.
Q2 volume recovery expected, subject to global transport normalisation; order book covers sales until about mid-Q3 FY27.
Realisation in Q2 expected near INR900/kg, similar to Q1.
Margins expected to stay broadly stable, with partial pressure from higher ocean freight (more than doubled since Q4 FY26) and rising farm-gate prices.
Capacity utilisation targeted at 35-40% through FY27; next growth stage of 14,000-15,000 MT considered for FY28-29, not yet firmly committed.
Japan business initiated; Russia expected to start by end-Q2 or Q3 FY27; Australia still at audit stage.
capex_capacity: Volume capacity utilisation 38% in Q1 FY27 vs 39% in Q1 FY26; management targets sustained 35-40% through the year.
RTE capacity utilisation 16%, similar to prior year.
Labour shortage in April-May due to summer heat was resolved toward end-Q1 per management.
Raw material supply tightness expected to ease as new crop comes in.
No capex plans were announced in the call.
demand_pricing: Realisation of INR930/kg is up about INR80-90/kg YoY, helped by higher USD unit values, a weaker rupee and a higher RTE mix.
US buyers placed more orders after tariff uncertainty eased; the 10% tariff has been stable since the start of the year.
Farm-gate prices rose about 6-7% over the 3-4 weeks before the call; Q1 prices were described as stable.
Management said realisations above a certain level would hurt consumption and volumes, as in FY22-23.
UK-India FTA effective 15 July 2026, but non-tariff barriers such as 50% testing of Indian shipments remain; EU FTA expected around December 2026 or January 2027.
Ocean freight costs have more than doubled since Q4 FY26 due to war-led disruption.

qa_highlights.question: How are fish meal and feed price increases affecting farmers and the company, and are they temporary?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said feed manufacturing is not part of the business. Farm-gate prices rising gave farmers comfort; margins should stay stable, with freight and farm-gate price increases as partial offsets.

qa_highlights.question: Why was volume below the 12,500-14,000 MT run-rate, and what growth is expected for the rest of the year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the target is about 12,000 MT. Q1 was hit by labour shortage and container shortages, and EU shipments slipped into Q2, which made US volumes look high. The order book is firm to mid-Q3.

qa_highlights.question: What is the RTE contribution and its margin premium over RTC?
qa_highlights.answer: RTE was 16% of Q1 volume and is expected to reach at least 18-20% in FY27. The margin premium is at least USD 0.50/kg over RTC, with some products higher.

qa_highlights.question: Will US tariff refunds be received?
qa_highlights.answer: No refunds have been received yet. Timing and outcome are unclear because of ongoing US legal proceedings.

qa_highlights.question: Is Q1 realisation a new high versus history, and is it sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Similar levels were seen in FY22 during COVID phase 2, but those were driven by panic buying and hurt volumes. The company aims for a sustainable level through a richer value-added mix.

qa_highlights.question: What is the US CVD and ADD outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: ADD is at 3.4%, up from 1.35%, with a final determination around September 2026. CVD could fall by about 5.77% in December 2026 if duty drawback and RoDTEP are accepted as non-subsidies.

qa_highlights.question: What new adjacent products are being commercialised?
qa_highlights.answer: Proprietary customer-developed RTE and RTC products are already being shipped, estimated at 3-4% of sales (about 300-400 MT on 12,000 MT), rising to about 500 MT annually.

risks_watch: Ocean freight costs have more than doubled since Q4 FY26 because of war-led disruption; freight is the main risk to margin stability.
EU and UK volumes dropped to 25% of sales; watch whether shipments normalise in Q2 and whether testing or certification delays persist.
Full-year volume of about 12,000 MT requires roughly 9,000+ MT in the remaining three quarters versus 2,624 MT in Q1 FY27.
Capacity utilisation of 38% is well below the 14,000-15,000 MT next-stage ambition.
Possible US tariff refunds are unclear; the CVD review in December 2026 and the ADD determination in September 2026 could change pricing.
Farm-gate price increases and tight raw material supply could pressure costs.
540692|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on profitability and pricing, but cautious and hedged on volumes, freight and the timing of FTA benefits. Management avoided committing to FY28-29 volume figures and said it was too early to say.

540699|2026-03.headline: Dixon Q4 FY26 revenue flat at INR10,520 crore; FY26 revenue up 26% to INR48,893 crore, with FY27 guided to INR56,000 crore ex-Vivo.
540699|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue was flat, with management citing geopolitical concerns, softer consumer demand, brand inventory rationalisation and memory-chip cost inflation in smartphones and IT hardware. Q4 EBITDA excluding exceptional gain was INR418 crore and PAT after minority interest was INR192 crore. For the full year, revenue rose 26% to INR48,893 crore and PAT rose 20% to INR845 crore, excluding exceptional gain. Management guided FY27 to about INR56,000 crore excluding Vivo, with mobile volumes flat and smartphone selling prices up 12-15%, and said the PLI roll-off will compress margins this year.

540699|2026-06.headline: Dixon Q1 FY27 revenue rose to INR15,557 crore, but EBITDA of INR472 crore (ex fair value gain) and PAT of INR218 crore reflect margin compression as Mobile PLI 1 expired.
540699|2026-06.overview: Revenue for the quarter ended June 30, 2026 was INR15,557 crore, with EBITDA of INR472 crore and PAT after minority interest of INR218 crore, both excluding the fair value gain on the Aditya Infotech stake. Working capital absorbed roughly INR800 crore in the quarter, which management called temporary, linked to strategic inventory build and payouts of end-March cash.

Execution of multiple new lines (Inventec JV, HKC notebook and mobile lines, Gemtek JV, display, Longcheer) and PLI receivables timing.
MPMS incentive quantum not yet quantifiable; eligibility criteria stricter than earlier expectation per analyst.

Near-term external headwinds do not alter our medium to long-term growth story, and we continue to see strong opportunities for increasing localization, deepening of manufacturing, new customer additions.

540701|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue rose about 19% to INR 851 crore, with EBITDA of INR 163 crore (19.1%) despite INR 30 crore extra onerous-contract provisions.
540701|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue was INR 851 crore, up about 19% YoY, with CDMO up 21% to INR 690.8 crore and marketable molecules up 9.3% to INR 160.5 crore. EBITDA was about INR 163 crore (19.1% margin), held back by roughly INR 50 crore higher other expenses from onerous-contract provisions and a one-off CHF 2.5 million Swiss pension provision. For FY26, revenue was INR 2,932 crore (up about 8%), EBITDA INR 565 crore (19.3%, up 200 bps) and PAT INR 97.4 crore versus INR 3.2 crore. Management announced a promoter-entity 10-year unsecured external commercial borrowing, subject to shareholder approval, to repay high-cost Indian debt.

financial_highlights.change: up close to 19% YoY from INR 716 crore
up about 21% YoY from INR 569 crore
CDMO up about 6.5%, marketable molecules up about 17%
down about CHF 11 million from CHF 157.6 million

segments.name: CDMO
segments.commentary: Q4 EBITDA margin 18.7% versus 23.9% a year earlier, as Q4 FY25 had high-margin late Phase 3 deliveries; Q4 FY26 carried more commercial supplies and onerous-contract provisions. CDMO was about 81% of Q4 revenue and 83% of FY26 revenue.

segments.name: Marketable molecules (Vitamin D analogs, cholesterol)
segments.commentary: EBITDA margin 21.1% in Q4 and 18.8% for FY26, up about 940 bps on the year, helped by higher Vitamin D analog share and supplier diversification (wool grease).

guidance_outlook: Management is cautious on FY27 guidance, citing geopolitical uncertainty; an analyst's 22-23% FY27 growth figure was described as the target, with formal guidance to follow after about one quarter.
EBITDA margin target of 25% in FY28 for both segments.
Consolidated revenue CAGR of about 15% over the next three years.

India revenue of about INR 500 crore targeted for FY28; FY27 India revenue expected to rise about 25% from FY26 (about INR 220 crore), with the INR 400 crore FY25 level flagged as possibly difficult in FY27.

Net interest cost of not more than about INR 70 crore for FY27 after refinancing, versus about INR 100 crore consolidated FY26; quarterly interest of INR 30-35 crore seen from Q2 or Q3 FY27 if refinancing goes through.
Group effective tax rate about 40% in FY27, about 30% in FY28, and 15-20% in about three years.
Net debt reduction target of at least CHF 10-15 million (about INR 150 crore) every year.
French subsidiary FY27 revenue of EUR 11-12 million and EBITDA loss narrowing to about EUR 6 million; EBITDA breakeven aimed for FY28.
capex_capacity: FY26 capex was about CHF 22.4 million; no major capex planned beyond the Japanese innovator co-investment, which is 100% partner-funded, plus maintenance and SAP/digital spend.
Engineering for Swiss co-investments is on track; the last manufacturing line in France went live in Q4 FY25.
India capacity is in place and regulatory hurdles are cleared, according to management; India operating margin historically about 35-40%.
Tech transfer of a large Swiss molecule to India has started; it is expected to take several years, with an interim phase-wise move of intermediates.
French site has ANSM approval (about one year before the call) and is bidding for Phase 3 and commercial projects.
demand_pricing: More than 10 late-phase projects in drug substance, including PPQ campaigns; more than 30 commercial products form the revenue base.
ADC and linker-payload demand is strong and high-margin; ADC was about 25% of CDMO revenue in FY26, with purchase orders in hand for the next years.
Management expects ADC linker supply of CHF 30-40 million in FY27 and FY28 per the earlier indicator, and says the margin on this product could be more than double the consolidated margin.

India: a large innovator's tech transfer from Switzerland (CHF 20-25 million annual revenue currently in Switzerland; India could see about CHF 15-20 million after a roughly 30% customer discount) and a second innovator opportunity (at least CHF 20-25 million) are in progress.
Sprint initiative to win early-phase projects is reporting new big pharma and mid/small pharma clients; the sales force was expanded in both Europe and India.
Target CDMO/marketable molecules mix of about 85:15 over the next 2-3 years.

qa_highlights.question: How should depreciation and tax rate be modelled for FY27-FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Depreciation has been broadly flat QoQ in functional currency, with FX translation adding to INR figures. Effective tax rate is seen at about 40% in FY27, about 30% in FY28, and 15-20% in about three years as loss-making subsidiaries turn profitable.

qa_highlights.question: Will interest cost fall after refinancing, and when?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said quarterly interest could be INR 30-35 crore, conservatively from Q2 or Q3 FY27, after replacing about INR 800 crore of Indian debt costing about 10.5-11% with cheaper promoter-entity borrowing at about 4%.

qa_highlights.question: Is there FX risk from the Swiss-franc borrowing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Swiss-franc revenue from India and subsidiaries acts as a natural hedge, so no hedging is planned. It cited India revenue of about INR 5,000 crore in foreign currency over the 10-year tenor against about INR 800 crore of debt.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 and FY28 India outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 India revenue and profit are expected to be above FY26, with FY28 target of about INR 500 crore; the FY27 figure may be below the INR 400 crore mentioned. Management said the target holds whether or not the Swiss tech transfer proceeds.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the goodwill increase from INR 4,054 crore to INR 4,798 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it was purely FX restatement at closing rates, with no additions. About INR 550 crore is standalone India goodwill from the 2017 merger and the rest is consolidation goodwill.

qa_highlights.question: Why did borrowings rise and cash build up?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said syndicated facilities were drawn to avoid commitment fees and the USD proceeds are held as deposits earning interest, while Swiss-franc borrowing costs under 4%. Management said net debt is the right metric.

qa_highlights.question: What is the French subsidiary outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 French revenue was about EUR 8 million with EBITDA loss of about EUR 9 million. FY27 target is EUR 11-12 million revenue and about EUR 6 million loss; breakeven is aimed for FY28, which the analyst noted had slipped.

risks_watch: Onerous-contract provisions (INR 30 crore YoY swing in Q4) and project hour overruns could keep hitting margins.
Shareholder approval and execution timing of the promoter-entity ECB, which is central to the interest-cost savings; the analyst pushed back on the INR 2,500 crore gross debt and leverage level.
India ramp-up depends on tech transfers and innovator orders; visibility on the INR 500 crore FY28 target depends on contracts that are still pending.
Management said molecules can drop out even in late Phase 3, a risk for ADC and CDMO revenue.
FY27 guidance deferred, and the CHF 20-25 million India tech transfer timing is uncertain.
Quarterly phasing of ADC supplies is hard to predict, and management said QoQ comparisons are difficult.
Swiss-franc movements affect INR reported numbers, and the analyst noted a roughly 6-7% CHF depreciation against INR over six months.

Management was defensive when pressed on the rise in debt and the currency-hedge logic, and gave more direct answers on interest cost and cash flow.

Our target remains the same, which is to get to the 25% mark in the year after next, that is FY28.
So, getting to INR 500 crores is not unrealistic, whether this tech transfer happens or does not happen, because we have multiple projects in the pipeline.
We are not getting more leverage. That is what I would like to correct here.

rows.label: New capex announcement

rows.why: ADC linker supply of CHF 30-40 million is expected in FY27 and FY28, with ADC about 25% of FY26 CDMO revenue and purchase orders in hand for coming years, and management says its margin could be more than double the consolidated margin.

rows.label: Promoter-entity 10-year ECB to refinance about INR 800 crore Indian debt
rows.why: Quarterly interest could fall to INR 30-35 crore from about 10.5-11% Indian debt to about 4% borrowing, but the deal needs shareholder approval and the analyst pushed back on the leverage level.

rows.label: Net debt reduction of CHF 10-15 million a year
rows.why: Net debt fell about CHF 11 million to CHF 146.8 million in FY26 and management targets at least CHF 10-15 million (about INR 150 crore) reduction every year.

540701|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue fell 4% to INR 6,776 mn and EBITDA to INR 600 mn, mainly from an INR 10 mn order deferred to H2.
540701|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations was INR 6,776 mn versus INR 7,080 mn a year earlier, a 4% decline, which management attributed mainly to an order pushed from Q1 into the latter half of FY27. EBITDA fell to INR 600 mn from INR 1,406 mn, and the company posted a loss before tax of about INR 512 mn after finance costs of about INR 370 mn and an FX loss of about INR 117.3 mn. The CDMO segment revenue fell to INR 5,343 mn while Marketable Molecules rose to INR 1,432 mn. Management guided to single-digit group revenue growth for FY27 with EBITDA margin similar to or slightly above FY26, and said a promoter-level ECB of up to CHF 200 mn is expected to close in 60-90 days.

segments.name: CDMO
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 5,343 mn, down from INR 6,112 mn; EBITDA margin 6.3% vs 17.9%, hit by deferred order and FX loss.

segments.name: Marketable Molecules (cholesterol, Vitamin D and analogues)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 1,432 mn, up from INR 968 mn; margin normalised as cholesterol sales outweighed analogues versus a high analogue quarter last year. Vitamin D and analogues sales and margin reportedly rose.

guidance_outlook: FY27 group revenue growth guided to single digits; France and Swiss CDMO growth slower than planned.
FY27 EBITDA margin expected similar to FY26, possibly slightly higher.
Indian entity revenue guided to grow 25-35% in FY27 with operating margin near 10% (analyst's characterisation, not explicitly confirmed by management).
FY28-29: at least double-digit growth in France and India; group revenue growth above 10% YoY; EBITDA margin closer to 25-26% seen before EDQM issues.
No quarterly guidance; management said Q2 is difficult to guide. Net debt expected CHF 140-150 mn (excluding promoter infusion), reducing by about CHF 8-9 mn.
Interest expense guided at about INR 130-140 crores for the full year (about INR 35-40 crores per quarter).
Promoter ECB up to CHF 200 mn at 4% all-inclusive, 10-year tenor, to prepay high-cost India debt; expected in 60-90 days. RBI approval reportedly received.
capex_capacity: Two tech transfers from Carbogen Amcis Switzerland to India: one commercial contract signed with a US company (Switzerland to Bavla, to complete within FY27); a second legacy project approved by a Swiss MNC and already initiated; three more in advanced discussion.
Second co-investment with the Japanese ADC customer is in progress, with operations expected in calendar 2027.
Naroda and Bavla hold certifications from all major international health authorities; Naroda passed a Korea MFDS inspection and is under US FDA observation; two CEPs granted by EDQM.
Restarting some API production at the Netherlands entity.
Inspections scheduled for later in 2026 at Carbogen Amcis sites (no details given).
demand_pricing: New commercial leadership: Angela Ameriks joined as Global CCO; new India sales leadership; hiring in UK, Central Europe and US West Coast (start 1 Sept).
SPRINT early-phase acquisition initiative reported as successful; over 13 late-phase projects in drug substance portfolio, including PPQ campaigns.
Drug product (Saint-Beauzire, France): RFP volumes up and quotation rates raised, though market is challenging; big pharma audits had positive outcomes.
Naroda: CDMO RFPs rising steeply, several in final negotiation; semiconductor and fine-chemical projects in progress.
Biotech funding slowdown is weighing on development revenue; destocking by customers after pandemic stockpiling noted.
ADC-related revenue in the quarter was about INR 150 crores, including linker, payload and hyper molecule.
Specialty business: new wool grease sources at better prices; new markets in Vietnam, Africa and South America.

qa_highlights.question: What are FY27 revenue and EBITDA margin targets?
qa_highlights.answer: Single-digit revenue growth for FY27; EBITDA margin similar to last year, maybe slightly higher.

qa_highlights.question: How will the high-cost debt be refinanced?
qa_highlights.answer: Promoter entity to raise up to CHF 200 mn in foreign currency and infuse it as ECB into the Indian entity, at 4% all-inclusive for 10 years; expected in 60-90 days.

qa_highlights.question: Why does cash stay overseas rather than repay India debt?
qa_highlights.answer: Subsidiary-to-parent loans are not permitted, and repatriation via dividends triggers tax leakage, so Swiss cash is kept as deposits to fund overseas needs.

qa_highlights.question: What are FY27 net debt and interest expense?
qa_highlights.answer: Net debt about CHF 140-150 mn, falling CHF 8-9 mn; interest expense about INR 130-140 crores for the full year, excluding promoter infusion.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR 550 crore EBITDA for the remaining three quarters achievable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will not be INR 200 mn each quarter, but expects EBITDA similar to last year, with focus on the top line.

qa_highlights.question: Why has the company swung between profit and loss quarter to quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited lumpy B2B shipments tied to new chemical entities, a largely fixed cost base (employee cost about 50% of P&L), and Q4 typically the strongest quarter; each INR 10 mn revenue could add about 70% to EBITDA.

qa_highlights.question: How much goodwill remains and is it amortised?
qa_highlights.answer: Consolidated goodwill is above INR 4,000 crores, restated at closing rates and not amortised; standalone goodwill is about INR 550 crores and is amortised; original INR 1,350 crores.

rows.why: Up to CHF 200 mn at 4% all-inclusive over 10 years, RBI approval reportedly received, and India interest expense guided at INR 130-140 crore for FY27 should fall once high-cost debt is prepaid.

rows.why: Net debt was CHF 153.6 mn at 30 June 2026 and is expected to fall by about CHF 8-9 mn, excluding the promoter infusion.

rows.label: Deferred INR 10 mn order shifts into H2 FY27
rows.why: The order pushed from Q1 into the latter half of FY27 is the main reason Q1 revenue fell 4%, and it can lift H2 revenue against a lumpy Q1 base.
