540704|2026-03.headline: Matrimony.com Q4 FY26 consolidated billing rose 9.9% YoY to INR 126.1 crore; management guides Q1 FY27 PAT to more than double.
540704|2026-03.overview: Matchmaking billing grew 10.5% YoY to INR 125.4 crore in Q4 FY26, ahead of revenue growth of 8.4%, and Matchmaking EBITDA margin improved to 22% from 17.7% a year ago. Consolidated PAT rose 18.9% YoY to INR 9.7 crore, but full-year PAT fell to INR 34.2 crore from INR 45.3 crore as FY26 revenue grew only 0.9% and the Marriage Service and other segment loss persisted. Management said the one-year "Till You Marry" package is now flowing into revenue, narrowing the gap between billing and revenue. Management expects Q1 FY27 PAT to more than double year on year and billing growth in double digits or high single digits.

segments.name: Matchmaking
segments.commentary: Q4 billing INR 125.4 crore (+10.5% YoY), revenue INR 116 crore (+8.4% YoY); paid profiles 2.34 lakh (-4.3% YoY, +3.3% QoQ); average transaction value +15.3% YoY. FY26 billing INR 485.2 crore (+8.3%), revenue INR 455.7 crore (+1.3%).

segments.name: Marriage Service and other
segments.commentary: Q4 billing INR 73 lakh (-40.7% YoY), revenue INR 85 lakh (-36% YoY); EBITDA loss INR 5.7 crore vs INR 4.9 crore in Q4 FY25 and INR 3.2 crore in Q3, including impairment and ManyJobs costs. FY26 billing INR 3.4 crore (-25.9%), revenue INR 4.29 crore (-27%), EBITDA loss INR 15 crore vs INR 14.5 crore.

guidance_outlook: Q1 FY27: management is highly confident of either double-digit or high single-digit billing growth, double-digit revenue growth, and more than doubling of PAT versus Q1 FY26.
Marketing expenses expected to stay at a similar level (FY26 Matchmaking marketing INR 180 crore vs INR 185 crore in FY25) unless needs change.
Billing growth expected to converge with revenue growth as the one-year package revenue recognition flows through from Q4 FY26 onward.
Matchmaking double-digit or high single-digit billing growth expected in FY27.
Marriage Service and other losses expected to stay at a similar level; breakeven not expected in the near term, with a review possible in a couple of quarters or by year end.
capex_capacity: First Elite Matrimony Center opened in Hyderabad in Q4 FY26; management did not disclose segment-level numbers for Elite Matrimony.
Share buyback of INR 58.5 crore completed in Q4 FY26; management said further shareholder rewards would be evaluated subject to Board and shareholder approval.

ManyJobs monetisation started in Tamil Nadu only; over 1 million registered users and more than 10,000 companies using it. Expansion to South or pan India planned after reaching a revenue milestone, likely by year end.
Investment made in an early-stage AI-based astrology startup; Astro Free Chart is in experiment stage with monetisation still undecided.
demand_pricing: Average transaction value up 15.3% YoY and 3.6% QoQ in Q4; growth driven by Personalized Services and Online Services, with renewal rates and first-time conversion rates marginally higher.
Customer acquisition cost described as broadly stable YoY.
Organized matrimony market estimated at over INR 1,000 crore; dating about INR 100 crore plus. Management said organized online reach is around 15 million of 60 million people seeking partners.
Management said Tier-2 and Tier-3 combined is larger than Tier-1 market. Q4 and Q1 are the strongest quarters; Q2 and Q3 are festival-impacted.
Management said Luv.com (serious matchmaking, largely metro) is in early stages with good traction.

qa_highlights.question: Why did PAT fall about 24.5% and why did expenses rise while income was flat?

540710|2026-03.headline: Capacite Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 6% to INR712 crores, with EBITDA up 27% to INR109 crores at a 15.3% margin.
540710|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue grew 6% YoY to INR712 crores and EBITDA rose 27% to INR109 crores, with margin expanding to 15.3% from 12.8%. PAT fell to INR45 crores from INR53 crores as other income dropped to INR1.5 crores from INR33.5 crores. FY26 order inflow was INR4,446 crores, above the INR3,500 crore guidance, and working capital days fell 43 days. Management attributed the weak revenue growth to labour shortfall after West Bengal and assembly elections, and flagged commodity-driven escalation lag, with an INR10 crore provision and a margin guidance cut to 15.5-16.5% for FY27.

qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the shortfall to labour migration around the West Bengal and BMC elections. It estimated about INR40-45 crores lost in Q4 and about INR125 crores for FY26, and said a tree-cutting permission delay on one IIT project also hurt revenue.

540710|2026-09.headline: Capacite Q2 FY27 revenue hit a record INR771 crore (+19% YoY), but PAT fell to INR48 crore from INR51 crore on commodity-driven margin pressure.
540710|2026-09.overview: Management reported record quarterly revenue of INR771 crore, up 19% YoY, with EBITDA of INR119 crore (15.5% margin) and PAT of INR48 crore (6.1% margin). H1 FY27 revenue was INR1,400 crore (+13%) while H1 PAT fell to INR87 crore from INR98 crore. Order book stood at INR13,013 crore as on September 30, 2026, with INR2,487 crore of orders secured in FY27 so far. Management said elevated steel, aluminium and electrical item prices weigh on margins, partly offset by escalation clauses, and that no fresh commodity provision was taken in Q2.

segments.commentary: H1 FY27 revenue about INR123-124 crore; 25 of 34 rehab towers received, with a rehab work front of about INR4,200-4,300 crore (price variation included); company share about 35%.

segments.commentary: Run rate crossed INR60 crore per month; NGT disruption in November, with INR65-70 crore per month expected in non-NGT periods.

segments.commentary: Running at close to INR15 crore per month before NGT impact; expected to reach INR18-19 crore per month from Q4 FY27.

segments.commentary: Only one location (INR70 crore of INR550 crore contract) handed over so far; full frontage expected by March 31, 2027, implying about INR60 crore per quarter over 24 months.

guidance_outlook: FY27 order inflow target of INR4,500 crore; company says it has secured about INR2,500 crore so far and expects to surpass the target, with INR3,270 crore under active negotiation.
FY27 EBITDA margin guidance of 15.5-16.5% and cash PAT margin of 10.5-11.25% maintained; management will revisit in Q4 if commodity escalation catches up.

capex_capacity: Formwork and plant purchases: INR64.2 crore formwork and INR10.57 crore plant and machinery in H1 (management first said INR127 crore total, then corrected).
Budgeted procurement of INR135-140 crore to be completed in FY27, with the balance in H2.
Core fixed asset turnover of 4.7x for the quarter ended September 30, 2026.
Aluminium formwork written off over 7 years; project execution period reduced from 4.5 years to 3 years, so depreciation is expected to stay at current levels or rise.
Q2 depreciation about INR35 crore (up from 29% of revenue per analyst question).
demand_pricing: Public sector 54% and private sector 46% of order book; management targets roughly 55:45 government-private mix over time.
Private sector contracts are 100% pass-through for commodities; government contracts rely on WPI and commodity-based price variation with about a 6-9 month lag.
Escalation gap for government projects narrowed from 5-6% in Q1 to about 2% in Q2 per management.

Steel prices rose to about INR62,000 per tonne from INR47,000 three months ago; aluminium formwork rose from INR10,500 to INR14,500 per sq m (40%), with expected correction to INR12,000-12,500 for future procurement.
NGT restrictions in Delhi NCR: complete ban from November 5 to 20, 2026 (about 15 days); company has factored INR45-50 crore of revenue loss for Q3.

qa_highlights.question: What makes up contract assets and receivables, and how much is retention versus unbilled?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said retention is INR170 crore; contract assets (WIP milestone billings) were about INR1,188 crore after a INR217.62 crore negative contract asset adjustment. Net receivables plus unbilled were about INR2,400 crore, or 77-78% of FY27 revenue; debtors are about 120 days. It disputed peer comparisons of 18-20%.

qa_highlights.question: Will commodity provisions reverse?
qa_highlights.answer: No provision was taken in Q2. Reversal depends on government escalation catching up with commodity prices; a decision is possible for Q4 after a Q3 review. Management declined to predict market moves.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company hit FY28 revenue target of INR4,000 crore and what is the capex and cash implication?
qa_highlights.answer: Guidance reconfirmed. Capex is driven by order intake; management expects positive cash flow after term loan repayment of INR101 crore last year and cash PAT margin of 10.5-11.5%.

qa_highlights.question: Why is bottom-line growth flat in H1 despite revenue growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Last year's PAT was helped by recoveries of bad debts and sale of non-core assets. Management expects INR48 crore of held-for-sale asset sales in H2 to lift margins if realised; operating EBITDA guidance is unchanged.

qa_highlights.question: How will NGT restrictions affect execution, and what NCR revenue share applies?
qa_highlights.answer: Management assumes a 15-20 day disruption can be absorbed; a 45-day disruption cannot be quantified. It did not disclose the NCR share of H1 revenue.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the promoter share pledge?
qa_highlights.answer: Pledge reduced; only 50 lakh shares remain pledged for the SBI project limit, which fell from INR608 crore to INR140 crore. Completion targeted by March 31, 2027, with no further pledges to NBFCs.

risks_watch: Contract assets and receivables are high at about 77-78% of FY27 revenue (about 120-day debtor days); the aging was promised by email and not disclosed on the call.
Escalation gap on government contracts and possible further commodity provisions; margin guidance depends on Q3 catch-up.
NGT disruption in Delhi NCR during November-December; a 45-day disruption would be unquantified.
Election-related labour availability in Q4 FY27 (UP elections); Q1 FY27 revenue dipped due to Bengal elections.
Execution timing risk on MHADA rehab towers, CIDCO new scope (expected in Q1 FY28) and IIT Bombay frontage handover by March 31, 2027.
Recovery of old receivables, with INR100 crore still pending against settlements; settlement agreements not yet finalised.

540716|2026-03.headline: ICICI Lombard FY26 PBT rose 10.2% to ₹36.59bn and 1/n PAT 10.5% to ₹27.72bn; Q4 GDPI grew 18.2% but FY26 GDPI grew only 7.0%.
540716|2026-03.overview: FY26 profit grew double digits despite a ₹0.55bn wage code charge, with Q4 1/n PAT up 7.3% to ₹5.47bn. Top-line growth was 7.0% for FY26 versus the industry's 9.2%, with commercial lines lagging (5.4%) and retail health (51.1%) and Q4 motor (15.0%) accelerating. Management flagged intensifying commercial and fire competition, a Motor TP loss ratio it says is overdue for repricing, and a transition to Ind AS starting FY27 with a plan to seek forbearance. Solvency stayed high at 2.67x and the final dividend was ₹7.00 per share (₹13.50 total).

segments.commentary: FY26 growth 7.6% vs industry 9.2%; H2 12.0% vs 10.5%, Q4 15.0% vs 10.0%. Portfolio mix: private car 52.8%, two-wheeler 25.4%, commercial vehicle 21.8%. Full-year Motor loss ratio about 66.3%, within the 65-67% comfort range.

segments.commentary: Growth 51.1% in FY26 vs industry 19.9%; market share rose from 3.3% to 4.1%. Long-term share of new retail health business rose to 42.1% from 28.5%. Retail indemnity loss ratio 64.6% for FY26 (Q4 57.6%).

segments.commentary: Growth 11.0% in FY26 with 8.7% market share. Employer-employee loss ratio 91.9% for FY26 (Q4 98.1%).

segments.commentary: Health growth 20.0% vs industry 15.4% on a 1/n basis; Q4 growth 38.2% vs industry 20.5%.

guidance_outlook: Management expects industry motor growth in the higher single digits for FY27 and expects Q1 and Q2 FY27 to start positively, though it did not give numeric guidance.
Commercial industry growth could be single digit in FY27 because of fire pricing pressure; April 1, 2026 renewals are being reported at a discount.

Ind AS: IRDAI mandates Ind AS from April 1, 2026. The company intends to seek forbearance for the first year and will submit quarterly pro forma Ind AS numbers from Q1 FY27. Management guided to a 300-450 bps combined ratio decline in the adoption year, with economic value converging over time.
Dividend policy: about 25% of PAT on average; FY26 payout of ₹13.50 per share is roughly 25% of PAT. Solvency may be used for growth, subject to the transition to risk-based capital.
Motor TP: management hopes for an industry TP price hike, which it calls overdue, with the industry Motor TP loss ratio near 85%.
capex_capacity: Crop insurance: current crop exposure is about half of the level of two years ago; the company will not chase crop targets and will select risks, and it plans to expand beyond one state if commercially sensible.

Investment leverage (net of borrowings) fell to 3.48x from 3.60x in Q3 FY26.

Commercial competition has intensified, especially in fire in H2 FY26; reinsurance renewals for FY27 were soft.
Industry Motor combined ratio 128.1% for 9M FY26 vs 123.8% 9M FY25, driven by pricing pressure. Industry overall CoR 119.3% for 9M FY26 vs 113.2%.
Company 10-year (FY16-FY25) average combined ratio 102.9% vs industry 115.3%; average realised yield 8.7%; average ROE 19.1% vs industry 4.0%.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Q4 Motor TP loss ratio much lower, and why is the crop loss ratio negative? Has IFRS PAT been quantified?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said to judge Motor as a category over full year (66.3%, range 65-67%) and reserving philosophy is unchanged. Crop was booked mostly in Q2 at about 100% loss ratio, and the Q4 release reflects favourable experience. No Ind AS PAT quantification yet; the company will return with CoR and ROE impact.

qa_highlights.question: Solvency is high at 2.7x; can excess capital be deployed via dividends?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited Solvency 1 (exposure-based capital) and a pending risk-based capital transition. It will use some solvency for growth as growth returns, and continues a dividend policy of about 25% of PAT.

qa_highlights.question: Health loss ratio split between retail and group, and Motor TP price hike outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Employer-employee loss ratio was 98.1% in Q4 and 91.9% for FY26; retail indemnity was 57.6% in Q4 and 64.6% for FY26, with a 65-70% target range. Industry Motor TP loss ratio is about 85%, and a price hike is overdue but not in the company's control.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company claw back commercial market share and sustain 16% H2 growth into FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY26 share fell about 0.7-0.8 pp from 13.7% and it will be selective, not chasing volume. It expects an industry growth slowdown in commercial, possibly single digit, and was confident of positive Q1 and Q2 but declined to predict the H2 run-rate.

qa_highlights.question: Drivers of H2 motor outperformance and FY27 outlook, and the Motor TP reserve and CV growth question?
qa_highlights.answer: New vehicle sales grew 18.8% for the company vs 13.4% for renewals; retention improved about 5%. CV share of book remained around 22%, with cost of acquisition and a fleet management system cited. Management declined to give the Motor TP reserve figure as a useful metric.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of the commission (EOM) tightening?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said tightening applied uniformly would benefit ICICI Lombard, which says it has stayed within expense-of-management limits. It favours a single-slab EOM structure and awaits regulatory direction.

risks_watch: Commercial lines share loss and fire pricing pressure, with April 1, 2026 renewals reported at a discount.
Motor TP loss ratio sensitivity and a possible long-tail reserve build; industry Motor combined ratio 128.1% (9M FY26).
Crop insurance expansion beyond one state and the terms of the new crop framework.
Ind AS transition in FY27 (forbearance sought); combined ratio and ROE comparability to be disclosed.
Equity portfolio MTM (₹0.49 bn impairment in Q4) and solvency at 2.67x.
Geopolitical and energy-price shock from West Asia conflict that could slow auto sales and savings behaviour.
Possible EOM and commission regulation changes.

540716|2026-06.headline: ICICI Lombard Q1 FY27 PAT fell 46.0% to ₹4.03 bn, driven by a ₹1.65 bn Motor TP judgement provision and two large Fire losses.
540716|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 GDPI grew 7.5% to ₹83.18 bn, below industry growth of 10.9%, with retail lines driving growth while commercial lines de-grew 13.8%. Combined ratio rose to 107.2% from 102.9%, including a 2.8 pp hit from the Supreme Court Motor TP judgement provision and a 1.0 pp hit from two Fire large losses. Excluding these items, the combined ratio was 102.3% versus 102.2% a year ago, and PAT would have been ₹5.75 bn (down 23.0%). Investment income fell to ₹11.74 bn from ₹12.88 bn as capital gains halved, partly offset by higher portfolio yield and duration.

segments.name: Commercial lines
segments.commentary: De-grew 13.8% in Q1 FY27 amid pricing pressure; SME share rose to 33.6% from 28.4%. Fire line declined 27.8% for the industry and the company de-grew about 32%; June Fire de-growth improved to about 18% for the company.

segments.name: Motor
segments.commentary: Grew 14.0% in line with industry (13.9%), market share 10.5%; new vehicle sales up 33.6% vs industry 14.9%. Mix: private car 49.8%, two-wheeler 28.7%, commercial vehicle 21.5%. Motor combined ratio 106.6% in FY26 vs industry 128.0%.

segments.name: Health
segments.commentary: Grew 24.9% vs industry 20.1%. Retail Health grew 69.5% with share up to 4.5% from 3.5%; Group Health grew 16.3% with 10.3% share. Management attributed the higher health loss ratio to industry-wide claim incidence, not company-specific.

guidance_outlook: Management did not give a quantified forward impact of the Motor TP judgement; said it is too early and will update each quarter.
Expects an upward Motor TP premium rate revision; judgement-driven industry loss ratio impact estimated at 12-15%, which it sees as the minimum price change needed.
Expects Fire price aggression to moderate after Q1, though full recovery of de-growth in the rest of the year is uncertain.
Health claim incidence watch-point for Q2 (monsoon-linked); next detailed update to come with October results.
capex_capacity: No capex, capacity or commissioning plans were discussed on the call; the call covered underwriting, pricing, reserving and claims only.

Capacity was referenced only qualitatively: management said reinsurance renewals were relatively soft and capacity had been made available across the industry, which drove Fire price competition. No company-specific capacity figures were given.

Motor claims and servicing scale were cited as operating metrics, not capacity: Preferred Partner Network served 75.6% of non-OEM motor claims in Q1 FY27 vs 74.6% in Q1 FY26; 168,521 health and travel claims were serviced through the IL TakeCare app vs 141,116 a year earlier.
Digital servicing capacity: digital interactions rose to 624K in Q1 FY27 from 214K in Q1 FY26; digital share of servicing was 69.0% in Q1 FY27 and 71.0% in June 2026.
Management did not discuss any new product launches, branch or distribution expansion, or timelines for system or platform commissioning.

540716|2026-09.headline: ICICI Lombard Q2 FY27 PAT rose 27.5% YoY to ₹10.31 bn, while H1 PAT fell 5.8% to ₹14.54 bn on a weaker Q1 and Motor TP reserving.

540719|2026-03.headline: SBI Life FY26 VoNB rose 12% to INR66.7bn at a 27.5% margin, but PAT grew only 2% to INR24.7bn due to GST and Labour Code one-offs.

VoNB was INR66.7bn (27.5% margin), and excluding GST it would have been INR70.3bn at a 29% margin. qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is a matter of perception; the range gives flexibility to balance 14% growth with margin, and the product mix is being improved.

qa_highlights.question: What is the GST impact on margins going forward and the opex ratio trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: GST for the second half is already in the 27.5% margin, and the full-year effect is about 1.8-1.9%. Opex ratio would be about 5.5% without GST and the Labour Code versus 5.3% in FY25; the 6.1% reflects GST and Labour Code costs.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the EV operating variance strongly positive while VNB assumptions were strengthened?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said positive variance comes mainly from mortality and persistency, with lower expenses contributing. qa_highlights.answer: Rider attachment on ULIPs is about 45–50%, up from roughly 35% when riders were introduced 1–1.5 years earlier. Riders are counted within individual protection, and rider APE was not disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: Why is individual protection growth lower than peers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the shift from ROP to pure protection lowers ticket size, which makes headline growth look subdued. Individual protection grew 22% by its own measure against pure protection growth of 41%, with ROP share at 68%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the regular-pay deferred annuity plan launch slip, and what are the non-par and regulatory views?
qa_highlights.answer: The deferred annuity plan is expected in the next quarter and is being developed for an opportune time. On non-par, management said pricing is reviewed against yield movements. On regulation, management said it sees the company as well placed and expects future rules to be positive for the industry.

540719|2026-09.headline: SBI Life H1 FY27 VoNB rose 19% to INR32.7bn at a 27.9% margin, while PAT grew 17% to INR12.7bn despite a INR5.3bn GST hit.
540719|2026-09.overview: H1 FY27 showed solid value growth: VoNB up 19% to INR32.7bn with margin of 27.9% (Q2 at 29.3%), and embedded value up 15% to INR873.5bn. Individual rated new business premium grew 12% to INR97.2bn, but management said IRP growth of about 12% in H1 is below the 14-15% full-year target it reiterated. A one-off GST impact of INR5.3bn weighed on profit and opex ratio; excluding it, PAT was INR16.9bn (+39%) and VoNB INR33.8bn (+19.4%). Management said the mix shift toward non-par and annuity products helped margins, while the agency channel slowed in Q2 and the banca channel was softer in September.

financial_highlights.change: +12% YoY; private market share 22.6%, total market share 16%
vs 6.2% / 10.9% in H1 FY26; opex ratio ex-GST 5.8%

segments.name: Individual protection
segments.commentary: Individual protection APE INR4.3bn, +16%; pure protection +26%; including riders, protection APE +30%. Pure protection share moved from 90:10 to 58:42 versus ROP, and rider attachment is about 49%.

segments.name: Group business
segments.commentary: Group new business premium INR65.3bn (+6%), 32% of NBP; group APE INR117.5bn (+18%); group protection APE INR16bn (+134%). Credit life APE about INR140 crore in H1, roughly flat.

segments.name: Bancassurance (SBI and RRB)
segments.commentary: Contributes 53% of total APE; individual APE INR59.9bn (+10%). SBI branch productivity INR5 million on individual APE for the period.

segments.name: Agency
segments.commentary: Individual APE INR32bn (+12%); non-ULIP share rose from 39% to 47%; agency individual sum assured +50%. Added over 72,000 agents gross; average productivity about INR2 lakh. Q2 growth slowed to about 6%.

segments.name: Other channels (direct, corporate agents, other banks, brokers, online)
segments.commentary: Grew 67% and contributed 19% of total APE. Growth driven by a low base and new partners; J&K Bank added as a banca partner. Other-bank channel growing 30%+, mainly non-par.

segments.name: Product mix
segments.commentary: ULIP share 62% of product mix versus 65% in H1 FY26. Guaranteed non-par savings INR24.7bn (+27%); annuity and pension NBP INR46.2bn; participating individual APE INR5.1bn (+9%).

guidance_outlook: Full-year FY27 IRP growth guided at 14-15%, reiterated despite H1 at about 12%; Q3 is seasonally stronger.
VoNB margin guidance of 26-28% maintained for the current half.
Management expects limited impact from IRDAI distribution-economics consultation paper and sees SBI Life as among the least impacted insurers; final guidelines awaited.
Plans to launch a regular-pay deferred annuity soon (possibly in Q3), with margin similar to or above company average.

IFRS 17 transition approach to be finalised by end-March 2027, with adoption from June 30, 2027; investor day planned before that.

Hedging: 80% of premium hedged per policy; management views 80% as optimal.
demand_pricing: Non-par pricing repriced in Q2 with a pass-through of yield benefits to customers; management says it will keep repricing in Q3 and Q4.
Uniform commission and uniform product pricing across channels, so margins are the same across channels.
Management attributes about 70bps of H1 margin gain YoY to yield curve movement.
Individual sum assured +36% and group sum assured +78%; rider sum assured 40% of individual sum assured.
Persistency at 13th, 25th and 49th months: 87.6%, 78.4% and 69.3%, up 44, 110 and 40bps YoY.
Death claim settlement ratio 99.1%; misselling ratio 0.035%.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company satisfied with about 12% IRP growth versus its 13-15% aspiration, and what is the reason for the negative operating-adjustment impact in the VoNB walk?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated 14-15% IRP growth for FY27 and said it is in line with industry growth. The VoNB negative came from a March 2026 assumption refinement (mortality, persistency, expenses), not a change made in the period; operating variances were all positive.

qa_highlights.question: How did banca trend in October and what is the outlook for non-par and annuity distribution across channels?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q3 is seasonally strong and expected to be higher growth. Products are available across all channels and uniformly priced; the uptick has been stronger in agency than banca, and banca sales of these products are being pushed.

qa_highlights.question: Will margins move higher than the 26-28% guidance, and how much of Q2 margin gain came from non-par?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will stick to 26-28% guidance. It does not disclose the non-par margin contribution, but said the mix change helped Q2 margin and that repricing will continue.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of the IRDAI distribution paper, including credit life and bancassurance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said SBI Life is among the least impacted; credit life attachment is under 50% of the bank portfolio and largely paid via loans. It has little partnership outside SBI, so no challenge is seen yet.

qa_highlights.question: Why did agency growth slow sharply in Q2 and what is the protection mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said agency growth will normalise within a couple of months and the FY27 target is intact. Pure protection moved to 58:42 versus ROP, and the sum assured growth is the highest in the industry.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the conservation ratio fall to about 82% from 84%, mainly in linked pensions?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the decline is marginal and not a concern; 13th and 25th month persistency improved and renewal collections grew at high double digits.

IFRS 17 transition approach and treatment of ULIP CSM release, still undisclosed.

540724|2026-09.headline: Prataap Snacks Q2 FY27 revenue rose 26% YoY to Rs 541 crore, but EBITDA fell to Rs 12.9 crore (2.4% margin) as input costs squeezed gross margin to 25.5%.
540724|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue from operations crossed Rs 500 crore for the first time, at Rs 541 crore (+26% YoY, +10% QoQ), with H1 revenue at Rs 1,031 crore (+23%). Gross margin fell to 25.5% from 29.8% a year ago, and EBITDA dropped to Rs 12.9 crore from Rs 22.9 crore; H1 EBITDA was Rs 32 crore. Management attributed the squeeze to palm oil, potato, packaging laminate, fuel and logistics inflation, partly offset by price hikes, grammage cuts and channel-margin changes. Management also announced a proposed Rs 421-422 crore greenfield plant near Indore and guided to a strong double-digit FY27 revenue growth.

segments.name: Namkeen
segments.commentary: Roughly 25% of revenue now, up from about 20% last year and 15-16% two years ago; leading growth, with manufacturing centralised in Indore and Rajkot.

segments.name: Extruded (Rings, Pellets)
segments.commentary: Extruded category about 39% of revenue: Pellets about 19-20%, Rings about 10%. Rings declined post-COVID; non-Rings grew at about 12% CAGR over 5-6 years.

segments.name: Potato chips
segments.commentary: Chips contribution reportedly rose to about 25% from 20% last quarter; available at about 30-35% of total outlet reach, with headroom.

segments.name: Quick commerce
segments.commentary: Currently about 1.2-1.5% of sales; target about 5% of revenue over the next 3 years.

Channel margin reduced from 14% to about 10.5% after eliminating super-stockists in 2022-23; about 2-2.5% headroom remains, being pulled selectively.

qa_highlights.question: How will raw material volatility stabilise, and how is pricing power holding up with gross margin near 25-26%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said gross margin fell about 8 pp from Q4 on input inflation, largely mitigated via price hikes, grammage and SKU optimisation; inefficiencies could add 5-6% margin.

qa_highlights.question: What are the new Indore plant's capacity, capex and land monetisation value?
qa_highlights.answer: Capacity about 65,000-70,000 MT; project cost about Rs 421-422 crore with Rs 250-odd crore debt; existing land valued at Rs 250-300 crore to repay the term loan.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ESOP/ESAR charge in Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: About 50,000 ESARs granted with value of about Rs 5-6 crore, expensed over vesting of 4 years under Black-Scholes; about 2,300 shares allotted to employees on exercise.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Rs 125 crore short-term borrowing and the term loan rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Short-term borrowing is about Rs 25 crore OD plus Rs 4 crore Jammu loan instalment; the new project term loan has not yet been drawn, with bulk drawdown next year, at under 8%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the H2 margin trajectory given fresh inflation?
qa_highlights.answer: Further packaging and corrugated inflation after Q2; management described a 9.5-10 pp gross-margin headwind vs pre-war Q4, with about 2.5% hitting operating profit, and said H2 EBITDA margin should be similar to H1 around 3%.

540725|2026-03.headline: Share India standalone Q4 FY26 PAT rose 368% YoY to INR 75 crore on revenue of INR 383 crore (+103%).
540725|2026-03.overview: Standalone Q4 FY26 revenue nearly doubled to INR 383 crore and PAT rose to INR 75 crore from INR 16 crore, with EPS of INR 17.6 versus INR 11.7. For FY26, standalone PAT rose 20% to INR 298 crore on revenue of INR 395 crore. Consolidated FY26 PAT was flat-to-down at INR 324 crore versus INR 328 crore, held back by fair value adjustments on investments held by group companies. Management pushed diversification into MTF, PMS, wealth distribution, debt (Share India Cred), AIF and commodities, while flagging RBI curbs on intraday bank limits for prop trading.

segments.name: Broking and trading (prop vs client)
segments.commentary: Prop contributed ~70% of revenue but ~49% of consolidated FY26 profit (~52% standalone). Client turnover reportedly exceeded prop turnover (53% vs 47%) for the first time; target 60% client share of turnover by year-end.

segments.name: MTF (margin trading finance)
segments.commentary: MTF book grew from INR 239 crore (FY25) to INR 424 crore (FY26); Dec-25 level was INR 457 crore. FY27 target INR 650 crore; FY28 vision also cited as INR 650 crore.

segments.name: NBFC
segments.commentary: Reported NIM of 17.64% for FY26, roughly flat with FY25; management said NIM will decline as the book shifts to secured lending.

segments.name: uTrade (algo platform)
segments.commentary: Active clients crossed 5,000 in FY26 (5,231 currently); still small in revenue, with focus on adoption. Multi-broker plan slowed by a SEBI circular requiring vendors to set up separately for each broker.

segments.name: Wealth management and PMS
segments.commentary: PMS launched in Q4 FY26 with AUM above INR 100 crore; FY27 target INR 200 crore. Third-party distribution team under Charu Sehgal to start operations in Q3. AIF CAT-3 application filed with SEBI, approval expected by end-Q2 FY27.

segments.name: Share India Cred (debt)
segments.commentary: Started operations in Q1 FY27 with six issues closed; FY27 target at least INR 500 crore of issues.

segments.name: Institutional business
segments.commentary: Institutional empanelments rose 35% from 137 to 186.

segments.name: Other subsidiaries
segments.commentary: NBFC, merchant banking, insurance and technology together contributed about 7% of FY26 bottom line. MSCI (Metropolitan Stock Exchange) cash segment doing INR 300-400 crore daily volume; Sizable stake held.

MTF book target INR 650 crore by FY27, with mgmt saying INR 200 crore incremental is achievable if markets stay normal; deviation possible in low single digits on sentiment.

Options were ~18% of Q4 ADTO.
MTF demand said to have risen in the last 1.5 months; Tier-3 pricing reportedly better because of less competition from sub-brokers.

qa_highlights.answer: Abhinav Gupta said Q4 was weak in FY25 and FY26 due to volatile markets; management prefers annual view with EBITDA ~38% and PAT ~22% (+/-2%). Sachin Gupta said Q4 pressure is not structural.

segments.commentary: Revenue +14% and segment profit +32% YoY on realisations and volumes; volume +3% as broiler feed was deliberately de-prioritised, while cattle feed grew ~8% and layer feed double digits. Shrimp feed business exited.

segments.name: Oil palm
segments.commentary: Revenue +28% and segment profit +4%; FFB volumes +14% in Q2. OER fell to ~18.9% in Q2 (vs 18.8% in Q1) due to heat stress. Added 13,000 ha in H1; Khammam integrated complex inaugurated with mill, CPKO refinery and biogas plant commissioned.

segments.name: Crop care (domestic)
segments.commentary: Revenue grew on a low base but profitability fell on El Niño-led demand weakness and adverse product mix. Ashitaka maize herbicide expected to cross INR100 crore first-year revenue.

segments.name: Astec LifeSciences
segments.commentary: Weak enterprise demand and lower realisations offset CDMO growth; EBITDA hit by elevated input costs. Management flagged weak US and Brazil markets.

segments.name: Dairy
segments.commentary: Revenue +6% on calibrated pricing; profitability hit by elevated milk procurement, packaging and logistics costs. Management expects no milk-price respite for about two quarters.

segments.name: Godrej Foods
segments.commentary: B2C grew 50% with salience at 38%. EBITDA plus working media margin 5.8% vs 5.6% last year. About 25% of current business from products launched in the last year.

segments.name: ACI Godrej (Bangladesh JV)
segments.commentary: Delivered strong volume, revenue and profit growth; management said volumes grew at high double digits across aqua, poultry and dairy.

guidance_outlook: FY27 PBT double-digit growth is still being chased but management said it is tougher and more clarity will come monthly; not a firm commitment.
Oil palm: OER expected to recover toward ~19.7% for the year; aim to end FY at last year's annualised OER level.
Oil palm FFB volume growth guided at double digits for FY27 and FY28; cyclone assessment shows no tree damage.
Oil palm mid-term (2-4 years): downstream PKO derivatives expected to add ~2 percentage points to oil palm EBITDA margin; meaningful impact from Q4 FY27 and scaling in FY28.
Oil palm EBITDA: management aims for a healthy double-digit CAGR over FY27 and the mid-term (FY26 oil palm EBITDA about INR426 crore).
Astec CDMO mid-term share targeted at 50-55% of business; FY27 expected to be a tough year.
capex_capacity: Khammam integrated oil palm complex inaugurated: mill, CPKO refinery and biogas plant commissioned in Q2 (PKO derivatives plant operational from 1 September); full hydrogenation and fractionation in December, second scale-up phase in December.
Plantations: 13,000 ha added in H1 FY27.
Agchem pipeline: three new products to launch this year (including soybean herbicide Ghassnash launched this month), 1-2 new launches a year, targeting seven crop segments by FY29-30.
Astec CDMO: about 90% of Q2 inquiries converted to R&D; around 15 products in R&D pipeline; management expects 70-80% R&D-to-commercialisation conversion.
Sales transformation CoE hired head from Britannia and Marico; two more members to join by December.
demand_pricing: Monsoon ended about 13% below normal; June rainfall about 40% deficit; reservoirs at 10-year low, raising Rabi risk for agchem.
Oil palm: September OER back to last year's level and October marginally ahead; Q2 FFB collections at an all-time high.

Palm oil: management expects CPO to range INR4,250-4,400 over the next couple of months, creeping up from February-March; Brent volatility and Malaysian inventory cited. PKO volatility lower than CPO.
Andhra Pradesh fruit price order for the new year not yet issued; last year's order assumed 20.01% OER; management hopes for a lower rate but cannot guide.
Dairy: no respite in milk prices for about two quarters (El Niño cattle productivity hit) plus structural value-added shift.
Broiler feed deliberately de-prioritised; management said it could have added thousands of tonnes given inflation.

qa_highlights.question: Oil palm plantation health in Andhra Pradesh after the drought and cyclones; is 10%+ FFB growth still achievable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said cyclones refilled soil water with no widespread tree damage; Q2 FFB grew double digits despite three extreme-heat months, and FY27 double-digit FFB growth stands.

qa_highlights.question: Contribution from the PKO derivatives plant and margin impact in FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Plant opened 1 September, so no meaningful Q2 contribution; meaningful impact from Q4 and scale-up in FY28, adding ~2 percentage points to oil palm EBITDA margin over 2-4 years.

qa_highlights.question: Outlook for palm oil prices and Andhra Pradesh OER pricing order?
qa_highlights.answer: CPO expected in INR4,250-4,400 range near term, rising from February-March if El Niño persists; AP order not yet out and management cannot guide on the outcome.

qa_highlights.question: Dairy pricing environment and any relief?
qa_highlights.answer: No relief for about two quarters: temporary El Niño-driven productivity loss plus a structural shift to value-added products that resets milk pricing.

qa_highlights.question: Update on FY27 PBT guidance and debt increase?
qa_highlights.answer: Double-digit PBT still chased but harder. Debt rose on deliberate inventory build ahead of inflation; working capital days cut to about 22 (cited); debt-to-equity about 0.8 and expected to stay around that level in H2.

qa_highlights.question: Poultry margin trajectory and dairy GTM revamp?
qa_highlights.answer: Dairy GTM simplification with an AM/PM distributor pilot in Chennai, with ~18 months of correction. Foods margins under pressure as B2C shift; EBITDA plus working media margin up 20bps to 5.8%.

risks_watch: El Niño impact on Rabi season and agchem demand (cotton, chilli); management expects a couple of years of structural correction in crop care and Astec.
Oil palm OER recovery from ~18.9% in Q2 toward 19.7%+ and the upcoming Andhra Pradesh fruit price order.
Palm and PKO price volatility tied to crude, biodiesel mandates and Malaysian inventories.
Dairy milk procurement costs with no price relief for about two quarters; heavy inflation across feed inputs.
Rising debt and inventory build; H2 cash release needed to hold debt-to-equity near 0.8.
Rising employee costs from sales transformation hires, annualising into FY28.
540743|2026-09.management_tone: Candid and cautious on the outlook: management said agchem is facing a structural correction and FY27 PBT growth is harder, while staying confident on oil palm volumes and the B2C foods shift. 540749|2026-03.headline: MAS Financial Q4 FY26 consolidated PAT rose 25% YoY to INR104 crore, with AUM at INR15,304 crore, up 19%.
540749|2026-03.overview: Consolidated PAT for Q4 FY26 was INR104 crore versus INR83 crore a year earlier, and full-year PAT was INR379 crore, up 21%. Standalone AUM grew 18.71% and standalone PAT grew 23.39% YoY in the quarter to around INR100 crore. Standalone net Stage 3 was 1.70%, slightly better than 1.72% in December 2025, while gross Stage 3 edged up to 2.57% from 2.56%. Cost of borrowing fell 42 bps YoY to 9.39%, and management guided to 9.20-9.25% over the next two to three quarters. Credit cost was elevated because of deliberate aggressive write-offs of 90+ DPD assets, which management said were funded from profit.

segments.name: Standalone MFSL - Micro-enterprise loans (MEL)
segments.commentary: AUM rose about 20% to INR5,737 crore from INR4,793 crore.

segments.name: Standalone MFSL - SME loans
segments.commentary: AUM grew 15.78% to INR5,213 crore from INR4,502 crore.

segments.name: Standalone MFSL - Two-wheeler
segments.commentary: AUM grew 35.43% to INR1,063 crore from INR785 crore; yields cited at 19-23%.

segments.name: Standalone MFSL - Commercial vehicle
segments.commentary: AUM grew 11% to INR1,085 crore from INR979 crore; growth being deliberately slowed for 1-2 quarters.

segments.name: Standalone MFSL - Salaried personal loan
segments.commentary: AUM grew around 22% to INR1,264 crore from INR1,040 crore.

segments.name: Housing finance subsidiary
segments.commentary: AUM rose 22.41% to INR940 crore from INR768 crore; Q4 PAT INR3.70 crore vs INR2.64 crore, net Stage 3 0.68%. Management aims for INR1,000 crore, now about a quarter later than planned.

guidance_outlook: AUM growth guided at 20-25% on a sustained basis; long-term target of INR1 lakh crore AUM by 2036.
Credit cost guided at 1-1.25% of closing AUM statistically, with management indicating about 1.25-1.3% on closing AUM, and up to about 1.5% in quarters with aggressive write-offs.
Cost-to-NII guided at 35-37%; ROA after opex and credit cost targeted at 2.75-3%.
Yield range-bound at 16-17%, expected to be sustained into FY27.
Cost of borrowing guided to fall from 9.39% to around 9.20-9.25% over the next 2-3 quarters.
Branch additions of 30-35 planned in FY27 after a year of consolidating existing branches.
Dividend: final dividend INR0.75 per share, total INR2 per share for FY26, about 10% payout.
Capital adequacy to be maintained at around 20%; debt tie-up for about half of FY27 done, full-year tie-up expected soon.
capex_capacity: More than 200 branches and about 16,500 centres; branch network to grow by 30-35 in FY27.
Average cash and cash equivalent balance of about INR1,000 crore plus unutilised cash credit of over INR200 crore.
Cash credit facility of about INR1,500 crore across 14 banks, utilised at 70-75%.
Sanctioned facilities over INR2,000 crore as of 31 March (term loans, NCDs, direct assignment, co-lending).
Term loan sanctioned pipeline of about INR1,300 crore; INR750 crore term loan raised in Q4 at 3-5 year tenor; INR100 crore NCDs raised in Q4.
Direct assignment of INR940 crore executed in Q4; a further INR500 crore+ of direct assignment and co-lending sanctions to be used in the current quarter.
demand_pricing: Direct sourcing is about 64% of the book; fintech partnerships are about 10% of business.
Yield rose about 40 bps sequentially, attributed to fintech mix and 2-wheeler growth; SME yields were also higher.
Management said assignment income is amortised, not upfront, and the NII rise was mainly from lower borrowing cost and the MCLR reset.
Standalone 90+ write-offs were aggressive in FY26 (more than 0.10% of assets), mostly unsecured per management.
Caution list added petrol pumps, gas agencies, transporters and some chemical industries in Feb-March 2026, alongside textile and agro, due to West Asia supply concerns.
Management reported no slowdown in disbursement growth as of the call.

qa_highlights.question: How is MAS using data and AI for risk-adjusted growth, and what early warning systems exist?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it back-tests risk models on its own repayment experience, not generic bureau scores; it moved from LOS to business rule engines and plans AI-based risk management after 6-9 months. Field checks included more than 2,000-3,000 commercial vehicle borrowers after the Middle East crisis, plus bounce data from 100% bank or e-NACH collections.

qa_highlights.question: Will the West Asia crisis and inflation affect lending and asset quality?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said asset quality should hold but is being watched closely; it is growing CV more slowly as an energy- and logistics-linked precaution. Disbursement growth has not slowed.

qa_highlights.question: Outlook for cost of borrowing and the Q4 cost of borrowing trend?
qa_highlights.answer: Cost of borrowing is 9.39% and is expected to fall to 9.20-9.25% over 2-3 quarters. Q4 interest expense was about INR222 crore vs INR219 crore in Q3, with the MCLR reset adding to NII.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the origination and fee cost high, and what is driving opex?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the fees and commission depend on product structure. Fintech partners get the spread as commission, and yields rose about 0.5%. Opex is judged against ROA, not in isolation.

qa_highlights.question: Why did credit cost rise and what is the normalised level?
qa_highlights.answer: The rise was from deliberate write-offs of 90+ DPD assets, not stress. Normal credit cost is 1-1.25% of closing AUM; 1.5% is possible in quarters with aggressive write-offs.

qa_highlights.question: Why is CV growth slow, and what is the write-off and recovery policy?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is slowing CV growth for 1-2 quarters due to logistics and transport risk. Write-offs occur after 360 days across all products; recoveries are credited to P&L net.

risks_watch: Rising inflation and energy costs from the West Asia crisis could hit logistics, transport and fuel-linked MSMEs.
Credit cost is a function of aggressive write-off policy; quarterly credit costs could run towards 1.5%.
Pricing may need to be passed on to borrowers if borrowing costs fall, which could compress the yield gain.
Housing finance subsidiary's INR1,000 crore AUM target now slips about a quarter.
Debt tie-up for FY27 is only about half complete; rate reduction depends on market conditions.
Gross Stage 3 is at 2.57%, up slightly QoQ.
540749|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on growth and profitability, with a clear 20-25% AUM growth target. Cautious on the macro, with CV growth slowed and sector caution lists expanded. Management was less direct on the split of NII growth and on the detail of the write-off strategy.
key_quotes: And on the asset side, we continue to have the confidence to grow anywhere between 20% to 25%, given the positive macro situation because we always prioritize risk management and profitability over just the growth.
So, we are at a striking distance away from INR1,000 crores.
We have cash credit facility of approximately INR1500 crore spread over 14 banks, of which we maintain utilization level of around 70 %-75%, keeping the remaining portion as liquidity buffer.
So, we do not upfront income in order to improve the profitability or the NII growth.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Cost of borrowing falling 14-19 bps (9.39% to 9.20-9.25%) with yields held at 16-17% should widen spread, though pass-through to borrowers and higher credit cost offset part of the gain.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Management plans 30-35 branch additions in FY27 on a base of more than 200 branches and about 16,500 centres, after a year of consolidation; no utilisation figure was given, so this is a planned branch rollout rather than capacity stress.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: AUM growth is guided at 20-25% sustained, consolidated AUM is up about 19% to INR15,304 crore, and disbursement growth showed no slowdown as of the call, with INR500 crore+ of assignment and co-lending sanctions queued for the current quarter.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex is not discussed as a balance-sheet event; the branch rollout is opex-led and utilisation is not disclosed, so no new capex announcement is signalled.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Cost of borrowing is guided down from 9.39% to 9.20-9.25% over 2-3 quarters, which supports NII, but pricing may be passed on to borrowers and the yield is held at 16-17%.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Credit cost is guided at 1-1.25% of closing AUM but could run to about 1.5% in quarters with aggressive write-offs, and gross Stage 3 edged up to 2.57% from 2.56%.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: No new product or model launch was discussed; the two-wheeler and SME lines are existing growth segments.

rows.label: Debt tie-up for FY27 about half complete
rows.why: Debt tie-up for about half of FY27 is done with full-year tie-up expected soon; the INR750 crore Q4 term loan and INR1,300 crore term-loan pipeline support the 20-25% AUM target, but rate relief depends on market conditions.

rows.label: Caution list expansion and CV growth slowdown
rows.why: CV AUM grew only 11% to INR1,085 crore and growth is being deliberately slowed for 1-2 quarters, with petrol pumps, transporters and other sectors added to the caution list due to West Asia supply concerns.

rows.label: Housing finance subsidiary to reach INR1,000 crore AUM
rows.when: about one quarter later than planned
rows.why: Housing AUM grew 22.41% to INR940 crore with Q4 PAT of INR3.70 crore vs INR2.64 crore, so the INR1,000 crore target is close and now slips about a quarter.

tone.note: Management was confident on 20-25% AUM growth, cost of borrowing falling to 9.20-9.25% and ROA of 2.75-3%, and cautious on the West Asia macro, CV slowdown and credit cost at up to 1.5% from aggressive write-offs; analysts pressed on opex, origination fees and the write-off and recovery policy.

540749|2026-06.headline: MAS Financial Q1 FY27: consolidated AUM up 21% to INR16,100 crores and PAT up 27% to INR110 crores; credit cost guided 1.25%-1.75%.
540749|2026-06.overview: Consolidated AUM grew about 21% YoY to INR16,100 crores and PAT rose about 27% to INR110 crores, with standalone PAT up 25% to INR105 crores. Asset quality was stable, with standalone GNPA at 2.58% and NNPA at 1.70%, flat QoQ, and a management overlay of INR17.60 crores held. Borrowing cost fell 55 bps YoY to 9.25%, while credit cost rose to about 1.6% of AUM, which management attributed to higher on-book mix, a 5 bps rise in Stage 1/2 provisioning and prudent write-offs. Management reiterated 20-25% AUM growth guidance, with the call leaning toward the upper end for FY27.

segments.name: MEL (Micro/MSME loans)
segments.commentary: Book grew 23% from INR5,009 crores to INR6,153 crores; MEL is about 77% of loan book combined with SME.

segments.name: SME loans
segments.commentary: Grew 21% from INR4,526 crores to INR5,485 crores.

segments.name: Two-wheeler loans
segments.commentary: Grew 19% from INR872 crores to INR1,039 crores; management said Q1 is seasonally muted, with festive Q3/Q4 stronger.

segments.name: Commercial vehicle (used CV)
segments.commentary: Grew 13% from INR967 crores to INR1,096 crores; eligible demand softer on fuel-cost-driven credit tightening, with growth push deferred 1-2 quarters.

segments.name: Salaried personal loans
segments.commentary: Grew 21% from INR1,131 crores to INR1,374 crores; about 9% of the loan book.

segments.name: Housing finance subsidiary
segments.commentary: AUM INR976 crores, GS3 0.98% and NS3 0.68%; PBT up 62% to INR5.70 crores; average yield about 14%, credit cost about 0.5%. Expansion into Tamil Nadu and Karnataka starts this quarter.

guidance_outlook: AUM growth guidance maintained at 20-25%, with management saying the full year is very likely to be at the higher end of the range.
Credit cost to stay in a 1.25%-1.75% range, depending on product mix; management pointed to commercial vehicles as high-yield, high-loss.
ROA target of 2.75%-3.25%, with an aspiration of 3%+.
Net interest margin target of 8%-8.5% on a 7%-7.5% spread; incremental borrowing cost 9.2%-9.25%, expected to stay stable (9.2%-9.3% per Q&A).
Direct distribution share (currently 66%-67%) expected to reach 70%-72% in 1-1.5 years; off-book target kept at 20-25% of AUM.
Used CV growth expected to pick up only after 1-2 quarters; housing finance AUM expected to inch up in the next few quarters.
Credit rating upgrade being pursued, timing not given; sub-9% borrowing cost called far-fetched in the next 1-2 quarters.
capex_capacity: Distribution of 16,500 centres through 209 branches, with more than 200 NBFC partners providing about 33% of originations; direct share 67%.
Employee count reduced by 380 in Q1 due to technology adoption; no quantified headcount target given.
In-house tech team of close to 100 people; LOS live for all products, with BRE added and straight-through processing improving.
Branches opened after March 2024 expected to mature (sweat) by 2027-28 or earlier.
demand_pricing: Standalone MSME/SME demand stable across manufacturing and trading; eligible demand fell in Q1 due to tighter credit screens on energy-dependent sectors (restaurants, gas-dependent manufacturing, export businesses).
Used CV demand robust, but eligible demand lower because of fuel-cost tightening.
Two-wheeler Q1 degrowth QoQ attributed to seasonality; monsoon and Gujarat floods flagged as temporary and not expected to cause major stress.
Working capital demand rising for some businesses on higher input costs; underwriting parameters also tightened.
Write-offs were INR29 crores in March and INR19 crores in June, offset by higher ECL provisioning, keeping impairment cost flat QoQ.

qa_highlights.question: Why did credit cost rise from about 1.2-1.3% to about 1.6% of AUM despite the microfinance impact and Q4 write-offs last year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited higher on-book assets (on-book up 8.25% QoQ vs AUM up 5.5%), which added INR6-7 crores of Stage 1/2 provisioning from a 5 bps rise to 0.7%. Prudent write-offs and mix shift toward higher-yield commercial vehicles also contributed; ROA not affected.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 20-25% growth guidance at risk given the West Asia conflict and energy-linked stress?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said energy-dependent segments were tightened early and stress was limited; eligible demand fell in Q1 and Q2 but normalised, and guidance is expected to hold with the upper end targeted.

qa_highlights.question: Will borrowing cost fall further from 9.25%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is hard to predict and depends on RBI and liquidity; the target is to stabilise at 9.2%-9.3%, with a credit rating upgrade being pursued.

qa_highlights.question: What is the reason for the Stage 1/2 provisioning increase and whether there are macro-related buffers?
qa_highlights.answer: Stage 1/2 provisioning rose to 0.7% from 0.65%, adding INR6-7 crores; management described it as a buffer.

qa_highlights.question: What was the nature of the INR10 crore OCPS redemption in the subsidiary MRHMFL?
qa_highlights.answer: The OCPS was refunded to the parent because the housing subsidiary's CRAR exceeded 37% and it did not need the capital.

qa_highlights.question: Why did off-book share fall and what is the housing finance growth plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Off-book is dynamic and chosen by price; target stays at 20-25%. Housing finance plans to expand into Tamil Nadu and Karnataka from Q1, with results expected in Q3-Q4.

risks_watch: Used CV: eligible demand softer on fuel-cost-driven credit tightening; management says growth push is 1-2 quarters away, and CV is high-yield, high-loss, so credit cost direction depends on mix.

Credit cost: rose to about 1.6% of AUM from about 1.2-1.3% a year earlier; management guides a 1.25%-1.75% range and Stage 1/2 provisioning went to 0.7% from 0.65% (INR6-7 crores), which management calls a buffer.
Energy-linked and West Asia stress: eligible demand fell in Q1 and Q2 and management says it has normalised; the next quarter will show whether this holds.
Borrowing cost: 9.25% average with incremental cost at 9.2%-9.3%; a sub-9% level is called far-fetched in the next 1-2 quarters, and the credit rating upgrade has no timing.

Off-book share fell below the 20%-25% target this quarter; management says it is opportunistic and the target is unchanged. Gujarat floods and monsoon effects on two-wheeler and collections are still unquantified.
key_quotes: So, very high possibility, yes. We are working on that quite optimistic. Can't predict, but you are thinking on the right lines.
So, that is the impact which translates to roughly around between INR5 crores to INR7 crores in provisioning.
Difficult to comment right now because the cost of borrowing is dependent on the macro situation.
So, currently, sub-9 immediately within next 1 or 2 quarters looks like a far -fetched assumption.
540749|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on headline growth, profitability and asset quality, with the 20%-25% AUM guidance reaffirmed and the upper end targeted. More cautious and non-committal on credit cost trajectory, borrowing cost, used CV recovery timing and the flood impact, where management repeatedly said it cannot yet predict or quantify.

rows.label: Direct distribution share rising to 70%-72%
rows.why: Direct share is 66%-67% now and management has guided to 70%-72% in 1-1.5 years, which supports spread and yield.

tone.note: Management was confident on 20%-25% AUM growth, PAT and asset quality (GNPA 2.58% flat QoQ), and cautious on credit cost trajectory, borrowing cost, used CV recovery and flood impact; analysts pushed on credit cost rising to about 1.6% and whether West Asia energy stress threatens guidance.

540749|2026-09.headline: MAS Financial Q2 FY27 consolidated AUM rose 23.3% to INR 17,042 crores; PAT grew about 26% to INR 115 crores.
540749|2026-09.overview: Consolidated AUM crossed INR 17,000 crores, up 23.3% YoY, and consolidated quarterly PAT was INR 115 crores, up about 26%. Standalone PAT was INR 110.05 crores (+22.7%) and standalone net Stage 3 was 1.70%, unchanged QoQ, while gross Stage 3 edged up to 2.63% from 2.58%. Management reiterated 20-25% AUM growth and a 2.75-3% ROA band, flagged an expected 20-25 bps rise in cost of borrowing as RBI hiked repo, and kept credit-cost buffers elevated. Analysts pressed on rising GNPA, wheels weakness, SME stress and yield compression; management attributed most of this to seasoning and product mix.

segments.name: MFSL standalone
segments.commentary: Gross Stage 3 2.63% (Q1: 2.58%), net Stage 3 1.70% (unchanged); management overlay of INR 17 crores not netted off. Standalone PBT INR 147.38 crores (+22.58%).

segments.name: MAS Rural Housing (subsidiary)
segments.commentary: AUM crossed INR 1,000 crores at INR 1,031.47 crores; Q2 PAT INR 4.62 crores (+54.71%). Gross Stage 3 0.99% (Q1: 0.98%), net Stage 3 0.70% (Q1: 0.68%); overlay INR 3.69 crores.

segments.name: MSME (MEL and SME)
segments.commentary: Flagship segment. Management said SME GNPA rose over the last three to four quarters due to book maturity; SME ticket size fell from about INR 35 lakh back to about INR 29 lakh, with a 6-12 quarter target of INR 35-45 lakh.

segments.name: Wheels (two-wheeler and commercial vehicle)
segments.commentary: Growth flattish; two-wheeler grew decently while CV growth is deliberately cautious. Wheels drove the uptick in 61-90 DPD and 91-120 DPD buckets. Wheels currently about 8-9% of AUM, targeted at 15-20% in 3-5 years.

segments.name: Salaried personal loans
segments.commentary: Capped at 10% of total AUM; management said current share is about 9%.

guidance_outlook: AUM growth guided at 20-25% YoY; management said H1 momentum should continue into H2 but growth could slow if opportunities are lacking.
ROA target maintained at 2.75-3%, despite margin pressure from rate hikes.
Cost of borrowing expected to rise 20-25 bps after repo hikes (25 bps done, another 25 bps expected in the year); analyst reconciled this to about 9.4-9.5%.
90+ DPD guided at 2.5-2.75% and net NPA below 2%.
Long-term aim of INR 1 lakh crore AUM by 2036; INR 20,000 crores AUM expected by year-end; medium-term INR 30,000-35,000 crores cited.
Branch count guided to rise from about 210 to around 300 over roughly two years; centres up about 1,000 in the last four to five quarters.
Off-book (direct assignment) share to be held at 20-25%, versus 17% currently; assignment range 20-22% indicated.
capex_capacity: Average on-balance-sheet liquidity about INR 1,000 crores; cash credit lines about INR 1,500 crores across 12 banks, utilised 80-85%.
Sanctions in hand exceed INR 2,500 crores; company said it is tied up for the full year.
Q2 long-term borrowing about INR 1,195 crores (term loans, NCDs INR 575 crores, ECB USD 25 million); sanctioned long-term lines about INR 1,500 crores.
Direct assignments of about INR 850 crores in Q2; a further INR 850 crores sanctioned for execution in Q3.
Lateral hubs opened in Mumbai and Delhi for senior hires in sales, underwriting, operations and technology.
demand_pricing: Management said credit demand remains strong; lower sanction rates are being offset by higher demand.
Analyst asked about drought in 5-6 states: about 10% of the portfolio sits in drought-declared states, but direct agri exposure is under 1%; management saw no SME stress yet.
Asset mix: about 65-70% fixed-rate, 30% floating; liabilities about 20% fixed, about 50% MCLR-linked (mostly 1-year), with the rest repo-linked and reset every 3 months.
Q2 yield on loans 16.08% vs 16.17% in Q1 (about 9 bps decline, attributed to product mix); analyst's 58 bps figure to be reconciled offline.
Distribution: direct about 68% of AUM, DSA/NBFC partners about 32%.

qa_highlights.question: Are drought-hit states causing SME cash-flow stress and what is the agri exposure?
qa_highlights.answer: Management sees no SME stress as demand is continuous and financials are reviewed; direct agri is under 1% and about 10% of the portfolio is in drought-declared states.

qa_highlights.question: What is the fixed vs MCLR split of borrowings and how will margins hold up?
qa_highlights.answer: Around 20% fixed (mainly capital market borrowings and some term loans), about 50% MCLR-linked mostly 1-year; margins to be protected by bargaining on spreads, repricing floating assets (about 30%) and short-tenure loans.

qa_highlights.question: Why is GNPA rising for 12 quarters and where will it stabilise?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited seasoning of the retail book (mix moved from 40/60 to 30/68), high-loss wheels and MSME stress over 1-1.5 years; 90+ DPD guided at 2.5-2.75%.

qa_highlights.question: Why does credit cost look high versus the asset-quality trend?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it deliberately built extra provisions in Stage 2 and Stage 3 this year as a buffer, which lifts credit cost without disturbing ROA; buffers may be released if NIM pressure is high and conditions normalise.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for wheels and CV growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Wheels growth flat; CV caution continues while distribution and manpower are rebuilt, with pickup expected in 2-3 quarters; the aim is to grow wheels to 15-20% of AUM in 3-5 years.

qa_highlights.question: Why has SME ticket size declined and what are the restrictions?
qa_highlights.answer: Ticket size fell from about INR 35 lakh to INR 29 lakh; management is cautious on import-export, transport/logistics and some metal businesses, with changes described as incremental.

risks_watch: Rising GNPA and wheels asset quality; gross Stage 3 rose to 2.63% and 61-120 DPD buckets increased.
Cost of borrowing rising 20-25 bps against a 2.75-3% ROA target; yield pressure with about 9 bps decline in Q2.
SME book maturing with rising GNPA; ticket-size volatility.
El Nino and drought exposure, with about 10% of the portfolio in drought-declared states.
Management is not chasing growth; it is open to slowing if opportunities fall short.
540749|2026-09.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on growth, funding and capital (22.12% CRAR), but defensive on asset quality and margins, repeatedly reframing rising GNPA and provisions as seasoning and deliberate buffers. Several answers were deferred offline (58 bps yield reconciliation, write-off figures).
key_quotes: We have a capital adequacy of more than 22% giving us sufficient room to grow further.
we plan our activities in such a manner that we can maintain the ROAs between 2.75% to 3%.
2.58% to 2.62% should not be reckoned as a deterioration in the quality, nor 2.62% to 2.55% should be considered as an improvement in the quality.
our aim is to reach INR 1Lakh crore AUM by 2036.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning

rows.label: Volume growth

rows.why: Sanctions above INR 2,500 crores are tied up for the full year, which supports the 20-25% AUM guide.

rows.why: Off-book share is 17% today with INR 850 crores of direct assignments sanctioned for Q3, and management committed to hold 20-25%.

rows.label: Spread defence and repricing of floating assets
rows.why: About 30% of assets are floating and management plans to protect margins by bargaining on spreads, but the 20-25 bps rise in borrowing cost is not yet offset.

540750|2026-03.headline: IEX Q4 FY26 consolidated PAT rose 10.8% YoY to INR 129.8 crore on record 39.4 billion units traded volume.
540750|2026-03.overview: IEX delivered record quarterly electricity volume of 39.4 billion units (up 24.3% YoY) and consolidated revenue of INR 196.4 crore (up 12.5%), with PAT up 10.8% to INR 129.8 crore. Full-year PAT rose 14.9% to INR 492.9 crore and a final dividend of INR 2 per share was declared. Exchange prices fell sharply on higher sell-side liquidity (DAM down 12.2% YoY in Q4), and other income dropped about 29% sequentially-adjusted per analyst, attributed to treasury mark-to-market losses in March. Market coupling (CERC draft of April 17, 2026 naming Grid India as MCO, comments till May 16) is the dominant overhang, with management disputing its benefit. Gas exchange (IGX) volumes fell 8% in Q4 on Middle East supply disruption and management expects no growth in Q1 FY27.

financial_highlights.value: INR 2 per share (200% of face value)

segments.name: Electricity - DAM/RTM
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 DAM price averaged INR 3.89/unit (down 12.2% YoY) and RTM INR 3.68/unit (down 15%) as DAM sell-bids rose about 49%. RTM was 39% of electricity volumes in FY26 (55 billion units, up about 41%).

segments.name: Green market (G-DAM)
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 green volume rose 26.5% to 2.4 billion units; FY26 volume 10.8 billion units (+23%).

segments.name: Renewable energy certificates (REC)
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 RECs traded 71.7 lakh (+6% YoY); FY26 187 lakh (+5%).

segments.name: IGX (gas exchange)
segments.commentary: Q4 volume down 8% on Middle East supply disruption; FY26 volume 76.8 million MMBtu (+28%); Q4 PAT INR 9.4 crore (+5.4%). Exchange holds about 3% of India's gas consumption and 20% of spot market.

segments.name: ICX (I-REC)
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 issued 46 lakh I-RECs (+29% YoY); FY26 179 lakh (over +200%). Q4 revenue INR 2.2 crore; FY26 INR 7.7 crore.

guidance_outlook: Management expects electricity volume growth of 15-20% annually to continue in FY27, dependent on demand-supply conditions.
IGX gas volumes expected flat YoY in Q1 FY27 and to grow from Q2 FY27 if Middle East supply normalises.
Coal exchange: draft Coal Regulations 2025 out; final regulations expected later in calendar 2026; board gave in-principle approval to explore setting up a coal exchange.
Management says market coupling would add no value and cost Grid India extra; IEX says it would absorb software changes at no extra cost.
Buyback under consideration; SEBI has not finalised the mechanism, and the company is awaiting SEBI's open-market route draft.
capex_capacity: IGX IPO process has been initiated; management says it is progressing well but did not give status detail.
PNGRB has given IGX until December 31, 2026 to complete the stake reduction.
Pending CERC approvals: TAM extension to 11 months, green RTM petition (reserved), and peak DAM/peak RTM segments for merchant storage (reserved).
BESS: 13 GW under first VGF tranche underway; about three-quarters of the 30 GW second tranche awarded.
SECI 500 MW / 3-hour RE CfD pilot (1,500 MWh/day), backed by a INR 76 crore stabilisation fund; applies to battery capacity per management.
demand_pricing: DAM sell liquidity rose about 44% for FY26; FY26 DAM average INR 3.86/unit (down about 14%) and RTM INR 3.59/unit (down 16%).
More than 70% of cleared volume is now through the API system; management says over 5,000 industrial consumers use the platform.
Management says exchange customer count is rising and no customers have been lost to rival exchanges since the July 2025 coupling order.
Management sees the TAM segment (uniform liquidity across three exchanges) as evidence that transaction fees (about INR 0.036-0.037/unit) would hold up under coupling.
VPPA interest is currently limited, per management; data centres and multinationals could add demand later.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other income fall about 29% versus the recent quarterly run rate?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO Vineet Harlalka said the December quarter included a one-time treasury gain, and March saw mark-to-market losses from the Iran conflict and rupee weakness. He expects the numbers to recover as markets recover.

qa_highlights.question: What is the timeline for the final PMR and market coupling procedure?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it cannot estimate; PMR 2021 was notified in February 2021 after a 2019 draft, and the regulator will consider comments and market redesign.

qa_highlights.question: Would IEX lose volumes and margins if market coupling goes through?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said customer loyalty and value-added services would retain share; cited TAM margins holding at about INR 0.036-0.037/unit despite shared liquidity. No additional software cost is expected.

qa_highlights.question: Is RTM coupling feasible, given 48 auctions a day?
qa_highlights.answer: Management doubts RTM coupling is feasible: it would move from 48 to 288 five-minute blocks with no slack time, and an aggregation failure at one exchange could cause price jerks.

qa_highlights.question: What is the buyback stance?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said a buyback is a good option after the revised tax structure; the company is considering it and awaiting SEBI's open-market route decision.

qa_highlights.question: Will electricity volume growth continue in FY27 and why did REC volumes fall?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects 15-20% volume growth. On RECs, management said there was no fall: REC volume rose 5% in FY26.

risks_watch: Market coupling: CERC draft (April 17, 2026) names Grid India as MCO; comments close May 16, 2026, and the timeline for final rules is unknown.
Gas exchange volumes weak in Q1 FY27 on Middle East supply disruption and high gas prices.
Treasury and other income volatility from mark-to-market swings (other income fell in Q4).
Continued DAM/RTM price decline (down 12-15% YoY in Q4) could pressure fee income if volumes do not offset.
Pending CERC approvals (TAM 11-month extension, green RTM, peak DAM/RTM) and the legal challenge to market coupling.
540750|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on operating volumes and the value of customer relationships, but evasive on market coupling timelines and outcomes, saying it was too early to call. Cautious on Q1 FY27 gas volumes and on the other income decline, which management attributed to non-recurring factors.
key_quotes: And I'm sure in the time to come, almost everybody will do the bidding through the API system.
So I have my own doubts about coupling in the RTM market.
We have more than 5,000 industrial consumers who are using with us.
Quantum in that is not significant. So the revenue share is not meaningful.

rows.why: DAM price fell 12.2% and RTM 15% YoY in Q4 as sell-bids rose about 49%, and other income fell about 29% sequentially-adjusted, so fee pricing and treasury income are both pressured.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management guides 15-20% electricity volume growth for FY27 after Q4 volume of 39.4 billion units (+24.3% YoY) and RTM +48.2%, though IGX is flat in Q1 FY27 on Middle East disruption.

rows.why: Exchange is asset-light with no utilisation or capacity constraint discussed; the only capital moves are a buyback under consideration and an IGX IPO, not a capex plan.

rows.why: Electricity volume guided at 15-20% growth for FY27 after Q4 volume rose 24.3% YoY, and IGX growth is expected from Q2 FY27 if Middle East supply normalises.

rows.why: IGX volume is guided flat in Q1 FY27 after an 8% Q4 decline, and DAM/RTM prices fell 12.2%/15% YoY in Q4 while other income dropped sharply on March mark-to-market losses.

rows.why: Pending CERC approvals for green RTM and peak DAM/RTM segments (reserved) and a TAM 11-month extension could open new products, but timing depends on the regulator.

rows.why: CERC draft of April 17, 2026 has comments till May 16, but management cannot estimate the final timeline and PMR 2021 took about two years from draft to notification, so the outcome is a major overhang on volumes and fees.

rows.why: Buyback is under consideration pending SEBI's open-market route draft, and PNGRB gave IGX until December 31, 2026 to complete its stake reduction, with the IPO process initiated.

rows.why: Coal Regulations final rules are expected later in calendar 2026, and the 13 GW BESS first VGF tranche is underway with about three-quarters of the 30 GW second tranche awarded, but no IEX contracts are quantified.
