540750|2026-06.headline: IEX Q1 FY27 consolidated PAT rose about 12% to Rs 134.8 crore on Rs 202.8 crore revenue, with electricity volume up 16% to 37.5 billion units.
540750|2026-06.overview: IEX reported Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue of Rs 202.8 crore and PAT of Rs 134.8 crore, up about 12% YoY, on electricity volume of 37.5 billion units (+16%). Real-Time Market growth was the main driver, with RTM up about 25% in Q1 and its share of mix reaching about 34% last year. Management used the analyst meet to push a set of new products (Green RTM, peak contracts, 11-month TAM, carbon trading, coal exchange) while pushing back on CERC's proposed market coupling and the Day-Ahead Market pilot, which it has challenged at APTEL and the Supreme Court. The call was mostly a policy and product narrative; no formal FY27 guidance was given.

segments.name: Electricity (DAM / RTM / TAM)
segments.commentary: RTM is now roughly the size of DAM; DAM share of mix fell from 95% in FY16 to about 39%, RTM rose to about 34% in FY26, and RTM is up about 25% in Q1 FY27. Term-Ahead Market and Green Market are about 7-8% of the mix.

segments.name: IGX (gas exchange, associate)
segments.commentary: FY26 volume 76.8 million MMBtu and PAT Rs 42 crore; Q1 FY27 volume 27.5 million MMBtu and PAT Rs 16 crore. DRHP filed for IPO of a 22.3% stake to bring IEX's 47.3% holding down to 25% under PNGRB rules, after a one-year extension.

segments.name: ICX (I-REC / environmental)
segments.commentary: Sole I-REC issuer in India; management cited about 200% growth in I-REC volumes last year. Q1 REC volumes were down sharply YoY, which management attributed to the first quarter and possible RPO buy-out confusion.

segments.name: Indian Coal Exchange (new)
segments.commentary: Incorporated as a separate company in June 2026; coal rules notified 4 June 2026 require e-auction and marketplace trades to move to exchanges within six months of launch. Market size cited at about 120 million tonnes today, with a target of at least 100 million tonnes in year one.

guidance_outlook: No formal FY27 volume or revenue guidance given; management expects RTM volumes to grow about 25-30% a year.
Management expects carbon credit trading to begin in FY27, with BEE targeting 1 October 2026.

Management expects the Green RTM, peak-power contracts (DAM and RTM) and 11-month TAM products to be approved by CERC; timing was not committed, and the 11-month TAM application has been pending for over two years.
Management sees the exchange-routed share of electricity rising to about 25% over five to six years, against about 14-15% short-term market today.
Management said it would consider a buyback in future, citing SEBI's revised market-buyback rules.
Management said the coal exchange's fee should exceed those of MSTC and M-Junction, since exchanges perform price discovery, clearing and settlement.
capex_capacity: Management cited about 80 GW of thermal capacity in the pipeline, 41 GW under construction with PPAs signed, 20 GW awarded, and 16 GW in planning; most is expected in FY31-FY33.
Management said it has built a hot standby for RTM and a DC-to-DR switch; both were positioned as ready for the proposed 5-minute bidding window.

BESS merchant capacity cited: ACME about 3,200 MWh, Juniper about 500 MWh, Adani about 3,400 MWh, with more than Rs 9,000 crore of BESS VGF support. Management said the arbitrage window may last 3-5 years.
The SECI 500 MW CfD pilot for peak power was cited as launched; it is a peak-power product, not solar.
demand_pricing: Management expects demand growth of about 5-5.5% a year, versus 11% in Q1 FY27 on heat and delayed monsoon. Peak demand touched about 271 GW in May and July.
Management said exchanges as a group grew 18% in FY26 against 1% demand growth.

On market coupling, CERC proposed Grid India as Market Coupling Operator, with DAM first. Management said it has challenged the July 2025 order at APTEL (order dated 13 February 2026) and is now before the Supreme Court; a second hearing was held on 27 July 2026.
Management said that even after coupling, DAM share could fall 20-40%, but said business impact would not be significant. The market-share loss figure is management's own estimate.
Management said top-10 sellers account for about 40% of the sell side and the top-buyer concentration is 50-60%, with 800-900 participants daily.

Management cited an RTM realisation issue in a Q&A: an analyst's per-unit realisation calculation (about 0.4 paisa vs 3.7 paisa a year earlier) was not reconciled; management pointed to incentives in REC and TAM.

financial_highlights.change: about 11% QoQ per management; YoY not stated

qa_highlights.question: What RTM share of the mix to expect over the next 3-5 years, and what could be the next star product after RTM (peak contracts, Green RTM, BESS)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said RTM has grown about 30-35% CAGR since 2020 and expects RTM volumes to keep growing 25-30% a year, possibly exceeding DAM volumes over time; it named BESS as a potential next growth product. No numeric RTM share target was given.

qa_highlights.question: Will IEX pursue a buyback given low valuations, and can IEX shareholders get a reservation in the IGX IPO?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said an IGX IPO reservation for IEX shareholders is not really possible as it is an independent IPO. It said a buyback will be considered in future, since SEBI has revised the rules for market buybacks.

qa_highlights.question: Why has RTM grown to near DAM size in India, unlike in Europe where DAM dominates?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to 25-year PPAs covering about 85% of DISCOM demand, with DAM used for seasonal and daily shortfalls and RTM used to handle renewable variability; it said PPAs will persist because banks lend only against them.

qa_highlights.question: How far can exchange share of electricity grow given long-term PPAs dominate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said exchange-routed share could reach about 25% of generation in five to six years, versus about 14-15% in the short-term market today, as bilateral and trader transactions shrink.

qa_highlights.question: Who bears the cost of Grid India as Market Coupling Operator, and will MCO fees force IEX to cut fees?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said all costs are ultimately passed to consumers, directly or indirectly, and that cost allocation and fee questions are among the open issues Grid India has raised with CERC; no timeline or answer was given.

qa_highlights.question: What is the likely timeline for final market coupling regulations, and what is the expected DAM market-share loss?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give a timeline, citing the need to examine software, settlement and reliability, and compared it to availability-based tariff taking years. On share loss, management said it sees no material loss given customer integration, though it earlier estimated DAM share could fall 20-40%.

qa_highlights.question: Does the market coupling challenge affect CERC approval of the new products?
qa_highlights.answer: Goel said the legal challenge is against the order, not CERC, and that regulators and government are aligned on peak power products. He said delays are due to procedural hurdles and the products will be released over time.

qa_highlights.question: Why did REC volumes fall about 80% YoY and QoQ, and why is standalone realisation per unit down sharply?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 is early in the year and that a draft allowing RPO buy-out has created market confusion, which will lift REC volumes once clarified. On realisation, management pointed to incentives in REC and Term-Ahead Market and did not reconcile the 0.4 paisa vs 3.7 paisa comparison.

qa_highlights.question: What is the long-duration 11-month Term-Ahead contract timeline, given the application is over two years old?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is difficult to say when approval will come, as CERC is reviewing performance of the existing 3-month contracts and standardising longer contracts, and that contracts beyond 3 months are currently not significant in volume.

qa_highlights.question: How does the 0.3% social welfare gain claim and DAM coupling risk relate to customer concentration, and what is the buyer/seller concentration?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said top-10 sellers account for about 40% of the sell side, buyer concentration is about 50-60% of volume, and 800-900 participants trade daily; it said concentration on the buy side has been falling.

qa_highlights.question: Why are sell bids in daytime far above cleared volumes, and is solar being curtailed in the exchange?
qa_highlights.answer: Rohit said about 10,000-12,000 MW clears in daytime, of which solar is only about 2,000-3,000 MW, and curtailment is mainly thermal, not solar; solar has not reached the stage of curtailment on the exchange.

qa_highlights.question: How long will BESS arbitrage last and are two cycles per year feasible?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said two cycles are possible on 100-150 days, mainly in winter, and that arbitrage may last 3-5 years, with no definitive model; it cited FY26 arbitrage of Rs 4.81 per cycle versus Rs 5.03 in FY25 and Rs 3.80 in FY24.

risks_watch: Timing of CERC approval for Green RTM, peak power contracts and 11-month TAM; orders reserved, and the 11-month TAM application has been pending over two years.
Market coupling: Supreme Court hearing (second hearing 27 July 2026), Grid India's objections to MCO design, and management's own 20-40% DAM share-loss estimate.
Proposed RTM window cut from 15 to 5 minutes and gate closure from 75 to 50 minutes, which could reduce liquidity or affect bidding systems.
Q1 FY27 REC volume decline and a draft RPO buy-out rule that could change REC demand; realisation per unit fell sharply in the analyst's calculation and was not reconciled.
Coal exchange: registration and licensing under way, six-month transition away from e-auction, and competition from MSTC and M-Junction; fee levels not yet set.
IGX IPO (22.3% stake sale) and PNGRB stake dilution from 47.3% to 25%; IGX Q1 PAT of Rs 16 crore needs to hold.
key_quotes: And I am sure with the kind of trust which we have built over the years in these last 18 years, we should be able to retain significant market share even in the Day-Ahead Market.
So, as far as business is concerned, I do not think it is going to be significant.
So, it will be difficult for me to give any timeline on this , I can only tell you one thing that sometime in 1994-95 when availability--based tariff was first discussed in the country.
The IGX IPO is an independent IPO, but buyback, yes definitely, we will consider it in future because now SEBI also has revised its rules for doing the buyback through the market.
540750|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on growth drivers, RTM and BESS arbitrage, and the view that market coupling will have limited business impact. Noticeably cautious and non-committal on timelines for CERC approvals, market coupling regulations, the 11-month TAM contract, and the buyback, and openly declined several numeric questions.

rows.why: No new exchange capacity was discussed; the brief cites hot standby and DC-to-DR switch already built for RTM, and the 80 GW thermal pipeline is a demand backdrop, not IEX capacity to come live in the window.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Q1 FY27 electricity volume rose 16% YoY to 37.5 billion units and RTM grew about 25%; management expects RTM volumes to grow 25-30% a year, though this is a CEO gut-feel view, not guidance.

rows.why: Capex and utilisation were not discussed for IEX; the brief gives no utilisation figure for the exchange.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: No formal FY27 guidance was given, and the brief's main pending items (CERC approvals, market coupling) are unresolved, so there is no basis for an upgrade in the window.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade

rows.label: New product launch

rows.label: Market coupling (CERC MCO, DAM first) and Supreme Court challenge
rows.why: Second Supreme Court hearing held 27 July 2026, no CERC timeline given, and management's own estimate puts DAM share loss at 20-40%, though it says impact would not be significant.

rows.label: Carbon credit trading start in FY27

rows.label: IGX IPO (22.3% stake) and buyback consideration

540750|2026-09.headline: IEX Q2 FY27 revenue rose 10.7% YoY to INR203 crore and PAT 12.9% to INR139 crore, on 39.7 billion units traded (+12.7% YoY).
540750|2026-09.overview: IEX reported Q2 FY27 revenue of INR203 crore (up 10.7% YoY) and PAT of INR139 crore (up 12.9% YoY), with electricity volume of 39.7 billion units. A weak monsoon and record power demand pushed DAM and RTM prices up sharply, shifting volume toward RTM and bilateral/TAM contracts. IGX volumes and profit grew strongly, and IGX is preparing an IPO as it cuts its stake to 25%. Management said the market coupling timeline is likely 1.5 to 2 years away and that a buyback is under evaluation.

financial_highlights.value: ~16.5 billion units (Q2 FY27), ~42% share of IEX volume

financial_highlights.change: +144% YoY from INR9.6 crore; H1 FY27 INR39.7 crore, +67.4%
+38.4% YoY in Q2; +15% YoY in H1

segments.name: Day-Ahead Market (DAM)
segments.commentary: Average DAM price rose about 46% YoY to INR5.72/unit in Q2 FY27 as buy bids grew nearly 120% YoY; DAM volume growth was described as sluggish. Management says DAM volume has grown only 2-5% CAGR since 2020.

segments.name: Real-Time Market (RTM)
segments.commentary: Average RTM price rose 49% YoY to INR5.24/unit. RTM volume was about 16.5 billion units (~42% share), with a record single-day volume of 315 million units in September.

segments.name: Term-Ahead Market (TAM)
segments.commentary: Market share about 35%. Roughly 70%+ of TAM volume is daily/weekly/monthly contracts and under 30% is intraday (DAC/ITD). Volume rose in Q2 as buyers secured power during the weak monsoon.

segments.name: IGX (gas exchange)
segments.commentary: Volume +160% YoY to 42 million MMBtu; about 30% from the power sector. PAT INR23.4 crore. IPO process on track; stake must fall from 47.3% to 25% by December 2026 under PNGRB rules.

segments.name: ICX (I-REC registry)
segments.commentary: Issued 52 lakh I-RECs in Q2 (+38.4% YoY); revenue INR2.3 crore. Management guides ICX revenue growth of 20-25%.

segments.name: Renewable Energy Certificates (REC)
segments.commentary: REC volume fell to 15.3 lakh certificates from 44 lakh YoY. Management says RECs are no longer a significant revenue driver; prices around INR310-330, and the buyout option caps value at about INR0.35.

guidance_outlook: IEX volume growth expected at about 15% for FY27, in line with the 14-15% trend.
IGX volume growth guided at 40-50% YoY for FY27, with a reasonably good second half expected.
ICX revenue growth guided at 20-25%.
Market coupling is not expected in calendar 2026; management estimates 1.5 to 2 years after final regulations are notified.
Management is evaluating a share buyback and other options for surplus cash, with no decision announced.
capex_capacity: IGX IPO on track; IGX must lower its holding from 47.3% to 25% by end-December 2026 per PNGRB rules.
Indian Coal Exchange Limited (wholly owned subsidiary) applied for a licence with the Coal Controller Organisation in September 2026.
Mineral exchange regulations notified by the Ministry of Mines; IEX is exploring this opportunity.
Management cited about 80 GW of thermal capacity under construction and 43 GW of VGF-awarded BESS, with battery capacity expected above 100 GW by 2032.
CEA draft proposes co-located storage (2-hour, then 4-hour from 2029) for new solar and wind projects, with 10% of installed capacity.
demand_pricing: Q2 FY27 power demand rose a record 11.5% YoY to 502 billion units; H1 demand grew 10.2% to 897 billion units.
Prices reached about INR20/unit in some time blocks; RTM prices fell near zero in some blocks late in the quarter as cyclones and rains cut demand.
Management says DAM/RTM prices corrected to about INR4/unit by end-October, with volumes returning to DAM and RTM.
Market share in DAM and RTM is 99%+ (management cited 99.2-99.3%).
Transaction fee is the same for DAM and RTM. DISCOMs are about 80% of buy-side volume.

qa_highlights.question: Why is there no movement on the CERC market coupling draft regulations, and when will final rules come?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no hurry and no timeline; implementation would take 1.5 to 2 years after notification, and not in calendar 2026.

qa_highlights.question: Why did DAM grow slowly while TAM and RTM grew faster?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said tight evening supply led DISCOMs to shift to bilateral contracts during the monsoon. Prices have since corrected to about INR4/unit, and DAM and RTM volumes are recovering.

qa_highlights.question: What is the split of TAM volume?
qa_highlights.answer: Daily and monthly contracts are over 70% of TAM volume; intraday (DAC/ITD) is under 30%.

qa_highlights.question: How much of FY26 REC volume came from designated consumers?
qa_highlights.answer: About 80% of FY26 REC volume came from large DISCOMs and C&I buyers; some may return if prices fall another 10-15%.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Supreme Court or APTEL case against the market coupling order proceed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said IEX is not aggrieved yet because coupling needs final regulations; IEX can challenge those regulations.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capital return plan given the surplus cash and low share price?
qa_highlights.answer: The company has paid about 60-65% of profit as dividend. A buyback is under evaluation after tax changes, with the board yet to decide.

qa_highlights.question: Would coupling shift DAM buyers to RTM on other exchanges?
qa_highlights.answer: Management does not expect buyers to leave IEX and said shifts between DAM and RTM are driven by price and availability, not coupling.

risks_watch: Market coupling timeline, with the RTM gate-closure reduction (75 to 50 minutes) under CERC discussion making coupling harder in RTM.
Designated consumers have largely stopped buying RECs under the buyout option, so REC volume may stay weak.
Treasury income depends on float (settlement and margin money), which management does not control; treasury yield is currently 15-18%.
IGX IPO and the stake reduction to 25% by December 2026.
Coal stocks around 8 days, with about 100 plants at a critical 3-day level, which could drive price volatility.
Pending CERC approvals for TAM extension to 11 months, Green RTM and Peak DAM/RTM products.
540750|2026-09.management_tone: Confident on volume growth and the structural RTM and storage story, but cautious on market coupling timing ("no hurry", "not in this calendar year"). Evasive on buyback timing and surplus-cash deployment, saying only that options are being evaluated.
key_quotes: So RTM market volumes are growing at a significant rate, and with high renewable, I am very sure that RTM market volume will further continue to increase.
It is difficult to say any definite timeline about it, but definitely not in this calendar year.
Buyback, yes, the price is low and we will definitely consider this option also.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Exchange is asset-light with no physical capacity plans; growth rests on volume (about 15% FY27 guide) and no new plant, branch or line was announced, so capacity-driven growth is not a trigger.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management guides about 15% IEX electricity volume growth for FY27, in line with the 14-15% trend, with H1 FY27 volume at 77 billion units (+14.2% YoY) and IGX volume guided at 40-50% YoY.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: No utilisation figure is given and the company is asset-light; a buyback is under evaluation and surplus cash is building, so capital deployment rather than capex is the likely announcement.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Q2 revenue rose 10.7% and PAT 12.9% YoY with IGX PAT +144%, but management guided only about 15% volume growth with no upgrade stated, so an upgrade depends on prices holding.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: DAM/RTM prices spiked to INR5.2-5.7 and then corrected to about INR4/unit by end-October, and RTM prices fell near zero in some blocks, so the price-driven revenue lift could reverse.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: CERC approvals are pending for TAM extension to 11 months, Green RTM and Peak DAM/RTM products, but no launch date was given.

rows.label: IGX IPO and stake cut to 25%
rows.why: IGX must cut IEX's holding from 47.3% to 25% by end-December 2026 under PNGRB rules, and the IPO process is on track.

rows.label: Share buyback under evaluation
rows.why: Management is evaluating a buyback after tax changes, with no decision yet, and dividends already take about 60-65% of profit.

rows.label: Market coupling delayed
rows.why: Management says coupling needs final regulations and would take 1.5 to 2 years after notification, so it is not a trigger in the window.

tone.note: Management was confident on 15% volume growth, IGX 40-50% growth and the RTM/storage story, but cautious on market coupling timing and evasive on buyback timing; analysts pressed on coupling, DAM slowness and capital return.

540755|2026-03.headline: GIC Re FY26 profit after tax rose 25.23% to INR8,392.18 crores, with combined ratio down 2.79 points to 106.02%.
540755|2026-03.overview: GIC Re reported FY26 gross premium of INR44,006.74 crores, up from INR41,153.95 crores, and PAT of INR8,392.18 crores. Q4 PAT rose to INR2,254.24 crores from INR2,182.88 crores, while Q4 investment income fell to INR3,059.46 crores from INR3,903.02 crores. Management said the global market is moving from hardening to a competitive phase, with April 1 domestic renewals and January 1 international renewals showing price pressure. Management guided to a 1-2 point combined ratio improvement in FY27 and expects low single-digit growth.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR10,367 crores in Q4 FY25
vs INR3,903.02 crores in Q4 FY25

financial_highlights.metric: Adjusted combined ratio (incl. policyholders' investment income), FY26

financial_highlights.change: vs INR2,922.66 crores in Q4 FY25

financial_highlights.change: vs INR83,224.33 crores at prior year-end

segments.name: Domestic business
segments.commentary: Accounts for 75% of FY26 gross premium (INR32,979.23 crores). Domestic combined ratio was cited at around 101-102%, an improvement of roughly 250 bps versus FY25 per an analyst's reading; property is about 30% of the domestic book.

segments.name: International business
segments.commentary: FY26 gross premium of INR11,027.51 crores. Motor international is shrinking due to pruning (US contract ended; Israel and Turkey proportional treaties reduced), with claims running off more slowly than premium. Property results improving since it has no long tail.

segments.name: Motor
segments.commentary: About 83% of motor portfolio is domestic and about 60% of that domestic portion is obligatory. Domestic motor growth came from additional domestic treaties; international motor premium has degrown over three years.

segments.name: Health
segments.commentary: More than 99% domestic. Proportional treaties; some reserve strengthening under way, results described as fairly stable. Management is cautious on government schemes.

segments.name: Fire
segments.commentary: Q4 fire premium decline of around 20% was attributed to international portfolio; management said the quarter alone may not reflect the full year. Domestic fire will not grow at April 1 renewals.

guidance_outlook: FY27 combined ratio targeted to improve by 1-2 percentage points year-on-year; management said it would prefer to hold or improve on the FY26 106% level.
FY27 growth expected to be low single-digit; management said it would not chase premium in a soft market.
Obligatory share of 4% declared for GIC Re for FY26-27; management flagged possible glide-path pressure on obligatory share over time.
Solvency will be used for impending RBC and IFRS transitions; dividend payout raised to 13.25%, about 32.5% higher than earlier.
capex_capacity: Solvency ratio improved to 4.21 at year-end from 3.70, which management said supports capital deployment and the RBC and IFRS transitions.
Net worth excluding fair value change grew to INR51,301.27 crores from INR43,106.52 crores.
demand_pricing: April 1 domestic renewals were pressured by competition and softening fire pricing; GIC Re used reinsurance levers (proportional structures) so the first impact is borne by insurers. Contracts above a threshold were declined.
New entrants: multiple IFSC insurance offices in GIFT City and two domestic reinsurers set up just before 1 April, increasing competition.
International 1 January renewals: market in soft cycle beyond the 2023-24 hardening, with ample capital and benign cat seasons; reinsurers still holding discipline on coverage and retentions.
Crop: new 3-year tender cycle not yet in place; burn-cost model expected to be more prevalent for FY27; only 1-2 treaties concluded so far.

qa_highlights.question: How did April renewal pricing go, and do the two new domestic reinsurers affect obligatory or domestic-preferred business?
qa_highlights.answer: Pricing was pressured by competition and capacity, but GIC Re retained key relationships and declined contracts beyond thresholds; growth fell short of goals. Obligatory 4% is declared for FY26-27; management expects any new player to need a track record, but a glide path is possible.

qa_highlights.question: Can domestic combined ratio hold at around 101-102% in a soft market?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it can hold, with property (30% of book) under pressure but agriculture and health approached cautiously. The objective is a 1-2 point improvement.

qa_highlights.question: Will FY27 growth be low single digit and combined ratio improve 1-2 points?
qa_highlights.answer: Management agreed low single-digit growth is likely. It confirmed a 1-2 point year-on-year combined ratio improvement target, with more improvement possible in foreign business.

qa_highlights.question: Why is motor profitability weak despite strong growth, and what drove the Q4 fire decline?
qa_highlights.answer: Domestic motor growth came from new treaties; international motor is degrowing after pruning (US contract, Israel and Turkey treaties), so claims are running off slower than premium. Fire Q4 decline is from international; full-year view may be overstated by a single quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for health and April fire renewals?
qa_highlights.answer: Health has reserve strengthening but results are stable; more than 99% is domestic and government-scheme exposure is being handled cautiously. Domestic fire will not grow at April 1, offset by health, agriculture and domestic motor.

qa_highlights.question: Capital: will high solvency allow higher dividend, and how does the RBC transition affect it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management stated a 13.25% payout, about 32.5% higher than earlier, and said solvency will be used toward the RBC and IFRS transitions.

risks_watch: Softening in domestic fire and international property; new domestic reinsurers and IFSC offices raising competition.
International motor claims run-off lagging premium decline, keeping motor combined ratio elevated.
Possible glide path in the obligatory share, which currently stands at 4% for FY26-27.
Crop reinsurance volumes depend on how states choose between cup-and-cap and burn-cost models under the new tender cycle.
Investment income fell sharply in Q4 (INR3,059.46 crores vs INR3,903.02 crores), reducing support to earnings.
540755|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on FY26 results and capital, but cautious and somewhat defensive on FY27 growth, fire pricing and motor profitability. Management repeatedly framed softer premium as deliberate discipline rather than lost business.
key_quotes: So yes, our capital solvency is very high, and we are giving a dividend payout of 13.25%, which is 32% -- 32.5% more than what we have given earlier.
It can hold up because property is 30% of our book, wherein we -- as we mentioned, that we did that balancing act and there could be pressure on the combined ratio there.
And therefore, on the international side, there is a degrowth. But the degrowth impact is immediately seen on the portfolio.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management guides low single-digit (possibly single-digit) growth and won't chase premium in a soft market, after FY26 gross premium rose only 6.9% (INR44,006.74 crores vs INR41,153.95 crores).

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex was not discussed; the call instead centres on deploying solvency (4.21 vs 3.70) toward RBC and IFRS transitions and a higher 13.25% dividend payout, not new capacity.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: The soft global market is moving from hardening to competition, with April 1 domestic and January 1 international renewals showing price pressure, so management is not positioned to raise guidance.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Fire premium fell about 20% in Q4 and Q4 investment income dropped to INR3,059.46 crores from INR3,903.02 crores, while international motor claims run off slower than premium and the obligatory share faces possible glide-path pressure.

rows.label: Soft market pricing pressure at April 1 and January 1 renewals
rows.why: Management described the global market moving from hardening to a competitive phase, with April 1 domestic renewals pressured by competition and softening fire pricing, and new entrants (two domestic reinsurers and multiple GIFT City IFSC offices) adding competition.

rows.label: RBC and IFRS transitions funded by solvency
rows.why: Solvency ratio rose to 4.21 from 3.70 and management said it will be used for the impending RBC and IFRS transitions, alongside a dividend payout raised to 13.25%, about 32.5% higher than before.

rows.label: Obligatory share glide path risk
rows.why: Obligatory share is declared at 4% for FY26-27, but management flagged possible glide-path pressure, and domestic motor is about 60% obligatory of the 83% domestic motor book.

tone.note: Management was confident on FY26 profit (PAT up 25.23% to INR8,392.18 crores) and capital (solvency 4.21), but cautious on FY27 growth, fire pricing and international motor run-off; analysts pushed on whether domestic combined ratio can hold at 101-102% and on the low single-digit growth outlook.

540755|2026-06.headline: GIC Re Q1 FY27 combined ratio improved to 104.88% from 106.94%, with PAT of INR1,922.04 crores and solvency at 4.32.
540755|2026-06.overview: GIC Re reported Q1 FY27 gross premium of INR13,475.36 crores, up from INR12,388.01 crores a year earlier, and PAT of INR1,922.04 crores on PBT of INR2,490.25 crores. Incurred claim ratio fell to 85.04% from 90.42% and combined ratio improved to 104.88% from 106.94%. Investment income dipped to INR3,265.51 crores from INR3,313.74 crores. Management flagged soft global pricing, a provisional INR440 crores for the Gujarat floods, and continued pruning of the foreign book, which declined about 6% in the quarter.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR12,388.01 crores in Q1 FY26 (about +8.8%)
vs INR3,313.74 crores in Q1 FY26

financial_highlights.value: INR157,800 crores, of which equity about INR58,000 crores
financial_highlights.change: fixed income about 73.4%, equity about 17%, money market about 8.67%

segments.name: Domestic
segments.commentary: Domestic combined ratio was about 107.5% in Q1, versus the roughly 102-103% range management cited as typical; domestic motor deteriorated on legacy treaties. Growth was about 12.3%, led by non-property lines and retail health.

segments.name: Foreign / international
segments.commentary: Foreign book declined about 6% YoY; management is repricing motor, aviation and overseas cargo, with property the largest exposure. Overseas combined ratio improved sharply in Q1, but management said one quarter is not representative given seasonality.

segments.name: Life reinsurance
segments.commentary: Life book grew meaningfully and is held at about a 20% market share; management said the portfolio is still loss-making and should be judged over a cycle of a couple of years.

segments.name: Subsidiaries
segments.commentary: Consolidated profit fell versus standalone. AICL profit fell about 60%, South Africa posted a loss of INR287 crores and Moscow a loss of about INR29 crores in Q1.

guidance_outlook: Targets roughly 10% growth overall, with foreign growth expected to exceed domestic; mid-year review to revisit the target.
Combined ratio targets split by book: domestic about 103% (close to current levels) and foreign about 95%, expected in 2 to 3 years.
Maintain domestic market share despite competition; rebuild foreign business lost after the rating downgrade, while continuing pruning.
Long-term goal of 50:50 domestic-to-international mix; medium-term target 60:40. Management said it will not pursue these at the cost of risk-return.
A-rating upgrade (from A-) possible in about 4 to 5 years, subject to IFRS and RBC implementation and business position.
Management expects solvency to decline gradually as profitability improves and growth remains measured.
capex_capacity: No capacity or capex plans discussed on the call; the call covered reinsurance underwriting and investment book only.

Investment book: about INR120,000 crores at book value and INR157,000-157,800 crores at market value (equity about INR58,000 crores), as stated on the call. Management said the debt share is stable and equity will stay around 17%.
Major domestic reinsurance renewals occur on 1 April; management used reinsurance tools to support domestic insurers.
demand_pricing: Global reinsurance capacity is ample and pricing is soft; competitive behaviour is seen across most players, including Indian reinsurers, foreign branches and GIFT City entrants, especially in property cat.
Management said cat losses typically come to GIC at about 30-40% of market losses; flood claims for Gujarat are still developing.
IRDAI issued directives on 22 July 2026 on property rates quoted on the direct side, which management described as guidance whose impact will be seen over the next 2-3 quarters.
Health: growth driven by retail health rather than corporate or group health, which management views as more loss-prone. Obligatory share of domestic book was about 33% in Q1.
Foreign premium remains well below the roughly INR18,000 crores once reached; management expects recovery to take 3-4 years given softer rates.

qa_highlights.question: Which market players have been aggressive in pricing, and will the softness deepen given benign cat experience and Gujarat flood losses?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said almost all players have been competitive given surplus global capacity. GIC's cat losses usually run at 30-40% of market losses, and flood claims are still developing, so the company is watching claims development before concluding.

qa_highlights.question: What changed in the overseas book to produce the strong Q1 overseas combined ratio, and is it structural?
qa_highlights.answer: Sanjay Mokashi said the foreign book is being reviewed class by class, with action on motor, aviation and cargo, and property the largest exposure. One quarter may not be representative, there is seasonality, and some first-quarter accounting entries may affect the result. No number was given.

qa_highlights.question: Why did domestic combined ratio deteriorate to about 107.5%, and what is the full-year view?
qa_highlights.answer: Domestic motor deteriorated because of legacy treaties; competition is intense in property. Health growth is in retail rather than group. Management did not give a full-year domestic combined ratio and pointed to the 1 April renewals and reinsurance tools.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Gujarat flood provision in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: The company has provided INR440 crores in Q1 for the Gujarat flood event; the figure was restated several times on the call during the answer.

qa_highlights.question: Is the net worth excluding fair value falling from about INR51,000 crores to INR45,000 crores, and why is net worth including fair value flat?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it would recheck the excluding-fair-value figure. For net worth including fair value, the flat trend is attributed to falls in equity market value, which offset profits; the CIO put the fair value reduction at about INR11,000-15,000 crores. Details were deferred to a later call.

qa_highlights.question: What is the timeline to reach a 103% domestic and 95% foreign combined ratio, and how does it relate to capital?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said domestic is fairly close to 103%, while the 95% foreign target is 2-3 years away. Solvency at 4.3 is seen as conservative during the post-downgrade recovery and the IFRS/RBC transition, and is expected to decline gradually.

Gujarat flood claims development beyond the INR440 crores provision.

Domestic motor and retail health loss ratios; domestic combined ratio about 107.5% in Q1.
Life reinsurance profitability, which management said is still under review over a cycle.
Subsidiary losses (South Africa INR287 crores, Moscow INR29 crores) and the AICL profit decline of about 60%.
Net worth including fair value flat over several years; the Q1 net worth decline is under reconciliation by management.
IFRS and RBC implementation, and the IRDAI property-rate directive.

We do not want to grow at the cost of profitability.

540762|2026-09.headline: TI standalone Q2 FY27 revenue rose to Rs.2,710 Cr (from Rs.2,119 Cr) but PBT was flat at Rs.253 Cr as raw-material pass-through lagged.
540762|2026-09.overview: Standalone revenue grew about 28% YoY to Rs.2,710 Cr, with management attributing roughly 15% to volume and the rest to raw-material price pass-through. Standalone PBT was nearly flat at Rs.253 Cr versus Rs.250 Cr, and EBITDA was flat per an analyst, as commodity and cell-cost increases reached margins before customer price recovery. Consolidated revenue rose to Rs.7,330 Cr from Rs.5,523 Cr, driven by CG Power, while TICMPL (EV) revenue reached Rs.476 Cr and remained loss-making. Management expects price recovery to settle over one to two quarters and reiterated TICMPL EBITDA breakeven targets for truck in Q4 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Will standalone EBITDA catch up in H2 FY27 given flat EBITDA on 15-16% volume growth?

540767|2026-03.headline: NAM India posted record FY26 PAT of INR 15.29 bn (+19% YoY) and record quarterly operating profit of INR 4.93 bn (+39% YoY) in Q4 FY26.

540767|2026-09.headline: NAM India's Q2 FY27 operating profit hit a record INR 5.23 bn (+25% YoY), but PAT fell to INR 3.24 bn after a INR 96.76 crore SEBI settlement charge.
540767|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue rose 21% YoY to INR 7.96 bn and operating profit rose 25% YoY to a record INR 5.23 bn, with operating expenses up 14% YoY. PAT declined both YoY and QoQ to INR 3.24 bn because of a one-time exceptional item: the INR 96.76 crore settlement with SEBI over the Yes Bank AT-1 bond investments by certain NIMF schemes. Mutual fund market share was 9.02%, flat QoQ, and equity yield compressed to 52 bps (ex-arbitrage) from about 54 bps in Q1, which management attributed to telescopic pricing and equity inflows. The Board declared an interim dividend of INR 9.50 per share.

qa_highlights.question: What was the AT-1 bond case about and what triggered the provision this quarter?

qa_highlights.question: How are flows in small-cap and flexi-cap holding up amid corrections, and what is the distributor communication?

540768|2026-03.headline: Mahindra Logistics returned to profit in Q4 FY26, with reported PAT of INR20.2 crores versus a INR6.7 crores loss a year earlier.
540768|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 14% YoY to INR1,791 crores and gross margin expanded to 10.5% from 9.5%. Adjusted EBITDA (after deducting long-term lease rent) rose to INR57 crores, a 3.2% margin versus 2.4% a year earlier. Full-year reported PAT was INR2.3 crores against a INR35.8 crores loss in FY25, after a Q3 exceptional gratuity charge under the new Labour Codes. Express (MESPL) remained EBITDA-negative for FY26 but gross-margin positive for the full year and close to EBITDA breakeven per management. Freight forwarding faces West Asia-related headwinds going into FY27.

segments.name: Express (MESPL)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue grew 49% YoY; FY26 revenue INR449 crores (+25%), gross margin 1.3% for the full year. Quarterly GM rose from INR20 lakh in Q2 to INR2.7 crores in Q3 and INR6.6 crores in Q4. FY26 EBITDA loss INR31 crores vs INR51 crores loss in FY25.

segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR89 crores (+17% YoY); gross margin +50% YoY. FY26 revenue grew 14%, EBITDA INR10.1 crores vs INR6.8 crores in FY25. Q4 growth is now facing West Asia-related headwinds.

segments.name: Mobility
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR386 crores (+22% vs INR316 crores). Q4 revenue grew 42% YoY and gross margin 17% YoY; growth driven by large B2B accounts, with utilisation improvement a focus on the asset-heavy Alyte Prive premium offering in Delhi.

qa_highlights.question: What is Express volume growth, and can it sustain mid-teens revenue growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Express volume growth is mid-to-high teens YoY, and that a mid-teens revenue growth target is achievable. Volume is no longer disclosed alone as it is not a sufficient metric without yield.

qa_highlights.question: Is adjusted EBITDA margin likely to surpass the pre-Ind AS FY18-19 levels of about 3.6-3.9%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it agreed directionally but gave no forward guidance and said the turnaround has only just started.

qa_highlights.question: When will Express reach EBITDA breakeven?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said EBITDA breakeven is the immediate goal and it is 'very close', but gave no timeline.

qa_highlights.question: Are there further last-mile pruning or declines to expect?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said all last-mile pruning was done in FY26 and the business is now expected to grow with profitable clients.

qa_highlights.question: Are there similar receivable provisions expected? What drove the INR28 crore credit provision?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said the provision reflects prudence on aged receivables under management judgment. She said nothing similar warrants provisioning at present.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said only Freight Forwarding is affected so far; other segments are on plan. A 10-15% diesel rise would be passed through immediately, but management flagged broader economic inflation risk.

540777|2026-09.headline: HDFC Life H1 FY27 VNB rose 12% to ₹2,037 crore at a 24.7% margin, while solvency fell to 180% on capital consumption.

VNB reached ₹2,037 crore (up 12%, Q2 up 15%) and margin expanded to 24.7% from 24.5%. Persistency softened on unit-linked renewals and a non-par cohort, and the EV walk showed negative operating and investment variances from equity underperformance, yield rises and wider credit spreads. Solvency fell to 180%, prompting a ₹500 crore subordinated debt raise. Management spent much of the call on the IRDAI distribution-economics consultation paper, where it was non-committal on specifics.
